candidates.title: Plastic Parts and Products Surface Coating NESHAP (surface coating of plastic parts and products)

criteria.criterion: If the methylene chloride step is an application of a material for the purpose of bonding plastic surfaces (i.e., an 'adhesive' or 'coating' applied to a substrate), then that operation is a 'surface coating' covered by this subpart.

If the coating/adhesive materials used in that operation contain organic HAP and you use 378 liters (100 gallons) or more per year at a source that is a major source (or located at a major source), then the affected source is subject to this subpart.

If the coating operation uses only coatings, thinners, other additives, and cleaning materials that contain no organic HAP (as determined per the subpart), then the operation is not subject to this subpart.

If the activity falls within any of the enumerated exclusions in § 63.4481(c)(2)–(17) (for example certain research/laboratory activities, processes covered by other NESHAP subparts, web or in-mold coating exclusions, etc.), then the operation is not subject to this subpart.

If the material applied is an adhesive that is a 'product used on humans or animals' or is adhesive tape/contact paper or an adhesive pre‑incorporated on a substrate, then it is not treated as an 'adhesive' under this subpart and may not be covered as a coating/adhesive here.

candidates.title: General Provisions (definitions, performance testing, monitoring)

criteria.criterion: If your source is subject to a relevant standard under part 63 (for example Subpart PPPP), then Subpart A's General Provisions apply as part of that relevant standard.

If the relevant standard requires performance testing, then the owner/operator must perform required performance tests within 180 days of the compliance date (unless a waiver or other provision applies).

If the relevant standard requires installation or use of a continuous monitoring system (CMS) or other monitoring, then monitoring must be conducted, operated, and quality‑assured in accordance with § 63.8.

checklist: Determine whether the methylene chloride application is performed for the purpose of bonding (i.e., is the material applied to bond surfaces) versus being only a cleaner or surface prep; document how and why the solvent is applied.

Quantify the annual volume of methylene chloride (and any other coatings/thinners/additives/cleaning materials used in the bonding step) in liters or gallons per year (include the six new lines projected use).

Obtain manufacturer/supplier formulation data or test data for the methylene chloride and any mixtures to determine organic HAP content and mass fraction of coating solids (use Method 311 or Method 24 paths per subpart guidance if needed).

Determine whether methylene chloride (and any other solvents used) is an organic HAP and calculate potential annual HAP emissions to evaluate whether the facility is a 'major source' (≥10 tpy single HAP or ≥25 tpy combined HAP).

Verify whether the applied material leaves any coating solids or dry film on the part (document that no dry film remains and whether any volatile fraction reacts or becomes solids — relevant to reactive adhesive provisions).

Check whether the adhesive/product can be considered a 'product used on humans or animals' or otherwise fits any of the specific exclusions in § 63.4481(c); document why each exclusion does or does not apply.

If subject to the subpart, decide which compliance option you will use (compliant materials, emission rate without add‑on controls, or emission rate with add‑on controls) and collect the data required for that option (materials tracking, solids used, capture/control efficiencies if applicable).

Establish whether performance testing and/or CMS will be required, note the applicable compliance date, and prepare to meet Subpart A requirements for test notifications, site‑specific test plans, and monitoring quality assurance (timing per § 63.7 and § 63.8).

judge_text: {"score":1,"reason":"Part of EPA’s reasoning is captured: OUR ANSWER cites §63.4581 and treats methylene chloride used to bond as an ‘adhesive’/coating. However the EPA’s key point that the PPPP emission limit (lb HAP per lb solids, §63.4490) cannot be determined when no coating solids are left — and thus the rule is not applied — is not explicitly stated as a criterion in OUR ANSWER (the checklist asks to verify absence of solids but does not state the regulatory consequence that lack of solids makes the §63.4490 metric inapplicable)." }

candidates.title: Secondary Copper Smelters

criteria.criterion: If a facility processes copper scrap in a blast furnace and converter or uses another pyrometallurgical purification process to produce anode copper from copper scrap, then it is a secondary copper smelter and subject to this subpart.

If a facility merely melts recycled copper scrap or copper-alloy scrap to produce ingots or for direct use in a manufacturing process (and does not use a pyrometallurgical purification process to produce anode copper), then it is not a secondary copper smelter and is not subject to this subpart.

If the facility is a secondary copper smelter that is a new affected source (construction or reconstruction commenced on or after October 6, 2006) and is an area source of HAP, then this subpart applies to that new affected source.

candidates.title: Aluminum, Copper, and Other Nonferrous Foundries

criteria.criterion: If you operate a copper foundry that melts copper and pours molten copper into molds to manufacture complex castings and the affected source's annual metal melt production (existing) or annual metal melt capacity (new) for copper and other nonferrous metals is at least 600 tons per year, then this subpart applies.

If you are a primary or secondary metal producer that casts molten copper to produce simple shapes such as sows, ingots, bars, rods, billets, or anode copper, then you are not a copper foundry and this subpart does not apply.

candidates.title: Secondary Nonferrous Metals Processing

criteria.criterion: If you own or operate a secondary nonferrous metals processing facility that is an area source of hazardous air pollutant emissions, then this subpart applies.

candidates.title: General Provisions

criteria.criterion: If a relevant standard requires performance testing, then the owner or operator must perform the performance test within 180 days of the compliance date (unless another provision applies or a waiver/extension is obtained).

If a relevant standard requires continuous monitoring systems (CMS) or other monitoring, then monitoring must be conducted as set forth in § 63.8 and the CMS must be installed, operated, and maintained according to that section and any applicable relevant standard.

checklist: Does the facility process copper scrap using a pyrometallurgical purification process (e.g., blast furnace/converter or other smelting process) specifically to produce anode copper from copper scrap?
Is the final product anode copper (cast anodes shipped for electrolytic refining) or simple ingots/sows/other shapes for direct use?
Does the operation use a smelting or melting furnace with fluxes producing molten material and slag (i.e., meet the subpart FFFFFF definition of smelting/melting furnace)?
Was construction or reconstruction of the affected source commenced on or after October 6, 2006 (to determine new-source status under Subpart FFFFFF)?
Is the facility an area source or a major source of HAP (i.e., potential to emit <10 tpy of any single HAP and <25 tpy combined HAP for area source determination)?
For foundry applicability: what is the facility's annual metal melt production (existing) or annual metal melt capacity (new) for copper and other nonferrous metals (is it ≥600 tpy)?
Does the facility melt and pour molten metal into molds to make complex castings (characteristic of a 'foundry') or cast simple shapes (excluded from 'copper foundry')?

Does the facility meet any applicable local/state definitions or listings for 'secondary nonferrous metals processing' (check applicable definitions/permits or 40 CFR references available to the permitting authority)?

judge_text: {"score":2,"reason":"EPA's notes hinge on two points—(1) the anode furnace is a pyrometallurgical purification process producing anode copper from scrap, meeting 40 CFR 63.11158, and (2) the facility is a new area source covered by 40 CFR 63.11153(a)-(b). Both points are explicitly included in the FFFFFF criteria in OUR ANSWER."}

candidates.title: National Emission Standards for Perchloroethylene Dry Cleaning Facilities

criteria.criterion: if the dry cleaning facility uses perchloroethylene (PCE) then the provisions of this subpart apply to the owner or operator of the facility
if a dry cleaning system is located in a building with a residence on or after December 21, 2020 then the owner or operator shall eliminate any emission of PCE from that dry cleaning system

if the total yearly PCE consumption is less than 530 liters (140 gallons) per year for facilities meeting the conditions of §63.320(d) then the facility is exempt from many provisions of §§63.322, 63.323, and 63.324 but remains subject to §63.322(o)(5)(i)

if the total yearly PCE consumption is less than 760 liters (200 gallons) per year for facilities described in §63.320(e) then the facility is exempt from many provisions of §§63.322, 63.323, and 63.324 but remains subject to §63.322(o)(5)(i)
if the dry cleaning machine is coin-operated then it is exempt from the requirements of this subpart

if the dry cleaning facility emits or has the potential to emit more than 9.1 megagrams per year (10 tons per year) of PCE then the facility is a major source (different major-source provisions in this subpart may apply)

if the building contains a dwelling that meets the definition of 'residence' (excluding short-term housing occupied by the same person for less than 180 days) then that dwelling counts as a 'residence' for purposes of the Subpart M residence-related requirements

if construction or reconstruction of a dry cleaning system commenced on or after specified dates (e.g., December 9, 1991; December 21, 2005; July 27, 2006) then the compliance date and specific requirements applicable to that system follow the timelines in §63.320(b)

if a facility is located in a building with a residence, even if the residence is vacant at the time of notification, then the owner or operator had to report that fact under the notification provisions in §63.324(f)

candidates.title: General Provisions (applicability, compliance dates, operation and maintenance)

criteria.criterion: if you are an owner or operator of an affected source subject to a relevant standard under this part then you must operate and maintain the affected source and associated control and monitoring equipment in a manner consistent with safety and good air pollution control practices at all times
if an area source later increases its emissions or potential to emit such that it becomes a major source then the source becomes subject to the relevant emission standards as provided in this part

if you are subject to a relevant standard under this part then you must develop a written startup, shutdown, and malfunction (SSM) plan describing procedures for operation and corrective action as required by §63.6(e)(3)

if a relevant standard requires performance testing or monitoring then the timing, conduct, and reporting of tests and monitoring are governed by the performance testing and monitoring requirements in §§63.7 and 63.8

candidates.title: Industrial, Commercial, and Institutional Boilers: General provisions excerpt (references to applicability of General Provisions)

criteria.criterion: if your source were subject to Subpart EEEE then Table 12 to that subpart determines which parts of the General Provisions (§§63.1–63.15) apply

if equipment identified in §63.2338(b)(1)–(5) is in OLD operation then at those times you must be in compliance with the emission limitations, operating limits, and work practice standards in Subpart EEEE and operate consistent with §63.6(e)(1)(i)

checklist: Confirm whether your facility uses perchloroethylene (PCE) at all (any purchases) and collect purchase receipts for the last 12 months to calculate yearly PCE consumption per §63.323(d).
Determine the physical location of the dry cleaning machine(s): is any machine located in the same building that contains an apartment or other dwelling unit (identify address and unit)?
If there is an apartment/dwelling, determine whether it meets the Subpart M definition of 'residence' (not short-term housing occupied by the same person for less than 180 days).
Determine whether the apartment/dwelling is currently occupied or vacant (note: vacancy does not negate reporting or the residence-based requirement per §63.324(f)(3)).
Identify the type of machine(s): dry-to-dry or transfer machine system, and whether any machine is coin-operated.
Determine the date construction or reconstruction of each dry cleaning system commenced (to check which compliance dates apply under §63.320(b)).

Calculate total yearly PCE consumption (sum of purchases for previous 12 months per §63.323(d)) to check exemptions/major-source thresholds (530 L/140 gal, 760 L/200 gal, 6,800 L/1,800 gal, 8,000 L/2,100 gal) and whether the facility is a major or area source under §63.320(g)/(h).

If claiming exemption based on low consumption, verify which specific provisions you remain subject to (note that §63.322(o)(5)(i) remains applicable even for some exempted low-consumption configurations).

Check whether any required notifications or notifications of compliance status have been submitted (including the §63.324 notifications and the July 28, 2008 certification items in §63.324(f)), and whether any extension requests under §63.6(i) have been sought or granted.

If controls are installed (refrigerated condenser, carbon adsorber, vapor/vapor-barrier enclosure), gather equipment manuals, monitoring records, and operation procedures to confirm compliance with §63.322 and applicable monitoring/reporting (see §63.322, §63.323, §63.324).

judge_text: {"score":1,"reason":"The EPA Notes’ key point that a co-located residence (occupied or vacant) makes the facility co-residential is captured (see citations to 40 CFR 63.321 and §63.324(f)(3) and checklist note). However, the EPA’s second key point — that the December 21, 2020 requirement applies so long as the PCE machine remains in the building regardless of whether it is currently operating — is not explicitly captured (the answer ties applicability to PCE ‘use’/purchases and low‑consumption exemptions but does not state that mere presence of a PCE machine in the building triggers §63.322(o)(5)(i))."}

candidates.title: Area Source Standards for Metal Fabrication and Finishing

criteria.criterion: If you own or operate an area source that is primarily engaged (>=50% production as defined in §63.11522) in one of the nine metal fabrication and finishing source categories (e.g., Electrical and Electronic Equipment Finishing Operations) then you are subject to this subpart.

If you use materials that contain, or have the potential to emit, metal fabrication and finishing HAP (MFHAP — compounds of cadmium, chromium, lead, manganese, or nickel at the specified thresholds) and you perform machining, dry grinding/dry polishing with machines, dry abrasive blasting, spray painting, or welding operations then the affected source provisions of this subpart apply.

If your operations are research or laboratory facilities, or are tool or equipment repair operations, facility maintenance, or quality control activities, or are on-site operations at certain Federal agencies, or produce military munitions, then this subpart does not apply to those operations.

candidates.title: Area Source Standards for Plating and Polishing

criteria.criterion: If you own or operate a plating and polishing facility that is an area source and that is engaged in one or more listed processes (non-chromium electroplating, electroless or non-electrolytic plating, other non-electrolytic metal coating processes including thermal spraying, dry mechanical polishing after plating, electroforming, or electropolishing) and the facility uses or has emissions of plating and polishing metal HAP, then you are subject to this subpart.

If individual process units are subject to 40 CFR part 63 subpart N (chromium electroplating), are research and development or educational process units, are used strictly for repair/maintenance or restoration, or the process uses materials with plating metal HAP below the thresholds specified, then those process units are not subject to this subpart.

If you operate tanks that contain plating/polishing metal HAP used for non-chromium electroplating/electroforming/electropolishing/electroless plating/other non-electrolytic metal coating, or thermal spraying operations that apply plating/polishing metal HAP, or dry mechanical polishing operations that emit plating/polishing metal HAP, then those units are covered as affected sources under this subpart.

candidates.title: General Provisions (Part 63)

criteria.criterion: If an affected source is subject to a relevant standard then the performance testing requirements of §63.7 apply as specified in that section.
If an affected source is required to use a continuous monitoring system or other monitoring under a relevant standard then the monitoring requirements of §63.8 apply.
If your stationary source is not a major source (i.e., emits less than the major source thresholds) then it is an area source for purposes of these Part 63 area-source subparts.

checklist: Confirm whether the facility is an area source (potential to emit < 10 tpy single HAP and < 25 tpy total HAP) or a major source (use PTE calculation).

Determine whether the facility is 'primarily engaged' (≥50% of production by volume/appropriate metric over the previous continuous 12 months) in one of the nine metal fabrication/finishing categories (including Electrical and Electronic Equipment Finishing Operations).

List all metal fabrication and finishing activities performed on-site in the last 12 months (machining, dry grinding/polishing with machines, dry abrasive blasting, spray painting, welding, thermal spraying, plating, electroless plating, electropolishing, dry mechanical polishing, electroforming).

For each material, check supplier formulation data/MSDS to determine if it contains MFHAP/plating-and-polishing metals at or above thresholds (cadmium, chromium, lead, or nickel ≥ 0.1% by weight; manganese ≥ 1.0% by weight).
If performing welding, record welding rod usage on a rolling 12-month basis to see if it is ≥ 2,000 lb/yr (triggers additional welding requirements).
If plating tanks are used, identify tank types (non-chromium vs chromium) and bath pH and chemicals to determine coverage or applicability of Subpart WWWWWW vs subpart N (chromium electroplating).
Document whether any operations are research/laboratory, educational, facility maintenance, tool/equipment repair, quality control sampling, or military munitions production (possible exemptions).
Inventory spray painting methods and equipment (HVLP, electrostatic, spray booths/waterwash, filter efficiencies) and worker training records if spray-applied paints containing MFHAP are used.
Identify any dry abrasive blasting enclosures (totally enclosed/unvented vs vented) and whether capture and filtration controls are present and their manufacturer specifications.

Assemble production fractions, process lists, material MSDS, emissions estimates, and records so you can prepare initial notification/notification of compliance status and the required records if the subpart(s) apply.

judge_text: {"score":1,"reason":"OUR ANSWER includes the primary-engaged applicability criterion (citing §63.11514(a)/§63.11522) that EPA relied on, but it fails to capture the EPA Q&A mapping rationale (NAICS 335999 paired with SIC 3699, not the facility’s SIC 3679) cited in the EPA NOTES—so a key reason is missing."}

candidates.title: NESHAP for lime manufacturing plants (LMP)

criteria.criterion: If you own or operate a lime manufacturing plant (LMP) that is a major source, or that is located at, or is part of, a major source of hazardous air pollutant (HAP) emissions, then you are subject to this subpart.

If an establishment manufactures lime product (calcium oxide, calcium oxide with magnesium oxide, or dead burned dolomite) by calcination of limestone, dolomite, shells, or other calcareous substances, then it is an LMP for purposes of this subpart.

If you have a lime kiln at an LMP that is a major source, then this subpart applies to each existing or new lime kiln and their associated cooler(s) and processed stone handling operations located at that LMP.

If the LMP is located at a kraft pulp mill, soda pulp mill, sulfite pulp mill, beet sugar manufacturing plant, or only processes sludge containing calcium carbonate from water softening processes, then the LMP is not subject to this subpart.
If the emission unit is a lime hydrator, then it is not subject to this subpart.
If the material in question is an open material storage pile, then those open material storage piles are not subject to this subpart.

If you wish to claim area source status, then you must measure the emissions of hydrogen chloride from all lime kilns (subject to the exceptions left to the permitting authority) using EPA Method 320 or 321 or the specified ASTM alternative as set out in §63.7142.

candidates.title: General Provisions (NESHAP General Provisions)

criteria.criterion: If your affected source is required to do performance testing by a relevant standard, then you must perform the required performance tests within 180 days of the compliance date for that source unless a waiver or other exception applies.

If continuous monitoring systems (CMS) are required by a relevant standard, then the monitoring requirements in §63.8 apply to those CMS (including installation, operation, QA and reporting requirements) upon promulgation of CMS performance specifications as specified in the relevant standard.

If a collection of equipment, activities, or both within a single contiguous area and under common control is included in a section 112(c) source category or subcategory, then that collection is an 'affected source' as defined in §63.2 (and is subject to the relevant section 112(d) standard unless otherwise specified).

If the plant emits or has the potential to emit any single HAP at a rate of 9.07 megagrams (10 tons) or more per year or any combination of HAP at a rate of 22.68 megagrams (25 tons) or more per year, then it meets the 'major source' definition in §63.2 and the major-source thresholds referenced in §63.7081 apply.

If a CMS is required, then you must operate and maintain each CMS consistent with good air pollution control practices and the CMS provisions in §63.8 (including QA/QC, performance evaluations, and recordkeeping/reporting requirements).

checklist: Confirm whether the kiln is used to produce a 'lime product' (e.g., calcium oxide/quicklime or dead burned dolomite) by calcination versus only reprocessing non-calcareous wastes; list feedstock(s) (e.g., limestone, dolomite, shells, calcium carbonate lime mud).

Determine whether the kiln's calcination of calcium carbonate lime mud (from caustic recovery) results in a lime product (quicklime) as defined by the rule (i.e., is the output chemically and functionally a lime product).
Quantify actual and potential annual HAP emissions (by pollutant and combined) from the entire plant to determine major-source status (>=10 tpy single HAP or >=25 tpy combined HAP).

Verify whether the LMP is located at or part of any of the excluded facility types (kraft pulp mill, soda pulp mill, sulfite pulp mill, beet sugar manufacturing plant) or only processes calcium carbonate sludge from water softening.

Identify whether the emission unit is classified as a lime hydrator, an open material storage pile, or processed stone handling; if so, note that hydrators and open piles are excluded from this subpart.
Establish the construction or reconstruction date(s) for the kiln (and associated cooler) to determine new vs existing affected source status per the dates referenced in §63.7082(b)–(c) and §63.7083.

Determine whether the kiln is part of the LMP's 'processed stone handling' system or is solely used to calcine recycled lime mud (and whether the permitting authority treats that feedstock as 'processed stone' or 'other calcareous substance').
Inventory control devices and vent configurations (e.g., baghouse/FF, monovent, positive-pressure FF) and note stack/venting details relevant to compliance testing and monitoring requirements.

If claiming area source status (or evaluating that possibility), plan HCl testing for all applicable kilns using EPA Method 320 or 321 or the ASTM alternative per §63.7142 and confirm whether the permitting authority will allow testing of one representative kiln.
Gather records and dates to support whether any unit has been idled or is essentially identical to other kilns (permitting authority discretion affects testing requirements under §63.7142(c)).

Determine applicable monitoring and performance testing obligations (need for COMS, PM detectors, CEMS, performance test scheduling) and readiness to meet §63.7 and §63.8 requirements if Subpart AAAAA applies.

judge_text: {"score":1, "reason":"The answer includes the key elements that calcining calcareous lime mud meets the Subpart AAAAA definition (citations to §63.7143/§63.7081) and addresses major‑source status and the listed exemptions. However it does not explicitly state the EPA’s point that the pulp/beet‑sugar/water‑softening exemptions do not extend to soda‑ash chemical recovery, nor does it explicitly note the rule does not require the lime to be sold — so not all key reasons from the EPA notes are captured."}

candidates.title: National Emission Standards for Hazardous Air Pollutants for Stationary Reciprocating Internal Combustion Engines (Subpart ZZZZ)

criteria.criterion: If you own or operate an existing spark-ignition 4SLB or 4SRB stationary RICE with a site rating of more than 500 HP located at an area source of HAP that met the definition of remote stationary RICE on the engine's initial compliance date (October 19, 2013), then the engine is considered a remote stationary RICE under this subpart and may be subject to the remote-engine provisions.

If an existing spark-ignition 4SLB or 4SRB stationary RICE with a site rating of more than 500 HP located at an area source does not meet the definition of remote stationary RICE and is operated more than 24 hours per calendar year, then the initial compliance demonstration for that engine must be conducted as specified for non-remote engines (including performance testing requirements referenced in this subpart).

If a stationary RICE meets the geographic/occupancy criteria listed for a remote stationary RICE (for units not on pipelines: 5 or fewer buildings intended for human occupancy and no buildings with four or more stories within a 0.25 mile radius), then it meets the definition of remote stationary RICE in this subpart.

If you own or operate an existing spark-ignition 4SLB or 4SRB stationary RICE with a site rating of more than 500 HP that was considered remote as of October 19, 2013, then you must evaluate the remote status every 12 months, keep records of the initial and annual evaluations, and, if an evaluation shows the engine no longer meets the remote definition, comply with the non-remote requirements within 1 year of that evaluation.

If you own or operate an existing stationary RICE located at an area source of HAP emissions, then you are required to conduct any initial performance test or other initial compliance demonstration that applies to you according to Tables 4 and 5 to this subpart within 180 days after the applicable compliance date unless an applicable exception (e.g., remote treatment per this subpart) applies.

If you own or operate an existing stationary RICE located at an area source of HAP emissions, then you must submit the notifications and reports specified for such engines (including Notification of Compliance Status after completion of the initial compliance demonstration) as required by this subpart.

candidates.title: General Provisions (Subpart A)

criteria.criterion: If a relevant standard requires you to perform a performance test, then you must perform the performance test within 180 days of the compliance date unless a waiver or extension is approved by the Administrator.

If you are required to conduct a performance test for an affected source, then you must notify the Administrator in writing of your intention to conduct the performance test at least 60 calendar days before the performance test is initially scheduled to begin.

If an affected source becomes subject to a relevant standard, then the owner or operator must submit the initial notification required by §63.9(b) (including identification of whether the source is a major source or an area source) within 120 calendar days after the effective date of the relevant standard or after becoming subject to the standard.

If you are required to submit a Notification of Compliance Status following completion of a compliance demonstration (including a performance test), then you must submit that notification before the close of business on the 60th day following completion of the relevant compliance demonstration activity (or other time specified in the relevant standard).

checklist: Confirm each engine type (spark-ignition four-stroke lean-burn vs rich-burn) and manufacturer's site-rated brake horsepower for each engine.
Confirm whether each engine is an existing engine and the date construction/commencement occurred to verify 'existing' status under §63.6590.
Confirm that the facility is an area source (not a major source) of HAP emissions.

Determine whether each engine met the remote stationary RICE definition on the initial compliance date (October 19, 2013) by evaluating: (a) whether the unit is on a pipeline segment or not, (b) for non-pipeline units, count buildings intended for human occupancy within a 0.25 mile radius and check for any buildings with four or more stories within that radius, and for pipeline segments apply the pipeline-specific distance/building criteria per §63.6675.

Document the date when the engines first met the geographic/occupancy criteria for remote status (compare to Oct 19, 2013) and assemble any existing initial and annual remote-status evaluations and records.
Verify annual operating hours for each engine (is operation >24 hours per calendar year?).
Check whether the engines have ever been designated emergency or limited-use engines (to confirm applicability of non-emergency provisions).

Determine whether initial performance testing or other initial compliance demonstrations were performed and, if so, collect test dates and reports; if not performed, determine whether any waiver or extension was requested/approved under §63.7.

Check whether initial notifications and the Notification of Compliance Status required by §63.6645/§63.9 were submitted (to State permitting authority or EPA Regional Office depending on delegation) and the dates of submittal.

If claiming remote treatment without prior notification to the State, verify the State/EPA delegated authority and whether any additional notification or recordkeeping is required by the delegated authority for remote engines under this subpart.

If the engine was considered remote on Oct 19, 2013, verify that annual evaluations of remote status are being performed every 12 months and retained as required; if an evaluation shows loss of remote status, verify plan to comply with non-remote requirements within 1 year.

judge_text: {"score":2,"reason":"The answer cites 40 CFR 63.6603(f) that existing >500 hp 4SLB/4SRB area-source engines that met the remote definition on Oct 19, 2013 are treated as remote and may use the remote-engine provisions, it includes the 12‑month reevaluation and recordkeeping requirement from §63.6603(f), and it notes checking state/EPA delegation — which collectively capture the EPA Notes (no separate remote-status notification needed for such existing engines and the delegated state (Utah DAQ) governs). It does not verbatim state “no notification required,” but it addresses delegation/notification and the statutory basis for remote status, so the key EPA reasons are present."}

candidates.title: Gasoline Dispensing Facilities (GDF)

criteria.criterion: if a gasoline dispensing facility (GDF) is located at an area source then the affected source includes each gasoline storage tank and is subject to this subpart

if a stationary facility dispenses gasoline into the fuel tank of a motor vehicle, motor vehicle engine, nonroad vehicle, or nonroad engine then that facility meets the definition of a gasoline dispensing facility (GDF)

if the monthly throughput of gasoline at the GDF is less than 10,000 gallons then the facility must comply with the management practices in § 63.11116 (and not the control requirements in § 63.11117/§ 63.11118)
if the monthly throughput of gasoline at the GDF is 10,000 gallons or more then the facility must comply with the requirements in § 63.11117
if the monthly throughput of gasoline at the GDF is 100,000 gallons or more then the facility must comply with the additional requirements in § 63.11118

if an emission source is merely the equipment used for the refueling of motor vehicles (e.g., dispensers/pumps) then that equipment is not covered by this subpart (whereas gasoline storage tanks at a GDF are covered)

if the liquid in the tank is not 'gasoline' as defined (i.e., a petroleum distillate or distillate/alcohol blend with Reid vapor pressure ≥27.6 kPa) then that tank is not a gasoline storage tank for purposes of this subpart
if a gasoline storage tank has capacity less than 250 gallons then it is not required to meet the submerged fill requirements of § 63.11117(b) and is subject only to the requirements in § 63.11116

candidates.title: Area Source Standards for Bulk Gasoline Facilities

criteria.criterion: if you own or operate a bulk gasoline terminal, pipeline breakout station, pipeline pumping station, or bulk gasoline plant identified in § 63.11081(a)(1)–(4) then you are subject to this subpart

if gasoline storage tanks located at sources identified in § 63.11081(a)(1)–(4) are used only for dispensing gasoline in a manner consistent with tanks at a GDF then those tanks are not subject to this subpart and must comply with subpart CCCCCC instead

candidates.title: General Provisions

criteria.criterion: if a stationary source is not a major source (i.e., does not meet the major source thresholds) then it is an 'area source' as defined in § 63.2
if a relevant standard requires performance testing then the owner or operator must perform such tests within 180 days of the compliance date (unless a waiver/extension applies)
if a relevant standard requires a continuous monitoring system (CMS) then the CMS is subject to the provisions of § 63.8 upon promulgation of applicable performance specifications

checklist: Confirm whether each 500-gallon tank contains gasoline (meets 'gasoline' definition: RVP ≥ 27.6 kPa) or diesel (diesel is not gasoline for this subpart)
Confirm how gasoline is dispensed from each tank (directly into motor vehicle fuel tanks on-site, into portable containers for later on-site dispensing, or into cargo tanks)
Determine whether the tanks and dispensing are located at a single stationary facility that dispenses gasoline to motor vehicles or equipment (i.e., does the facility function as a GDF?)

Calculate monthly throughput per GDF as defined (sum current day + previous 364 days divided by 12) to determine whether throughput is <10,000, ≥10,000, or ≥100,000 gallons (per § 63.11111(h) / § 63.11132)
Verify individual tank capacities (500 gallons each) and check the <250-gallon and <2,000-gallon exceptions referenced in § 63.11117(c)
Determine whether tanks are loaded/unloaded by gasoline cargo tanks (cargo-tank unloading may implicate additional GDF requirements)

Confirm whether the storage tanks are part of a bulk gasoline terminal/plant/pipeline station (which would trigger subpart BBBBBB) or are solely operated consistent with a GDF (which would direct applicability to subpart CCCCCC)
Check whether any State/local/permit limits or title V obligations apply (federally enforceable permit conditions may affect applicability or compliance obligations)

candidates.title: National Emission Standards for Hazardous Air Pollutants for Portland Cement Manufacturing

criteria.criterion: If the coal mill uses kiln exhaust gases in its process (i.e., is an in-line coal mill), then the coal mill is an affected source under this subpart.

If an in-line coal mill associated with a kiln exhausts through a separate stack, then the combined PM emissions from the kiln and the inline coal mill (and any alkali bypass) are subject to the PM emission limit and must be accounted for in the kiln PM compliance determination.

If kiln gases are diverted to a coal mill and exhausted through a separate stack, then kiln-specific THC and HCl limits must be calculated as flow-weighted values that account for the coal mill stack and testing/measurements for THC and HCl must be performed either upstream of the coal mill or at the coal mill stack.

If subject to the PM limits in §63.1343(b), then initial PM compliance must be demonstrated using Method 5 or 5I and ongoing compliance must be demonstrated using a PM continuous parametric monitoring system (PM CPMS) and repeated performance testing per the procedures in §63.1349(b)(1) and §63.1350(b).

If mercury emission limits apply to the kiln, and kiln gases are diverted to a coal mill with a separate stack, then the owner must account for mercury emitted from the coal mill by conducting performance tests of the coal mill (e.g., Method 29 or 30B) and by summing hourly mercury emissions from kiln and coal mill to calculate the rolling 30 kiln operating day emission rate.

If you elect to demonstrate compliance with total organic HAP (oHAP) instead of the THC limit, and your kiln has an inline coal mill with a separate stack, then you must measure oHAP at the coal mill inlet or outlet and include the coal mill in the flow-weighted average oHAP calculation for the kiln.
If the onsite source is subject to standards for nonmetallic mineral processing plants in 40 CFR part 60 subpart OOO, then that onsite source is not subject to this subpart.

If the source is subject to a different emissions limit or monitoring requirement for the same pollutant under another regulation in title 40, then compliance with the most stringent applicable requirement obviates the less stringent requirement until the more stringent requirement is met.

If the coal mill exhaust is commingled with kiln exhaust and sent to the kiln PM control device as a single stream, then an alternative (commingled) PM limit calculated per the subpart equations may apply instead of treating stacks separately.

If THC/THC CEMS or periodic THC testing is required and the coal mill has a separate stack, then performance tests on the coal mill stack (and alkali bypass, if present) must be conducted using Method 25A and repeated every 30 months as specified.

candidates.title: General Provisions (Performance testing and monitoring requirements applicable to all subparts)

criteria.criterion: If an affected source is required by a relevant subpart standard to conduct performance testing (e.g., to demonstrate PM, HCl, THC, D/F, or Hg compliance), then the owner/operator must perform the tests, notifications, site-specific test plan, QA, and reporting as required by §63.7.

If a continuous monitoring system (CEMS, CPMS, COMS, BLDS) is required to demonstrate compliance, then the monitoring system must be installed, operated, maintained, quality-assured, and the data reduced and reported according to the procedures in §63.8.

If emissions from two or more affected sources are combined before release to the atmosphere, then the owner/operator may install applicable CMS on each emission stream or on the combined emissions stream provided the monitoring is sufficient to demonstrate compliance with the relevant standard.

checklist: Confirm whether the coal mill uses kiln exhaust gases (i.e., does the mill operate using kiln exhaust as the heat/source) to determine if it is an 'in-line coal mill' per 63.1341.
Confirm whether the coal mill exhaust is vented through a separate stack or is commingled with the kiln exhaust (and whether coal mill exhaust is routed to the kiln PM control device).

Identify and record exhaust volumetric flow rates for the kiln stack, coal mill stack, and alkali bypass stack (Qk, Qcm, Qab) and current units, and record clinker production rate (tons clinker) and feed-to-clinker ratio used on-site.
Determine whether the facility is a Portland cement plant and whether it is a major or area source (affects which limits in Table 1 apply).

Inventory existing control devices on the coal mill stack and kiln (fabric filter/ESP, wet/dry scrubber, tray tower, sorbent injection, activated carbon injection) and note whether coal mill exhaust passes through the same control device as the kiln.

Determine which pollutants you are required to monitor for the kiln (PM, THC/total organic HAP, HCl, mercury, D/F) and whether corresponding CEMS/CPMS/BLDS/PM CPMS or Hg sorbent-trap systems are installed and where probes are located (upstream of coal mill or in coal mill stack).

Check historical or planned performance testing: methods used (Method 5/5I for PM, Method 25A for THC, Method 321 for HCl, Method 29/30B for Hg, Method 23 for D/F, Method 18/320 for oHAP), dates, and whether tests on kiln, alkali bypass and coal mill were conducted simultaneously when required.

If demonstrating PM compliance with a PM CPMS, verify the PM CPMS make/model, calibration, instrument zero procedure, span/range, and the plan for establishing and annually reassessing the site-specific operating limit.

If HCl or THC or Hg monitoring is required, verify whether monitoring will be performed upstream of the coal mill or in the coal mill stack as permitted/required, and whether initial 30 kiln operating day averages or performance test procedures are planned.

If mercury limits apply, verify plan to obtain continuous flow-rate measurement at each relevant stack and to perform annual (or 30-month if eligible) Method 29/30B testing on the coal mill/alkali bypass and to sum hourly mass emissions per §63.1350(k)(5).

Confirm whether the coal mill or unit may be subject to 40 CFR part 60 standards (e.g., subpart OOO or NSPS for coal preparation) and gather applicable part 60 citations and state permit determinations to evaluate mutual applicability and most-stringent-rule interactions.

Verify availability and accuracy records for clinker production measurement (weigh scales or kiln feed-based calculation) to meet the ±5% accuracy requirement in §63.1350(d) because several limits are expressed per ton clinker.
Record whether the coal mill exhaust has previously tested below method detection limits for Hg or other pollutants (to evaluate reduced testing frequency options) and maintain prior test reports.

Prepare (or confirm) site-specific monitoring and CMS performance plans (per §63.1350(p)) addressing sampling locations, monitoring equipment specs, QA/QC, and procedures for establishing operating limits and exceedance responses.

It does not, however, identify that the coal mill is separately subject to NSPS Subpart Y (thermal dryer) nor explicitly state the annual PM testing requirement called out by EPA—only a generic check for Part 60 applicability and non-specific ‘‘repeated testing’’ language—so only some key EPA reasons are present."}

candidates.title: National Emission Standards for Hazardous Air Pollutants for Secondary Aluminum Production (Subpart RRR)

criteria.criterion: If an establishment uses aluminum scrap (or clean charge or dross) as raw material and performs one or more listed processes (including scrap drying/delacquering/decoating), then it meets the definition of a secondary aluminum production facility and Subpart RRR is applicable to the owner or operator.

If a facility is a major source of HAPs (per the part 63 definition of major source), then each scrap dryer/delacquering kiln/decoating kiln at that secondary aluminum production facility is an affected source subject to the standards in this subpart.

If a facility is an area source of HAPs, then the dioxin and furan (D/F) requirements of this subpart apply to scrap dryer/delacquering kiln/decoating kiln units (i.e., D/F portions of the rule still apply even for area sources).
If a unit is used solely for research and development and is not used to produce a saleable product, then the requirements of this subpart do not apply to that unit.

If the facility is an aluminum die casting facility, aluminum foundry, or aluminum extrusion facility that only melts clean charge, internal scrap, or customer returns and does not operate sweat furnaces, thermal chip dryers, or scrap dryers/delacquering kilns/decoating kilns, then it is not considered a secondary aluminum production facility for purposes of this subpart.

candidates.title: General Provisions (Subpart A)

criteria.criterion: If an owner or operator is subject to Subpart RRR, then the general provisions in Subpart A identified as applicable to Subpart RRR (see the applicability appendix) apply to that owner or operator.

If Subpart RRR requires performance testing for an affected source or emission unit, then the general performance testing requirements in § 63.7 apply to that testing (timing, site-specific test plan, number of runs, reporting, etc.).

If Subpart RRR requires continuous or periodic monitoring, then the general monitoring requirements in § 63.8 apply to the required CMS/COMS/parameter monitoring and quality assurance procedures unless the RRR-specific appendix notes otherwise.

checklist: Determine whether the delamination/delacquering chambers meet the definition of a "scrap dryer/delacquering kiln/decoating kiln" (i.e., are they used primarily to remove paint, lacquer, ink, plastic, rubber or similar organics from aluminum scrap) (40 CFR 63.1503).

Confirm whether the establishment uses aluminum scrap, clean charge, or dross as raw material and whether it performs scrap drying/delacquering/decoating (to determine if the facility is a secondary aluminum production facility) (40 CFR 63.1503, 63.1500(a)).

Calculate the facility's potential-to-emit (considering controls) of HAPs to determine whether the facility is a major source (>=10 tpy of any single HAP or >=25 tpy combined) or an area source (40 CFR 63.2 referenced by 63.1500).

If the facility is a die casting, foundry, or extrusion operation, confirm whether it only melts clean charge/internal scrap/customer returns and whether it operates any sweat furnaces, thermal chip dryers, or scrap dryers/delacquering kilns (exclusion condition in 40 CFR 63.1503).
Confirm whether the delamination units are operated only for research and development and do not produce a saleable product (exemption in 40 CFR 63.1500(d)).

Identify whether each delamination unit vents to atmosphere or to an add-on control device (e.g., afterburner, fabric filter) and document control devices and capture/collection systems (relevant to applicability of specific emission limits and monitoring in 40 CFR 63.1505, 63.1510).

If controls exist (afterburner, fabric filter), record design/residence time and typical operating temperature (for afterburner applicability and alternative limits per 40 CFR 63.1505(e) and monitoring in 40 CFR 63.1512(m)/(o)).

If subject to the rule, be prepared to develop/produce OM&M plan, monitoring plans, and performance test documentation per Subpart RRR requirements and the applicable Subpart A requirements (OM&M and testing obligations cited in 40 CFR 63.1510, 63.1511, 63.7, 63.8).

Document whether product granules are subsequently melted by you or your customers (note: the secondary production definition and applicability focus on processes performed at the facility; document downstream use as part of record).

If the facility is a major source and the delamination units are affected sources, determine expected emissions (PM, THC, D/F, HCl, HF as applicable) to identify which specific emission limits and monitoring requirements in 40 CFR 63.1505 and 63.1510/63.1512 will apply.

The answer includes the 63.1503 definition/identification of scrap dryer/delacquering/decoating units and the checklist/criteria state applicability is based on processes performed at the facility (not on whether recovered metal is later melted), matching the EPA note about the post‑2015 applicability change."}

candidates.title: Paint Stripping and Miscellaneous Surface Coating Operations (area sources)

criteria.criterion: If you operate an area source of HAP and perform paint stripping using methylene chloride (MeCl) for removal of dried paint, then your paint stripping operations are subject to this subpart.

If you operate an area source of HAP and perform spray application of coatings to motor vehicles or mobile equipment (other than applications that meet the definition of facility maintenance), then your motor vehicle and mobile equipment surface coating operations are subject to this subpart.

If you are the owner or operator of a motor vehicle or mobile equipment surface coating operation and you spray apply no coatings that contain the target HAP (as defined in this subpart) and you submit the required petition or notification and certification to the Administrator, then you may be exempted from the surface coating provisions of this subpart.
citations: 40 CFR 63.11180 (target HAP / target HAP containing coating definition)

criteria.criterion: If your surface coating activity meets the subpart's definition of facility maintenance, then that surface coating is excluded from motor vehicle and mobile equipment surface coating applicability under this subpart.

If you perform any paint stripping using MeCl (regardless of annual quantity), you must implement the management practices in this subpart to minimize MeCl evaporative emissions, and if annual usage exceeds one ton you must develop and implement a written MeCl minimization plan and retain usage records on site.

If you spray apply coatings that contain target HAP compounds at or above the numeric thresholds in the definition (>=0.1% by mass for carcinogenic target HAP and >=1.0% by mass for other target HAP), then those coatings are target HAP containing coatings for purposes of this subpart.
citations: 40 CFR 63.11180 (target HAP / target HAP containing coating definition)

criteria.criterion: If your activities are covered under another area source NESHAP or meet one of the listed exclusions (e.g., certain federal military/NASA installations, research/lab, quality control, personal hobby without compensation), then those activities are not subject to this subpart.

candidates.title: General Provisions (performance testing and monitoring)

criteria.criterion: If a relevant standard requires performance testing of an affected source, then the owner or operator must perform the required performance tests within 180 days of the compliance date unless a waiver or extension is obtained under the General Provisions.

If a relevant standard requires a continuous monitoring system (CMS) or other monitoring, then the provisions of §63.8 (monitoring design, operation, performance evaluation, and QA/QC) apply to that monitoring.

If an owner or operator seeks to use alternative test or monitoring methods or obtain waivers/approvals, then they must follow the procedures and notification/approval timelines in §§63.7 and 63.8 for site-specific plans, validations, and Administrator approval.

checklist: Determine whether your facility is an area source (i.e., not a major source as defined in 40 CFR 63.11170(b) and 40 CFR 63.2).

Confirm whether you perform spray application of coatings to assembled motor vehicles or mobile equipment (fixed-location autobody/refinish shop) versus facility maintenance or other excluded activity (compare operations to the 'facility maintenance' definition in 40 CFR 63.11180).

Inventory every coating you spray-apply and verify target HAP content using supplier formulation data/MSDS as allowed by the rule; verify that none exceed the target HAP thresholds (>=0.1% by mass for carcinogenic target HAP; >=1.0% by mass for manganese) per 40 CFR 63.11180.

If claiming the exemption (no target HAP coatings), prepare the required petition or, on/after May 9, 2023, submit the notification/certification to the Administrator and retain on-site records describing coatings and the certification (see 40 CFR 63.11170(a)(2) and 63.11175).

Determine whether you perform any paint stripping with methylene chloride (MeCl); if yes, quantify annual MeCl usage from purchase/usage records to see if it exceeds 1 ton/year (triggers written MeCl minimization plan requirements) per 40 CFR 63.11173(b) and (c)/(e).

If you use MeCl for paint stripping, keep on-site documentation of annual MeCl usage and, if >1 ton/year, develop/implement and maintain the written MeCl minimization plan and post required placards as specified in 40 CFR 63.11173.

If you intend to claim exemption or are subject to the subpart, check notification/reporting deadlines and submission method (initial notification, notification of compliance status, annual notifications) and whether submission via CEDRI/CDX is required (see 40 CFR 63.11175 and 63.11176).
Verify whether any other area source NESHAP covers your activities (which would exclude applicability under 40 CFR 63.11169(d)(6)).
Document whether your spray booths, spray guns, painter training, and gun-cleaning practices meet the work-practice and equipment requirements in §63.11173(e)–(g) in case the subpart applies.

judge_text: {"score":2,"reason":"All of the EPA’s key points are reflected: the spray-coating exemption under 63.11170(a)(2) based on certification of no target-HAP coatings is captured (criteria and checklist items about certification/notification under §63.11170/63.11175), methylene chloride paint stripping remains subject (criteria citing §63.11169/63.11170 and MeCl management requirements §63.11173), and the requirement to submit initial notification/comply if target-HAP coatings are later used is noted (criteria/checklist citing §63.11175)."}

candidates.title: General Provisions (Subpart A)

criteria.criterion: If your facility is subject to any relevant standard under Part 63, then the General Provisions in Subpart A apply as part of that relevant standard.
If a relevant subpart requires performance testing for your affected source, then you must meet the performance testing requirements in § 63.7.
If a relevant subpart requires continuous or other monitoring for your affected source, then you must meet the monitoring requirements in § 63.8.

candidates.title: Area Source Paint Stripping and Miscellaneous Surface Coating Operations (Subpart HHHHHH)

criteria.criterion: If you operate an area source of HAP and perform any of the activities listed in § 63.11170(a)(1)–(3) (MeCl paint stripping, spray application of coatings to motor vehicles/mobile equipment, or spray application of coatings that contain the target HAP to plastic and/or metal parts or products), then your source is subject to this subpart.

If you are an owner/operator of a motor vehicle or mobile equipment surface coating operation and you spray apply no coatings that contain any target HAP (per the target HAP definition and thresholds), then you may petition the Administrator for an exemption or may submit the Administrator notification (in lieu of a petition) that you do not spray apply any target HAP-containing coatings.

If you operate an area source and you do not perform paint stripping with MeCl, you do not perform spray application to motor vehicles/mobile equipment, and you do not perform spray application of coatings that contain the target HAP to metal or plastic parts/products, then you are not subject to this subpart for those activities.

candidates.title: Surface Coating of Miscellaneous Metal Parts and Products (Subpart MMMM)

criteria.criterion: If you own or operate an affected source that uses 946 liters (250 gal) per year or more of coatings that contain HAP in the surface coating of miscellaneous metal parts and products and the affected source is a major source (or is located at or part of a major source of HAP), then you are subject to this subpart.

If your coating operation at the facility uses only coatings, thinners, and cleaning materials that contain no organic HAP (as determined under the referenced test/determination provisions), then that coating operation is excluded from this subpart.

If your surface coating operation meets any of the specific exclusions listed in § 63.3881(c)(1)–(17) (for example research/laboratory, quality control, facility maintenance, small-volume exemptions, or coverage under another surface-coating NESHAP), then that operation is not subject to Subpart MMMM.

checklist: Is the facility an area source or a major source of HAP (verify using the major source thresholds and whether the facility is located at/part of a major source)? (see 40 CFR 63.11170(b) and 40 CFR 63.3881(b))

For the polyurea line: is the coating spray-applied (hand-held or other atomizing device) as defined by the applicable subpart(s)? (see 40 CFR 63.11180 spray-applied definition and 40 CFR 63.3981 coating/coating operation definitions)

Does the polyurea coating contain any target HAP (Cr, Pb, Mn, Ni, Cd) at or above the threshold concentrations (≥0.1% by mass for carcinogenic target HAP and ≥1.0% by mass for manganese) when considered 'as applied' (or, per the rule, you may rely on supplier formulation/MSDS data)? (see 40 CFR 63.11180 target HAP / target HAP containing coating)

Are the parts coated on the polyurea line motor vehicles or mobile equipment (assembled vehicles) as defined in Subpart HHHHHH, or miscellaneous metal parts/products? (see 40 CFR 63.11180; 40 CFR 63.3881(a))

If the facility applies target-HAP-containing coatings on other lines at the same contiguous facility under common control, is the polyurea line part of the same affected source collection (mixing rooms, spray booths, guns, cleaning equipment, storage, etc.)? (see 40 CFR 63.11171(b) and 40 CFR 63.3882(b))

Annual coating usage for the polyurea line and the facility: how many liters/gallons per year of coatings containing HAP are used (to compare against 946 L/yr threshold for Subpart MMMM)? (see 40 CFR 63.3881(b))

Does the facility use only non-organic-HAP coatings/thinners/cleaning materials (to qualify for the Subpart MMMM exclusion at § 63.3881(c)(1))? Verify using formulation data or MSDS per the subpart methods.
Does the polyurea operation qualify as facility maintenance, research/laboratory, or quality control (which are excluded) under the definitions in § 63.11180 and § 63.3981?

If the polyurea line coats motor vehicles/mobile equipment and you claim you apply no target-HAP coatings, have you prepared the petition or the May 9, 2023 notification (and are you retaining records describing the coatings sprayed) as allowed by § 63.11170(a)(2)?

If subject to any subpart requirements, determine whether performance testing or monitoring is required and, if so, plan to comply with § 63.7 and § 63.8 (timing, notifications, site-specific test/monitor plans, QA/QC).

candidates.title: Subpart YYYY

criteria.criterion: If the unit is a new or reconstructed stationary combustion turbine located at a major source of HAP, then it is an affected source subject to this subpart.
If the unit is a lean premix gas-fired stationary combustion turbine, then it must comply with the emission limitations and operating limitations in Table 1 and Table 2 of this subpart.

If your stationary combustion turbine is not equipped with an oxidation catalyst, then you must petition the Administrator for operating limitations you will monitor to demonstrate compliance with the formaldehyde emission limitation (or petition for approval of no additional operating limitations) and you must not conduct the initial performance test until the petition has been approved or disapproved by the Administrator.

If you petition the Administrator for approval of additional operating limitations, then your petition must identify the specific parameters to be monitored, discuss the relationship between those parameters and HAP emissions, explain how upper/lower parameter values will be established, describe the measurement and monitoring methods and instruments including their accuracy and precision, and identify recalibration frequency and methods.

If you petition the Administrator for approval of no additional operating limitations, then your petition must identify parameters that could change, discuss any relationship between parameter changes and HAP emissions, explain why establishing limits is not possible or feasible, describe possible measurement/monitoring methods and recalibration, and explain why adopting parameters as operating limitations is infeasible, unreasonable, or unnecessary.

If you are not using an oxidation catalyst, then you must continuously monitor any parameters specified in your approved petition in order to comply with the operating limitations and as specified in Table 5 of this subpart.

If you are required to comply with the formaldehyde emission limitation, then you must submit a Notification of Compliance Status, including each performance test result, before the close of business on the 60th calendar day following the completion of the performance test.

If required to perform performance tests under this subpart, then you must conduct the performance tests listed in Table 3 according to the subpart's requirements and conduct three separate test runs at high load (100 percent ±10 percent), each run lasting at least 1 hour.

If your stationary combustion turbine must comply with the formaldehyde emission limitation, then you must keep the records and submit the reports specified in this subpart including semiannual compliance reports and the records needed to show continuous compliance with each operating limitation.
If your stationary combustion turbine is a new or reconstructed lean premix gas-fired unit, then the compliance dates applicable depend on your startup date as specified in § 63.6095.

candidates.title: General Provisions

criteria.criterion: If you intend to use an alternative monitoring procedure or parameters in place of the monitoring specified in a relevant standard, then you must submit an application to the Administrator describing the proposed alternative and addressing the monitoring definition elements and the performance evaluation test plan as required in § 63.8(f)(4).

If you intend to use an alternative test method to demonstrate compliance during a performance test, then you must notify the Administrator at least 60 days before the test, validate the alternative using Method 301, and submit Method 301 validation results with your notification as required by § 63.7(f)(2) and (3).

If you are required to use a continuous monitoring system (CMS) for compliance, then you must develop and implement a CMS quality control program with written procedures and keep those procedures on record as specified in § 63.8(d).

If you will conduct performance testing, then you must notify the Administrator in writing of your intention to conduct the performance test at least 60 calendar days before the scheduled test date and provide a site-specific test plan if requested.

If you use a CMS, then you must operate and maintain it consistent with good air pollution control practices and the operational, QA/QC, and performance evaluation provisions in § 63.8, including daily checks, calibration drift procedures, and reporting of out-of-control periods.

checklist: Confirm whether the turbine is new or reconstructed (did construction or reconstruction commence after Jan 14, 2003?).
Confirm whether the facility is a major source of HAP (≥10 tpy single HAP or ≥25 tpy combined HAP).
Confirm that the unit is a lean premix gas-fired stationary combustion turbine as defined by the subpart.
Confirm whether the turbine is equipped with an oxidation catalyst (yes/no).
If no catalyst, decide whether you will petition for monitored operating limitations (and whether you instead will petition for approval of no additional operating limitations).

For a petition proposing monitored parameters (e.g., turbine speed and inlet air temperature), prepare evidence showing the relationship between each parameter and formaldehyde/HAP emissions and how limits will control emissions (per § 63.6120(f)(1)-(3)).
Specify measurement methods, monitoring instruments, their accuracy/precision, and recalibration frequency for each proposed parameter (per § 63.6120(f)(4)-(5)).
Do not schedule or conduct the initial performance test until the Administrator has approved or disapproved your petition (per § 63.6120(e)).
Plan performance testing to meet subpart requirements: conduct tests in Table 3, at high load (100% ±10%), three runs, each ≥1 hour (per § 63.6120(a),(c),(d)).

Prepare to submit the required notifications: Initial Notification deadlines and Notification of Compliance Status (including performance test results) within 60 days after test completion (per § 63.6145(c) and (f)).
If seeking alternative monitoring or test methods, prepare application and validation (Method 301) and submit ≥60 days before the performance test as required by § 63.7(f) and § 63.8(f).
Develop and implement a CMS quality control program and written procedures for CMS per § 63.8(d) (if CMS will be used for continuous monitoring).

Ensure instruments chosen for continuous monitoring can operate continuously and meet data recording and QA/QC requirements in § 63.8 (including daily calibration drift checks and recording of out-of-control periods).

Prepare to keep records and make semiannual compliance reports and other reports/records required by the subpart (including records to demonstrate continuous compliance with operating limitations) as specified in § 63.6150 and § 63.6155.
Verify startup date relative to the compliance dates in § 63.6095 to determine timing for compliance obligations.

The answer also includes related procedural items (wait for approval before testing, notifications, and CMS/QA provisions) cited in the notes."}

candidates.title: National Emission Standards for Hazardous Air Pollutants: Metal Fabrication and Finishing Area Sources

criteria.criterion: If you own or operate an area source that is primarily engaged in the operations in one of the nine metal fabrication and finishing source categories listed in § 63.11514(a)(1)–(9), then you are subject to this subpart.

If you perform dry abrasive blasting, machining, dry grinding and polishing with machines, spray painting, or welding operations that use materials that contain MFHAP or have the potential to emit MFHAP, then the affected source for that operation is subject to this subpart.

If your materials or welding rods contain metal fabrication and finishing HAP (MFHAP) at or above the thresholds defined (cadmium, chromium, lead, or nickel ≥ 0.1% by weight; manganese ≥ 1.0% by weight) as shown in manufacturer/supplier formulation data (e.g., MSDS), then those materials are considered to contain MFHAP for purposes of this subpart.
If the operations are tool or equipment repair, facility maintenance, or quality control activities as defined in § 63.11522, then those operations are not subject to this subpart.

If you commenced construction or reconstruction of the affected source before April 3, 2008 then the affected source is an existing source, and if on or after April 3, 2008 then it is a new source (which affects applicable compliance dates and requirements).

If a welding affected source uses 2,000 pounds or more per year of welding rod containing one or more MFHAP (rolling 12-month basis), then additional management practice and fume-control monitoring/recordkeeping requirements in § 63.11516(f)(3)–(8) apply.

candidates.title: National Emission Standards for Hazardous Air Pollutants: Paint Stripping and Miscellaneous Surface Coating Operations at Area Sources

criteria.criterion: If you operate an area source and perform spray application of coatings to motor vehicles and mobile equipment located in stationary structures at fixed locations (or mobile repair/refinishing operations) then you are subject to this subpart (unless you successfully petition/notify that you do not spray apply target-HAP coatings).

If you perform spray application of coatings that contain the target HAP to a plastic and/or metal substrate on a part or product (and the application is not facility maintenance), then you are subject to this subpart.
If you perform paint stripping using methylene chloride (MeCl) to remove dried paint, then you are subject to this subpart.

If your affected source meets the criteria for a new source (commenced construction after September 17, 2007 and the equipment was not used for coating prior to that date), then it is a new affected source; otherwise it is an existing affected source.
If your activity qualifies as facility maintenance (see the referenced definitions in this subpart), then the spray coating or paint stripping activity may be excluded from this subpart.

candidates.title: National Emission Standards for Hazardous Air Pollutants: Shipbuilding and Ship Repair Operations

criteria.criterion: If you perform shipbuilding and ship repair operations at a facility that is a major source of HAP, then this subpart applies to that facility.

If you are an existing area source that increases emissions (or potential to emit) such that the source becomes a major source, then you must comply with this subpart within one year after becoming a major source.

If a coating is used in volumes of less than 200 liters (52.8 gallons) per year and the total volume of coatings exempt under this provision does not exceed 1,000 liters (264 gallons) per year at the facility, then that coating is exempt from the provisions of this subpart (provided it is labeled and recorded as required).

candidates.title: General Provisions (Part 63 Subpart A)

criteria.criterion: If you are subject to a relevant standard under Part 63, then Subpart A (General Provisions) applies to you, including the definitions and applicability rules in § 63.2.

If a relevant standard requires performance testing, you must follow the performance testing timing, notification, QA/QC, and reporting requirements in § 63.7 unless a waiver or other exception applies.
If monitoring is required by a relevant standard, you must follow the monitoring, CMS operation/maintenance, QA/QC, and data handling procedures in § 63.8.

checklist: Determine whether the facility is a major source or an area source (calculate potential to emit and actual emissions; major source = ≥10 tpy single HAP or ≥25 tpy combined HAP per 40 CFR part 63/§63.2).

Determine whether the facility is "primarily engaged" (≥50% of production over the previous continuous 12 months) in one of the nine metal fabrication and finishing source categories in Table 1 of Subpart XXXXXX (document the metric used and the 12‑month period) per §63.11514(a) and §63.11522 (primarily engaged).

Inventory all operations: list whether you perform dry abrasive blasting, welding, machining, dry grinding/dry polishing with machines, or spray painting (include whether activities are performed indoors/outdoors and object sizes).

Collect MSDS/manufacturer formulation data for all coatings, solvents, welding rods, abrasives and any other materials to determine MFHAP content (cadmium, chromium, lead, nickel ≥0.1% by weight; manganese ≥1.0% by weight) per §63.11514(b) and §63.11522.

Record annual volumes (rolling 12‑month) of all coatings and solvents (gallons per year) and of individual coatings to check Subpart II low‑usage exemptions (≤52.8 gal per coating and ≤264 gal total low‑usage) and to determine applicability of HHHHHH provisions.

Determine whether coating/spray activities are classified as facility maintenance, tool/equipment repair, or quality control (compare your activities to the definitions in §63.11522 and the exceptions in §§63.11514(f) and 63.11170(a)(2)).

If you perform spray painting, document application method (HVLP, electrostatic, airless, etc.), whether parts are painted in spray booths/rooms, whether objects exceed size thresholds (e.g., >15 ft for spray painting exemptions in XXXXXX), and painter training records per §63.11516(d).

If you perform dry abrasive blasting, document whether enclosures are totally enclosed and unvented, vented, or open/outdoor; whether blasted objects exceed 8 ft in any dimension; and whether capture and filtration control devices are used and manufacturer's specifications are available per §63.11516(a).

If you perform welding, track welding rod usage (pounds per rolling 12‑month) and determine if ≥2,000 lb/yr of MFHAP-containing rods to identify additional requirements; document fume capture/control, and be prepared for visual fugitive emission monitoring per §63.11516(f).

Maintain and make available records of applicability determinations, notifications, certifications, manufacturer specifications for control devices and equipment operation, filter efficiency/waterspray demonstrations, spray paint worker training, welding emissions monitoring and any Site‑Specific Welding Emissions Management Plan, and keep records for the required retention periods per §63.11519 and §63.2.

Document construction/reconstruction/startup dates for affected equipment to determine new vs existing affected source status (compare to April 3, 2008 for Subpart XXXXXX and September 17, 2007 for HHHHHH) per §§63.11514(c)–(d) and 63.11171(c).

If using or considering performance tests or CMS, confirm notification and site‑specific test plan timing and QA requirements in §§63.7 and 63.8 (60 days notification, audit/sample plans, QA/QC) before testing.
