candidates.title: General Provisions

criteria.criterion: If your facility contains an 'affected source' as the collection of equipment and activities included in a section 112(c) source category or subcategory, then the General Provisions in part 63 apply to that affected source.
If a relevant standard requires performance testing for your affected source, then you must perform such performance tests within 180 days of the compliance date unless a waiver applies.

If a relevant standard requires continuous monitoring systems or other monitoring, then the monitoring provisions and minimum operation/quality assurance requirements in this section apply to that monitoring.

candidates.title: Metal Fabrication and Finishing Area Sources NESHAP

criteria.criterion: If you own or operate an area source that is primarily engaged (≥50% of production over the prior continuous 12 months, measured by an appropriate production metric) in operations in one of the nine metal fabrication and finishing source categories listed in §63.11514(a)(1)–(9), then your facility is subject to this subpart.

If you operate any of the affected-source operations defined in §63.11514(b)(1)–(5) (dry abrasive blasting, machining, dry grinding/dry polishing with machines, spray painting, welding) that use materials that contain MFHAP or have the potential to emit MFHAP, then those affected-source provisions of this subpart apply to those operations.

If the materials you use contain MFHAP (cadmium, chromium, lead, or nickel ≥0.1% by weight; manganese ≥1.0% by weight based on manufacturer/supplier formulation data), then the provisions for MFHAP-emitting metal fabrication and finishing operations apply.

If your welding affected source uses 2,000 pounds or more per year of welding rod containing one or more MFHAP (rolling 12-month basis), then you must demonstrate implementation of the management practices or fume control measures specified in §63.11516(f)(3)–(8) (Tier 1–3 requirements and Site-Specific Welding Emissions Management Plan as applicable).
If your operations are limited to tool or equipment repair, facility maintenance, or quality control activities as defined in §63.11522, then this subpart does not apply to those operations.
If you perform spray-applied painting using paints that contain MFHAP, then you must implement the spray-painting management practices and equipment/filter requirements in §63.11516(d).

candidates.title: Surface Coating of Miscellaneous Metal Parts and Products NESHAP

criteria.criterion: If you own or operate an affected source that uses 946 liters (250 gallons) per year or more of coatings that contain hazardous air pollutants in the surface coating of miscellaneous metal parts and products and your affected source is a major source, then you are subject to this subpart.
If your facility is not a major source (i.e., is an area source) then the applicability criterion in §63.3881(b) is not met and this subpart does not apply on the basis of the major-source cutoff.

If your surface coating operation is an exempt type listed in §63.3881(c) (for example research/lab, janitorial/maintenance, hobby noncommercial, or uses coatings in volumes <189 liters (50 gal) per year with total exempt coatings ≤946 liters (250 gal) per year), then this subpart does not apply to those coating activities.

checklist: Determine whether the facility is an area source or a major source for HAPs (calculate facility potential to emit for individual HAPs and combined HAPs).

Identify which of the nine metal fabrication and finishing categories (Table 1 of the subpart) best fits your products (e.g., Industrial Machinery and Equipment Finishing Operations or Fabricated Metal Products) and document the basis.

Calculate whether production of the listed product(s) represents ≥50% of facility production over the previous continuous 12 months using an appropriate metric (units, linear/area measure, or other industry-suited metric) to determine 'primarily engaged' status; retain documentation and rationale.

Count and categorize parts/products (or other metric) to confirm what fraction of pumps undergo finishing operations (dry machining, dry grinding, dry abrasive blasting, spray painting, welding) versus simple assembly/repair.

For each finishing operation, verify whether materials used (base metals, paints/coatings, welding rods, blasting media) contain MFHAP using supplier formulation data or MSDS: cadmium, chromium, lead, or nickel ≥0.1% by weight; manganese ≥1.0% by weight.
Measure annual usage of coatings that contain HAPs (gallons or liters per year) to check the 946 L (250 gal) threshold for subpart MMMM applicability.
For welding, track rolling 12-month usage of welding rod containing MFHAP to determine if it meets or exceeds 2,000 pounds per year.

Determine whether finishing activities performed are classified as tool/equipment repair, facility maintenance, or quality control per §63.11522 (if so, those activities may be exempt from Subpart XXXXXX).

If spray painting is performed, determine whether it is spray-applied (subject to Subpart XXXXXX) and whether paints contain MFHAP; if so, document spray booth/filter type and worker training plans per §63.11516(d).

Document and retain records of applicability determinations, production metrics and rationale for 'primarily engaged' determination, coating/welding usage logs, and any manufacturer's specifications for control devices or filters as required by the cited subpart sections.

The answer includes the Industrial Machinery and Equipment Finishing Operations category and the XXXXXX criterion stating an area source is subject if 'primarily engaged' (≥50% of production) in a listed category, plus a checklist item to identify the applicable category and to calculate ≥50% production of listed products — which captures EPA’s two key points that pump manufacturing is in that category and 'primarily engaged' is judged by product production, not by the share of units that receive finishing."}

candidates.title: National Emission Standards for Hazardous Air Pollutants for Stationary Reciprocating Internal Combustion Engines (RICE NESHAP)

criteria.criterion: If you own or operate a reciprocating internal combustion engine that is not mobile and is not a non-road engine (i.e., a stationary RICE) located at a major or area source of HAP emissions, then the engine is an affected source under Subpart ZZZZ.

If the engine is used to propel a motor vehicle or otherwise meets the definition of a non-road engine (as referenced in §63.6585(a)), then it is not a stationary RICE and is not subject to Subpart ZZZZ.

If the plant site emits or has the potential to emit a single HAP at a rate of 10 tons per year or more or a combination of HAP at 25 tons per year or more, then the site is a major source and the stationary RICE are evaluated as located at a major source; otherwise they are evaluated as located at an area source.

If the stationary RICE meets the definition of emergency stationary RICE in §63.6675 and operates according to the provisions referenced in §63.6585(f), then that emergency stationary RICE may be excluded from this subpart as listed in §63.6585(f).
If the stationary RICE is being tested at a stationary RICE test cell/stand, then it is excluded from being an affected source under this subpart.

If your engine is new or reconstructed and located at an area source, then in many cases meeting the requirements of 40 CFR part 60 subpart IIII (compression ignition) or subpart JJJJ (spark ignition) satisfies part 63 and no further requirements apply under this part as specified in §63.6590(c).

If the engine's site rating, date of construction or reconstruction, and whether it is new/existing/reconstructed meet the thresholds and dates in §63.6590, then determine applicability and compliance dates under Subpart ZZZZ accordingly.

candidates.title: General Provisions (Subpart A)

criteria.criterion: If a relevant standard under this part applies to your affected source, then the definitions in §63.2 apply for interpreting terms used throughout the standards.

If a relevant standard requires performance testing, then you must perform performance tests in accordance with §63.7 (including the timing, notification, site-specific test plan, and QA requirements) unless a waiver or extension applies.

If a relevant standard requires continuous monitoring systems or other monitoring, then the monitoring requirements and procedures in §63.8 apply (installation, operation, QA/QC, out-of-control reporting, and data reduction).

checklist: Is each engine a reciprocating internal combustion engine that is 'not mobile' (i.e., not used to propel a motor vehicle and not a non-road engine under 40 CFR 1068.30)? (see 40 CFR 63.6585(a))

Are the engines mounted on portable vacuum units that are moved around the site in a manner that would make them 'mobile' or do they remain at fixed locations during use (document how and how often they are moved)?
Is the fuel type compression-ignition (diesel) for each engine? (identify as diesel/compression ignition) (see 40 CFR 63.6675)
What is the site rating (brake horsepower, HP) of each engine? (determine site-rated HP to compare to thresholds in §63.6590)
When were the engines constructed, installed, or reconstructed (dates) to determine new vs existing vs reconstructed status per §63.6590?

How many hours per year does each engine operate and for what purposes (emergency-only, routine production, cleanup operations)? (to evaluate emergency/limited-use status and applicability of exclusions)

Does the facility (plant site) emit or have the potential to emit ≥10 tons/year of any single HAP (e.g., beryllium) or ≥25 tons/year combined HAPs (calculate actual and potential to emit for the site)? (see 40 CFR 63.6585(b)-(c))

Are the engines operated as emergency stationary RICE and do they meet the full definition and operational requirements referenced in §63.6675 and §63.6640(f)? (document the emergency-use criteria and operating records)
Are the engines being tested at a stationary RICE test cell/stand at any time? (if yes, document test cell/stand status) (see 40 CFR 63.6585 and 63.6590(a))

Are the engines new or reconstructed and located at an area source such that 40 CFR part 60 subpart IIII (CI) or JJJJ (SI) might apply instead of further Part 63 requirements? (determine construction dates and whether Part 60 standards apply) (see 40 CFR 63.6590(c))
Is any engine <100 HP and/or otherwise specifically exempt from initial notification or numerical standards per §63.6645(a)(5)? (document HP and applicability of notification exceptions)

If you determine Subpart ZZZZ may apply, gather records needed for §63.7 performance testing and §63.8 monitoring (startup dates, maintenance records, operating hours, test plans, and any existing emissions test data).

candidates.title: National Emission Standards for Engine Test Cells/Stands (Subpart PPPPP)

criteria.criterion: If you own or operate an engine test cell/stand located at a major source of HAP emissions, then you are subject to this subpart.

If the apparatus is used for testing uninstalled engines (an engine not installed in or integrated into the final product), then the apparatus meets the engine test cell/stand/uninstalled engine definition relevant to this subpart.

If the collection of equipment and activities are engine test cells/stands used for testing uninstalled stationary or mobile engines located at a major source, then that collection is the 'affected source' for this subpart.

If the affected source is new or reconstructed and is used in whole or in part for testing internal combustion engines with rated power of 25 horsepower or more and is located at a major source, then the affected source must meet the emission limitations in Table 1 of this subpart.

If the affected source is an existing affected source (construction or reconstruction commenced on or before May 14, 2002), then that affected source does not have to meet the requirements of this subpart and of subpart A of this part.

If any portion of a new or reconstructed affected source located at a major source is used exclusively for testing internal combustion engines with rated power less than 25 horsepower, then that portion does not have to meet the requirements of this subpart and of subpart A except for the initial notification requirement.

If any portion of a new or reconstructed affected source is used exclusively for testing combustion turbine engines, rocket engines, in non-commercial research and teaching, or for testing/evaluating fuels, transmissions, or electronics as listed in paragraphs (d)(1)–(4), then that portion does not have to meet the requirements of this subpart and of subpart A.
If you use add-on emission controls on a new or reconstructed affected source, then you must meet the operating limits specified in Table 2 established during the performance test.

If a CEMS is required or used to meet the CO or THC emission limitations, then you must install, operate, and maintain CEMS to monitor CO or THC and O2 at the outlet (or at inlet and outlet for percent reduction) according to the specified performance specifications and continuous operation requirements.

If you are required to demonstrate initial compliance, then you must conduct the initial compliance demonstrations and initial performance evaluations (capture/control system and CEMS) according to the procedures and equations specified in this subpart within the timelines in Table 3 and § 63.9310.

If you must conduct performance tests for this subpart, then those performance tests must be conducted under representative engine testing and capture/control operating conditions and follow the performance test procedures in §§ 63.9321–63.9324.

candidates.title: General Provisions (Subpart A)

criteria.criterion: If you are subject to a relevant standard under this part, then the definitions in § 63.2 (including 'major source', 'affected source', 'potential to emit', and 'uninstalled engine') apply to determine applicability.

If required to do performance testing by a relevant standard, then you must perform the performance tests within 180 days of the compliance date for the affected source unless a waiver or Administrator-approved extension applies.

If required to conduct a performance test, then you must notify the Administrator of intent to test at least 60 calendar days before the initial scheduled test, prepare any requested site-specific test plan, and follow the quality assurance and test conduct provisions in § 63.7.

If a relevant standard requires use of continuous monitoring systems (CMS/CEMS), then the owner/operator must comply with the monitoring requirements, operation/maintenance, quality control, performance evaluation, data reduction, and reporting provisions in § 63.8.

If multiple emissions streams are combined or multiple CMS are used, then monitoring may be installed per allowances in § 63.8(b) but must still demonstrate compliance and provide representative measures as required.

checklist: Confirm whether each test engine is 'uninstalled' (not installed in or integrated into the final product) per 40 CFR 63.9375 and 40 CFR 63.9285(a).
Confirm whether the apparatus in which the engines sit is an 'engine test cell/stand' used for testing uninstalled stationary or mobile engines per 40 CFR 63.9285(a) and 40 CFR 63.9290(a).
Determine whether the plant is a 'major source' of HAP (potential to emit ≥10 tpy single HAP or ≥25 tpy combined HAP) per 40 CFR 63.9285(c) and 40 CFR 63.2.
Determine the rated power of each engine (hp) to check the 25 hp threshold for exemptions in 40 CFR 63.9290(c) and applicability in 40 CFR 63.9300.
Establish whether the affected source is existing (construction/reconstruction commenced on or before May 14, 2002) or new/reconstructed to evaluate exemption in 40 CFR 63.9290(1–3) and 63.9290(b).

Confirm whether any portion of the test activities is used exclusively for combustion turbine engines, rocket engines, non‑commercial research/teaching, or testing/evaluating fuels, transmissions, or electronics (exempt portions) per 40 CFR 63.9290(d)(1)–(4).
Calculate the plant's potential to emit (PTE) for HAP to determine major vs area source status per 40 CFR 63.2 (potential to emit definition) and 40 CFR 63.9285(c).

Determine whether the affected source uses add-on control devices or CEMS (if add-on controls/CEMS are present, review operating limits, monitoring, and performance test obligations) per 40 CFR 63.9302 and 40 CFR 63.9307.

If subject to the subpart, identify applicable compliance dates and the requirement to conduct initial compliance demonstrations/performance tests within 180 days per 40 CFR 63.9310 and 40 CFR 63.7(a)(2).

If performance testing or CEMS performance evaluations will be done, prepare site-specific test and CMS performance evaluation plans and submit notifications at least 60 days before testing per 40 CFR 63.7(b)(1) and 40 CFR 63.8(e)(3)(iii).

Verify whether any portion of testing has been operated for SSM or nonrepresentative conditions (operations during SSM/nonoperation are not representative for performance tests) per 40 CFR 63.9321(a)(1) and 40 CFR 63.7(e)(1).

It also omits mention of applicability to 40 CFR 63.4241 et seq. (Subpart ZZZZ) and NSPS IIII noted by EPA."}

candidates.title: National Emission Standards for Hazardous Air Pollutants for Coal- and Oil-Fired Electric Utility Steam Generating Units (MATS)

criteria.criterion: If you own or operate a coal-fired EGU or an oil-fired EGU as defined in § 63.10042, then you are subject to this subpart.
If an electric steam generating unit meets the definition of a natural gas-fired EGU in § 63.10042, then it is not subject to this subpart.

If a unit has the capability of combusting more than 25 MW of coal or oil but did not fire sufficient coal or oil to satisfy the average annual heat input requirement in § 63.10042, then it is not subject to this subpart.

If an EGU burns oil for more than 10.0 percent of the average annual heat input during the three previous calendar years or for more than 15.0 percent of the annual heat input during any one of those calendar years, then it meets the definition of an oil-fired EGU (and is subject if otherwise covered).

candidates.title: National Emission Standards for Hazardous Air Pollutants for Major Sources: Industrial, Commercial, and Institutional Boilers and Process Heaters (Boiler MACT)

criteria.criterion: If you own or operate an industrial, commercial, or institutional boiler or process heater that is located at or is part of a major source of HAP as defined in § 63.2, then you are subject to this subpart except as specified in § 63.7491.

If a boiler or process heater is an electric utility steam generating unit (EGU) covered by subpart UUUUU or is a natural gas-fired EGU that fires at least 85 percent natural gas on an annual heat input basis, then it is not subject to this subpart.

candidates.title: General Provisions

criteria.criterion: If a stationary source emits or has the potential to emit, considering controls, 10 tons per year or more of any single HAP or 25 tons per year or more of any combination of HAP, then it is a major source as defined in § 63.2.
If a source is subject to a relevant standard under this part, then Subpart A general provisions apply to that source.
If an affected source is required by a relevant standard to perform performance testing, then the requirements of § 63.7 apply to that performance testing.
If an affected source is required by a relevant standard to use continuous monitoring systems (CMS), then the monitoring requirements of § 63.8 apply to that CMS.

checklist: Confirm whether the unit is an electric utility steam generating unit (EGU): does it serve a generator that produces electricity for sale and is its capacity >25 MWe (per the EGU definition in 40 CFR 63.10042)?

Calculate the unit's oil heat input percentages: the 3-year rolling average percent of heat input from oil and the percent of oil heat input for each single calendar year (use the heat input definition in 40 CFR 63.10042).

Determine whether oil combustion occurred only during startup and how startup hours are defined/counted at your unit (see the definition of startup in 40 CFR 63.10042) and whether those hours are included in heat-input percentage calculations.

Verify whether the unit meets the oil-fired EGU thresholds (oil >10% of 3-year average or >15% in any single year) or instead meets the natural gas-fired EGU definition (per 40 CFR 63.10042) or the limited-use liquid oil-fired subcategory criteria (e.g., <8% oil capacity-factor definitions in 40 CFR 63.10042).

Check the facility's Title V/permit conditions and on-site fuel handling/permit allowances to confirm which fuels the unit is 'capable of combusting' (required to determine 'fossil fuel-fired' capability under 40 CFR 63.10042).
Determine whether the boiler is located at or part of a major source of HAP by calculating site-wide potential-to-emit HAP (≥10 tpy single HAP or ≥25 tpy combined HAP) as defined in 40 CFR 63.2.

Confirm whether the unit is already identified as covered by subpart UUUUU in permits or prior determinations, or whether any permanent conversion to natural gas/biomass or enforceable limits exist that would change subpart applicability (see § 63.10000(n) and related provisions).

If considering Boiler MACT applicability, verify the unit category: is it an industrial/commercial/institutional boiler or is it an EGU excluded by § 63.7491(a) (EGU covered by UUUUU or natural gas-fired EGU ≥85% gas on annual heat input basis)?

candidates.title: Pesticide Active Ingredient (PAI) Manufacturing (Subpart MMM)

criteria.criterion: If the equipment is part of a facility-wide collection of pesticide active ingredient manufacturing process units (PAI process units) that process, use, or produce HAP and the plant site is a major source, then the affected source is subject to subpart MMM.

If the new or dedicated PAI process unit commenced construction or reconstruction after November 10, 1997 or has the potential to emit ≥10 tons/yr of any one HAP or ≥25 tons/yr combined HAP, then it is a new affected source and subject to the new-source requirements of subpart MMM.
If the PAI process unit is subject to subpart F of this part, then that PAI process unit is excluded from subpart MMM.

If a storage vessel feeding or serving the distillation column is assigned to a PAI process unit under the input/output or tank-farm assignment procedures, then that vessel and associated equipment are part of the affected source subject to subpart MMM.

candidates.title: Miscellaneous Organic Chemical Manufacturing (MCPU) (Subpart FFFF)

criteria.criterion: If you own or operate a miscellaneous organic chemical manufacturing process unit (MCPU) located at a major source that produces materials described in § 63.2435(b)(1) (e.g., organic chemicals under SIC/NAICS classifications) and the MCPU processes, uses, or generates organic HAP, and the MCPU is not subject to another Part 63 subpart, then the MCPU is subject to subpart FFFF.

If the distillation column is a nondedicated solvent recovery operation (i.e., receives used solvent from more than one MCPU), then it is within the scope of subpart FFFF as a nondedicated solvent recovery operation.
citations: 40 CFR 63.2550 (definition of nondedicated solvent recovery operation)

criteria.criterion: If the operation falls within one of the exemptions listed in § 63.2435(c) (for example certain R&D or listed NAICS exclusions), then subpart FFFF does not apply to that operation.

candidates.title: Chemical Manufacturing Process Units / Subpart F applicability (Subpart F)

criteria.criterion: If the distillation unit is part of a chemical manufacturing process unit (CMPU) that (a) manufactures as a primary product one or more chemicals listed in § 63.100(b)(1) or (b) uses as a reactant or manufactures one or more organic HAP listed in § 63.100(b)(2), and the CMPU is at a plant site that is a major source, then subparts F (and the related subparts G/H) apply to the CMPU and its distillation vents.

If the distillation unit is dedicated to a CMPU that is subject to subpart F, then each vent from the distillation unit is considered separately and is part of the source subject to subpart F per the distillation-unit assignment rules.

If the distillation unit is shared among process units, then applicability is determined by assigning the unit according to greatest input/output or the special tank-farm/distillation assignment rules in § 63.100(i)(2), and then applicability follows the CMPU to which the unit is assigned.

candidates.title: General Provisions (Subpart A)

criteria.criterion: If the plant site is a major source (i.e., emits or has the potential to emit ≥10 tons/yr of any one HAP or ≥25 tons/yr of any combination of HAP), then Part 63 subparts (including MMM, FFFF, and F) apply to affected sources at that site as defined in this part.

checklist: Determine whether your Michigan site is a major source per 40 CFR 63.2 (annual potential to emit ≥10 tpy single HAP or ≥25 tpy combined HAP).
Confirm whether the product chain is a pesticide active ingredient (PAI) and whether the distillation output is used to produce a PAI (see PAI and PAI process unit definitions).

Decide whether the new distillation column will be part of an existing PAI process unit (PAI process unit) or part of a miscellaneous organic chemical MCPU or a SOCMI/CMPU as defined in § 63.100/§ 63.2435.
Establish whether the distillation unit is 'dedicated' to a single process or 'shared' among processes (determine greatest input/output to assign the unit per § 63.1360(f) and § 63.100(i)).
If shared, document the inputs/outputs (mass flows) to determine assignment of the distillation unit or storage tanks (apply § 63.1360(f)(2)-(3) and § 63.100(i)(2)).

Determine construction/reconstruction dates (was the unit constructed/reconstructed after the new-source trigger dates listed in the subparts?) and whether the unit has potential to emit ≥10/25 tpy thresholds for new-source status (see 63.1360(b) and 63.2435(c)/(d)).

Calculate the distillation unit's potential to emit HAP (tons/yr) based on feed composition, purge/vent streams, and control devices to compare to applicability thresholds (10/25 tpy and other group thresholds).

Identify whether the distillation receives 'used solvent' from multiple units (nondedicated solvent recovery) or is a purification step for a purchased raw material (affects FFFF vs. MMM/CMPU assignment).

Determine whether existing storage tanks that hold the purchased raw material are already assigned to a PAI process unit or another subpart (document tank assignment, date of assignment, and whether tanks are in HAP service).
Document whether any other Part 63 subpart already applies to the process or tanks (e.g., if the CMPU is already subject to subpart F/G/H, that may preclude subpart MMM for that equipment).
Record raw material composition (HAP species and concentrations), vapor pressures, and storage capacities (for tank grouping and Group 1/2 determinations under applicable subparts).
Record whether any exemptions apply (research & development, NAICS exclusions, etc.) per § 63.1360(d) and § 63.2435(c).

candidates.title: General Provisions

criteria.criterion: If any relevant section 112 area-source NESHAP listed in this part applies to your affected source, then the General Provisions in Subpart A (definitions, performance testing, and monitoring requirements) apply to that affected source.

candidates.title: Chemical preparations (definitions shown)

criteria.criterion: If the cathode slurry mixing is a chemical preparations operation (mixing/blending of wet materials under NAICS 325998) and the materials processed are target HAP-containing (e.g., contain nickel at or above the target-HAP threshold), then this chemical preparations subpart applies to those operations.

candidates.title: Chemical Manufacturing Area Sources (CMPU applicability and dates)

criteria.criterion: If the cathode slurry mixing is part of a chemical manufacturing process unit (CMPU) located at an area source and the CMPU uses feedstocks or contains streams with Table 1 HAP (including metal HAP such as nickel) at concentrations above the thresholds (e.g., Table 1 HAP >0.1 percent by weight or specified metal thresholds), then the CMPU is subject to this subpart.

checklist: Determine whether the facility is an area source (calculate potential to emit for each single HAP and combined HAP to confirm below major-source thresholds).
Confirm the applicable NAICS code for the cathode mixing/coating line (is the operation part of NAICS 325 or NAICS 325998 chemical preparations?).
Document whether the cathode slurry mixing operation is a 'chemical preparation operation' (mixing/blending of wet materials, milling, extruding) as defined in 40 CFR 63.11588.
Obtain formulation/SDS data and quantify nickel content (as metal) in the active material, slurry, and feedstocks to determine if nickel ≥ 0.1% by weight (target HAP threshold).

Verify whether any other Table 1 HAP (organic or metal) or specified metal thresholds are present in feedstocks/streams above the concentrations listed in 40 CFR 63.11494(a)(2) (e.g., >0.1% for Table 1 organics or >1.0% for listed metals where specified).

Determine whether the operation is instead part of 'paints and allied products manufacturing' or another excluded category (if so, check applicability/exemptions in 40 CFR 63.11599 and 63.11494(c)(1)(i)).

candidates.title: General Provisions (definitions, performance testing, and monitoring)

criteria.criterion: If you are subject to a relevant subpart in this part that requires performance testing, then the Subpart A performance testing requirements apply to your affected source.
If you are subject to a relevant subpart in this part that requires continuous monitoring systems or other CMS, then the Subpart A monitoring requirements apply to those CMS.
If you are an affected source as defined in this part, then the definitions and terms in 40 CFR part 63, §63.2, apply for determining applicability and obligations under the subparts.

candidates.title: Chemical Manufacturing Area Source Standards (CMPU)

criteria.criterion: If you own or operate a chemical manufacturing process unit (CMPU) located at an area source of HAP and the CMPU uses feedstock or contains Table 1 HAP at or above the concentration thresholds in § 63.11494(a)(2), then your CMPU is subject to Subpart VVVVVV.

If the CMPU is not located at an area source of HAP (i.e., is a major source) or Table 1 HAP are not present above the thresholds specified in § 63.11494(a)(2), then Subpart VVVVVV does not apply to that CMPU.

If your operations are one of the chemical manufacturing area source categories or specific production activities listed in § 63.11494(c)(1)–(2) (for example, Manufacture of Paint and Allied Products subject to subpart CCCCCCC), then those operations are excluded from Subpart VVVVVV.

If your facility becomes subject to Subpart VVVVVV and you have installed a federally enforceable control device necessary to keep the source at area source levels, then you may be required to obtain a title V permit per § 63.11494(e).

candidates.title: Paints and Allied Products Area Source Standards

criteria.criterion: If you own or operate a paints and allied products manufacturing facility that is an area source of HAP and your facility processes, uses, or generates materials containing HAP, then Subpart CCCCCCC applies to the paints and allied products manufacturing processes at the facility.

If your operation is only the manufacture of raw materials (such as resins, pigments, solvents, or other raw materials used in paints and coatings) rather than the production of paints/allied products that are intended to leave a dried film on a substrate, then Subpart CCCCCCC does not apply to those raw-material manufacturing activities.

If you are an affected paints and allied products source and you add or grind dry pigments/solids containing compounds of cadmium, chromium, lead, or nickel, then you must capture particulate emissions and route them to an appropriate particulate control device (and meet related work-practice/opacity requirements) as specified in § 63.11601.

candidates.title: Chemical Preparations Area Source Standards

criteria.criterion: If you own or operate a chemical preparations facility (as defined in § 63.11588) that is a stationary area source of HAP and has at least one chemical preparations operation in target HAP service, then Subpart BBBBBBB applies to the chemical preparations operations at the facility.

If your operations fall under NAICS code 325998 chemical preparations operations as defined in § 63.11588 (mixing, blending, milling, extruding of target HAP-containing products/intermediates), then those operations meet the definition of a chemical preparations operation for Subpart BBBBBBB.
If the chemical preparations operations at your facility are subject to Subpart VVVVVV or Subpart CCCCCCC, then you are exempt from the requirements of Subpart BBBBBBB for those operations.

checklist: Confirm the facility NAICS code (is the plant classified as NAICS 3255 vs NAICS 325998 or other) and whether the facility activities are covered by the industry definitions in the subparts.
Determine whether the stationary source is an area source (PTE <10 tpy for any single HAP and <25 tpy combined) or a major source per § 63.2 / § 63.11448(b).

Confirm whether the process is a chemical manufacturing process unit (CMPU) per § 63.11494(b) (i.e., production described by NAICS 325 and includes process vessels, storage, transfers associated with production).

Verify whether Table 1 HAP (check Table 1 in the rule) are present in feedstocks, byproducts, or products in the CMPU and at what concentrations (compare to thresholds in § 63.11494(a)(2); e.g., quinoline, manganese, Cr(III) >1.0% or other Table 1 HAP >0.1%). Specifically determine whether nickel is listed in Table 1 and the % by weight in your raw materials.

If you melt raw materials in furnaces to make frit, determine whether that activity is considered 'paints and allied products manufacturing' or 'manufacture of raw materials' (paints subpart excludes manufacture of raw materials) per § 63.11607.

If operating furnaces, determine whether they are 'continuous furnaces' and whether they are charged with compounds of glass manufacturing metal HAP and produce glass at ≥45 Mg/yr (for potential applicability to the glass subpart) using § 63.11448 and § 63.11449 criteria.

If your operations include mixing, blending, milling, or extruding, document whether those operations are chemical preparations operations under § 63.11588 and whether they process target HAP-containing materials (nickel, chromium, lead, manganese thresholds) that would put them in target HAP service.

Document whether your product is intended to leave a dried film on a substrate (i.e., a paint or allied product) versus being a raw material (e.g., frit used in glazes/coatings), per the paints subpart definition in § 63.11607.

Inventory and quantify HAP emissions (actual and potential to emit) to confirm area vs major source status and to determine subpart triggers (include annual production rates, e.g., if glass/frit production rate is ≥45 Mg/yr for glass subpart furnace criterion).

If any subpart appears applicable, check whether the operation is research & development, QA/QC lab, or an ancillary activity exempted in the relevant subpart (see exemptions in § 63.11494(c), § 63.11579(d), and § 63.11607 where applicable).

If you have control devices relied on to maintain area-source status, document whether those devices are federally enforceable and whether title V permitting obligations could be triggered per § 63.11494(e).
