candidates.title: National Emission Standards for Hazardous Air Pollutants: Municipal Solid Waste Landfills

criteria.criterion: If the landfill accepted waste since November 8, 1987 (or has additional capacity) and is a major source, collocated with a major source, or an area source with design capacity ≥2.5 million Mg and estimated uncontrolled NMOC emissions ≥50 Mg/yr, then the landfill is subject to Subpart AAAA.

If the landfill is subject to this subpart, then the affected source includes the entire disposal facility in the contiguous geographic space where household waste is placed (i.e., the whole MSW landfill is regulated as the affected source).

If you propose to cap, remove, or decommission the gas collection and control system, then the collection and control system may be removed only if the landfill is closed, the system has been in operation a minimum of 15 years or you demonstrate the system will be unable to operate for 15 years due to declining gas flow, and the calculated NMOC emission rate is less than 50 Mg/yr on three successive test dates 90–180 days apart following §63.1959(c).

If you will remove or cease operation of control equipment (including decommissioning of collection system components), then you must submit an equipment removal report at least 30 days prior that includes a closure report, the initial performance test report demonstrating the 15-year minimum control period has expired or information demonstrating inability to operate 15 years, and dated copies of three successive NMOC emission rate reports showing <50 Mg/yr (or a statement certifying prior electronic submission and dates).

If you are calculating the post-collection-system NMOC emission rate for purposes of determining when the system (or components) can be decommissioned, then you must use Equation 3 (MNMOC = QLFG × CNMOC × conversion) and determine QLFG by measuring total landfill gas flow at the common header before gas movers and determine CNMOC from the common header before any gas-moving or condensate removal equipment, or use an EPA‑approved alternative method.

If a single well is decommissioned (shut down), then that well may experience a static positive pressure after shutdown to accommodate declining flows, and any design changes associated with decommissioning must be approved by the Administrator.

If the collection/control system (or wells) remain in operation while you evaluate or alter the system, then you must continue to meet the operational standards including negative pressure at each wellhead except limited exceptions, interior well temperature operational limits, and surface methane monitoring and corrective actions for exceedances.

candidates.title: General Provisions

criteria.criterion: If a relevant standard (such as Subpart AAAA) requires a performance test, then the owner or operator must perform the performance test within 180 days of the compliance date unless a waiver or extension is obtained under §63.7.

If monitoring (CMS or other monitoring) is required by a relevant standard, then monitoring must be conducted and maintained as set forth in §63.8, including QA/QC, frequency, and operation/maintenance obligations.
If you need to determine whether your landfill is a major source for applicability purposes, then use the definitions in §63.2 (e.g., the definition of 'major source') to assess that status.

checklist: Confirm whether the landfill accepted solid waste since November 8, 1987 or currently has additional capacity for waste deposition.

Verify landfill design capacity (Mg and m3) from the most recent permit or engineering calculation and confirm the value (you reported ~5.9 million Mg); document permit or calculation per §63.1981(a)(2).
Determine whether the landfill is a major source or collocated with a major source (use definitions in 40 CFR 63.2).

Obtain the latest NMOC emission rate report(s) and calculation details (Tier 1/2/3 inputs) and verify whether uncontrolled NMOC ≥50 Mg/yr or <50 Mg/yr; if using Tier 2/3, collect dates and methods used per §63.1959(a).

If seeking to decommission the entire collection/control system, verify landfill closure status per §63.1990 (is the landfill 'closed'?) and whether a closure report has been or will be submitted per §63.1981(f).

Verify how long the gas collection and control system has been in operation (installation/start dates for system components) to confirm whether the 15‑year minimum control period has expired or whether you can demonstrate inability to operate 15 years due to declining flows per §63.1957(b)(2).

For the specific well (EW-308A), confirm installation date (May 2018), whether it is an interior well, whether it is connected to the active common header, and whether decommissioning is for that single well or part of system-wide removal.

If relying on three successive NMOC emission-rate test results to support removal, assemble the three NMOC reports that are each 90–180 days apart and show MNMOC <50 Mg/yr, and confirm sampling/analysis followed §63.1959 procedures (or header flow + header CNMOC per §63.1959(c) if post-installation).

If planning to remove control equipment or decommission wells, prepare to submit an equipment removal report ≥30 days prior including required attachments (closure report, initial performance test showing 15‑year period expired or documentation of inability to operate 15 years, and three NMOC reports) per §63.1981(g).

Confirm whether any design‑plan modifications or revised collection/control system design plan approvals are required and, if so, prepare submittal to Administrator as described in §63.1981(d) and obtain approval prior to implementing design changes.

Review monitoring records for the subject well and system (monthly gauge pressure, monthly oxygen or nitrogen, wellhead temperatures, surface methane surveys) per §§63.1961 and 63.1958 to determine whether positive pressure, elevated temperature, or surface exceedances exist and whether corrective actions or enhanced monitoring are required.

If a performance test will be needed (e.g., to demonstrate the 15‑year period or other control performance), schedule the performance test and provide required notifications and QA (site-specific test plan, audit samples) consistent with §63.7 timelines and procedures.

Confirm measurement points: if using post-installation Equation 3, ensure total landfill gas flow will be measured at the common header before gas movers and CNMOC measured at the common header before any gas-moving or condensate removal equipment as required in §63.1959(c)(1)-(2).

If decommissioning will cause temporary positive pressure or other operational deviations, document the reason (declining flow, shut down) and be prepared to show these conditions fit the allowed exceptions in §63.1958(b) and the corrective-action timelines in §63.1960(a)(3).

candidates.title: Plywood and Composite Wood Products (PCWP) NESHAP

criteria.criterion: If equipment is a reconstituted wood product press or a reconstituted wood product board cooler (each a 'process unit'), then you must meet one compliance option for each process unit and you cannot combine production-based and add-on control compliance options for the same process unit.
If you choose a production-based compliance option for a process unit, then you may not use an add-on control system or a wet control device to meet that production-based option.

If you choose a concentration-based add-on control option for a reconstituted wood product press or a reconstituted wood product board cooler, then the capture device must either meet the 'wood products enclosure' design criteria or achieve a capture efficiency greater than or equal to 95 percent and you must document enclosure design or capture-efficiency verification.

If you will demonstrate compliance using performance tests or production-based mass-per-unit calculations, then you must measure process unit throughput and include capture efficiency (for presses and board coolers) in the mass-per-unit calculation per the test procedures.

If emissions from one or more process units were co-mingled prior to July 6, 2026 (a 'mixed PCWP process stream'), then the affected source must continue to comply with the add-on control system compliance options in Table 1B for that mixed stream as specified.

If you use an add-on control system, then sampling sites, capture-efficiency measurements, and inlet/outlet sampling must be located and conducted as required by the subpart's testing rules to calculate percent reduction and compliance.

candidates.title: General Provisions

criteria.criterion: If the relevant standard requires performance testing, then unless a waiver applies you must perform the tests within 180 days of the compliance date (or as otherwise specified) and follow the §63.7 performance test procedures and notifications.

If emissions from two or more affected sources or process units are combined before being released to the atmosphere, then you may install monitoring (CMS) on the combined emissions stream instead of separate streams provided the monitoring is sufficient to demonstrate compliance with the relevant standard.

checklist: Identify whether each piece of equipment (press and board cooler) is a process unit as defined in 40 CFR 63.2292 and whether each unit is new, reconstructed, or existing per 40 CFR 63.2232.

Determine which compliance option you intend to use for each process unit (production-based from Table 1A versus add-on control from Table 1B/1C/1D/1E) and confirm you will not mix production-based and add-on-control options for the same process unit (40 CFR 63.2240(a)).

Confirm whether emissions streams from the press and the board cooler are routed separately or are co-mingled (and if co-mingled, whether co-mingling occurred before July 6, 2026) to determine applicability of 'mixed PCWP process stream' provisions (40 CFR 63.2292; 40 CFR 63.2240(d)(5)).

If planning to use add-on control concentration-based options for either unit, verify whether the capture device is a permanently installed wood products enclosure that meets the design criteria or plan to measure capture efficiency and demonstrate ≥95% (and prepare to submit enclosure documentation or capture-efficiency test results per Methods 204/204A–204F or the appendix A tracer gas method) (40 CFR 63.2240(b); 40 CFR 63.2267; 40 CFR 63.2292).

If using production-based compliance options, collect and document process-unit throughput during performance tests and ensure you will not rely on add-on control devices to meet production-based limits (40 CFR 63.2262(f); 40 CFR 63.2240(a)).

If you plan to monitor combined streams rather than individual vents, confirm the combined-stream monitoring approach is sufficient to demonstrate compliance and that sampling-site locations and test methods follow the subpart requirements (40 CFR 63.8(b)(2)(i); 40 CFR 63.2262(d)).

Prepare to follow §63.7 performance testing schedule and notification requirements (e.g., 60-day notice, test within 180 days of compliance date) and ensure test plans and QA/audit provisions are in place if tests are required (40 CFR 63.7(a),(b),(c)).

candidates.title: National emission standards for hazardous air pollutants (NESHAP) for rubber tire manufacturing

criteria.criterion: If you own or operate a rubber tire manufacturing facility that is located at, or is a part of, a major source of hazardous air pollutant (HAP) emissions, then you are subject to this subpart.

If your facility includes affected sources engaged in the manufacture of rubber tires or their components (including tire production processes that use cements and solvents, such as tire repair operations), then those affected sources are covered by this subpart.

If the materials used in your tire production processes are 'cements and solvents' as defined in §63.6015, then those materials and associated processes are included in the tire production affected source regulated under this subpart.

If the affected source at your facility is a tire cord production affected source but the primary product produced at that affected source is determined to be subject to another subpart (as of that subpart's effective date or the source startup, whichever is later), then that affected source is not subject to this subpart.

If your rubber tire manufacturing affected source is a research and development facility whose primary purpose is R&D, is operated under close supervision of technically trained personnel, and is not engaged in manufacture of products for commercial sale except de minimis, then the affected source is not subject to this subpart.

candidates.title: General Provisions

criteria.criterion: If your stationary source emits or has the potential to emit (considering controls) 10 tons per year or more of any single HAP or 25 tons per year or more of any combination of HAPs, then it is a 'major source' as defined in this part for applicability determinations.

If a collection of equipment, activities, or both within a single contiguous area and under common control is included in a section 112(c) source category or subcategory, then that collection is an 'affected source' for purposes of Part 63.

checklist: Determine whether your facility is a 'rubber tire manufacturing facility' (does it produce rubber tires or components, or only perform retreading/repair?) and list specific operations performed (e.g., tire building, tire repair/retreading, tread/cement operations, puncture sealant application, tire cord production).
Calculate actual and potential to emit HAPs for the entire stationary source (in tons per year) to determine whether the facility is a major source (≥10 tpy single HAP or ≥25 tpy combined HAP).

Identify whether your tire-related processes use any materials that meet the subpart's definition of 'cements and solvents' (e.g., tread/undertread/bead cements, green tire spray, paints, inks, slab dip, process cleaning materials); compile MSDS/CPDS or other documentation of HAP mass percent for each material.

Determine whether any tire cord production operations exist and, if so, whether the primary product from that affected source is subject to another subpart (identify primary product based on greatest operating time over a 5-year period or expected utilization).

Confirm whether your facility (or any affected source at the facility) is an R&D facility whose primary purpose is research and development and not commercial manufacture (and whether any commercial sales are de minimis).
Establish whether all emissions sources are within a single contiguous area and under common control (to aggregate PTE for major/area source determination).

If treating processes as potentially subject, quantify monthly and annual usage of cements/solvents (mass) and quantity of rubber used (megagrams) to enable emissions calculations under the subpart's methods if needed.

If you plan to claim control device credit, identify capture/control device(s) and prepare to demonstrate capture and control efficiencies and monitoring per the subpart (establish whether add-on controls are used and prepare monitoring plans).

candidates.title: National Emission Standards for Hazardous Air Pollutants: Petroleum Refineries—Catalytic Cracking Units, Catalytic Reforming Units, and Sulfur Recovery Units

criteria.criterion: If your catalytic cracking unit regenerator vent does not introduce any other gas streams into the catalyst regeneration vent (i.e., is a complete combustion unit with no additional combustion devices), then you may use the alternative procedure in this subpart to a continuous parameter monitoring system to determine the catalytic regenerator exhaust gas flow rate using the air-flow-and-temperature based equation.

If you have a gas analyzer installed in the catalytic cracking regenerator exhaust vent prior to the addition of air or other gas streams (measuring CO2, CO, and O2), and you have hourly average volumetric air flow to the regenerator from control-room instrumentation or a CPMS, then you may use the alternative gas-composition based procedure in this subpart to calculate Qr (the volumetric flow rate of exhaust gas before adding air or gas streams).

If you elect to demonstrate PM emissions using the coke burn-off procedures (e.g., Option 1b or Option 2) that use Rc (coke burn-off rate) and Qr, then you may use the alternative procedures in §63.1573 (either the air-flow-temperature equation or the gas-analysis equation, as applicable) to calculate Qr for use in the PM per coke burn-off emission rate equations.

If your FCC regenerator vent is subject to the NSPS PM limit and uses a wet scrubber, and you already have NSPS-approved alternative monitoring for the NSPS COMS requirement, and this subpart requires a COMS for the same regenerator vent, then you may request approval under this subpart to use alternative monitoring requirements (submit approved NSPS alternative monitoring plus a monitoring plan).

candidates.title: General Provisions

criteria.criterion: If you intend to use an alternative test method in lieu of the test method specified for a performance test, then you must notify the Administrator at least 60 days before the test, validate the alternative using Method 301 as applicable, and submit the Method 301 validation results with your notification.

If you wish to use an alternative monitoring procedure (minor, intermediate, or major change) instead of a monitoring method specified in a relevant standard, then you must submit an application describing the proposed alternative (addressing the monitoring elements in §63.2 and a performance evaluation test plan if required) and the Administrator will notify you of approval or intended denial within 30 calendar days after receipt (or after supplementary information).

checklist: Confirm the unit is a catalytic cracking unit catalyst regenerator vent covered by Subpart UUU (process vent associated with catalyst regeneration).
Confirm whether the regenerator vent is subject to the NSPS PM requirements (40 CFR part 60, e.g., §60.102) because Option choices and interactions are tied to NSPS applicability.
Decide which compliance option under §63.1564(a)(1) you intend to use (e.g., elect Option 1b or Option 2 that use PM per coke burn-off equations).

Determine whether the regenerator vent introduces any other gas streams (e.g., oxygen-enriched air, nitrogen streams, or other additions); if no other gas streams are introduced, the air-flow-temperature alternative in §63.1573(a)(1) may apply.

If considering the gas-analysis alternative (§63.1573(a)(2)), verify you have a gas analyzer installed in the regenerator exhaust vent upstream of any added gases and upstream of a CO boiler (you may measure upstream or downstream of an ESP but must measure upstream of a CO boiler).

Verify you can obtain and record hourly average volumetric air flow to the regenerator from continuous parameter monitoring or appropriate control room instrumentation (required by §63.1573(a)(1)(i) and (a)(2)(i)).

Verify you can measure and record vent gas temperature near the control device or opacity monitor and vent absolute pressure (Tempgas and Pvent) as required for the air-flow-temperature equation in §63.1573(a)(1)(iii).
Confirm you can measure or calculate coke burn-off rate (Rc) per §63.1564 (Equation 1) and have the data needed to compute PM emission rate using the subpart's equations.

If you will use an alternative test or monitoring method, prepare to submit the required application/validation: for alternative test methods, plan Method 301 validation and 60-day notification (per §63.7(f)); for alternative monitoring procedures, prepare the application addressing monitoring elements and performance evaluation plan (per §63.8(f)).
If your regenerator uses a wet scrubber and you have NSPS-approved alternative monitoring, gather the approved NSPS alternative monitoring documentation to include with any request under §63.1573(g).
Decide whether you will seek Administrator approval or rely on the conditions that allow you to proceed absent prior approval (and confirm timing requirements and notice periods in §§63.7 and 63.8).

Check whether the U.S. EPA or a delegated State/local authority implements/enforces this subpart at your facility and whether any approvals (alternatives) must be requested from EPA or the delegated authority (see delegation provisions).

Those key reasons and conditions are captured."}

candidates.title: National Emission Standards for Hazardous Air Pollutants for Petroleum Refineries (Refinery MACT)

criteria.criterion: If the process units and related emission points are located at a plant site that is a major source and emit one or more hazardous air pollutants, then those petroleum refining process units and related emission points are subject to subpart CC.

If a wastewater stream meets the Group 1 wastewater stream definition (total annual benzene loading ≥ 10 megagrams per year as calculated under 40 CFR 61.342, flow ≥ 0.02 L/min, benzene concentration ≥ 10 ppmw, and not exempt under 40 CFR part 61 subpart FF), then the wastewater provisions of subpart CC apply to that stream.

If a Group 1 wastewater stream is managed in a piece of equipment that is also subject to 40 CFR part 60 subpart QQQ, then after the applicable compliance dates that Group 1 stream managed in that equipment is required to comply only with subpart CC (and not with subpart QQQ).

candidates.title: National Emission Standards for Hazardous Air Pollutants: Chemical Manufacturing Process Units — Wastewater provisions

criteria.criterion: If a wastewater stream is determined or designated a Group 1 wastewater stream under subpart G procedures (including the owner/operator election procedures), then the wastewater treatment and control provisions of subpart G for Group 1 streams apply to that stream.

If a wastewater stream is also subject to 40 CFR part 61 subpart FF, then the owner or operator must either comply with the provisions of both subpart G and part 61 subpart FF or elect the alternative approach specified in subpart G (as described in 63.110(e) / 63.132), per the overlap provisions.

candidates.title: General Provisions

criteria.criterion: If a relevant standard in this part requires performance testing for an affected source, then the owner or operator must perform performance testing in accordance with the requirements of § 63.7.

If a relevant standard requires continuous monitoring systems or other monitoring, then the owner or operator must comply with the monitoring requirements and procedures in § 63.8 for those CMS and monitoring activities.

If a collection of equipment and emission points meets the definition of an affected source under part 63, then the general definitions and duty-to-comply provisions in subpart A (including the definition of affected source) apply to that collection for the purposes of part 63 standards.

candidates.title: Subpart FFFF — Compliance options (as provided)

criteria.criterion: If an equipment, emission stream, or wastewater stream is subject to provisions of more than one subpart of part 63, then the owner/operator may elect the compliance options and must identify the chosen option in the Notification of Compliance Status as provided in § 63.2535.

If a Group 1 or Group 2 wastewater stream is also subject to the provisions of 40 CFR 61.342(c) through (h) and is not exempt under those paragraphs, then the owner/operator may elect to comply only with the Group 1 wastewater stream provisions of subpart FFFF (and must identify that in the Notification of Compliance Status).

checklist: Is the plant site a major source as defined in Clean Air Act section 112(a) (i.e., emits or has the potential to emit ≥ 10 tpy of any HAP or ≥ 25 tpy of combined HAP)? (relevance to 40 CFR 63.640(a))

Does the wastewater stream meet the subpart CC Group 1 criteria: total annual benzene loading ≥ 10 megagrams/year (per 40 CFR 61.342), annual average flow ≥ 0.02 L/min, benzene concentration ≥ 10 ppmw, and not exempt under 40 CFR part 61 subpart FF? (see 40 CFR 63.641)

If the stream is currently Group 2, will you formally designate it a Group 1 stream (owner/operator election), and have you followed subpart G and subpart CC procedures for designation (including managing the stream per §§ 63.133–63.137 from point of determination to designation point)? (see 40 CFR 63.132(e) and 40 CFR 63.144(a)(2))

Where will the stream be conveyed, stored, or treated (identify the exact waste management unit or treatment equipment)? — determine whether that specific equipment is currently subject to NSPS 40 CFR part 60 subpart QQQ (check applicability of QQQ to that equipment and its compliance status).

If the stream will be managed in equipment covered by NSPS subpart QQQ, has the facility passed the applicable compliance dates referenced in subpart CC (i.e., are the overlap rules effective)? (see 40 CFR 63.640(h) and 63.640(o)(1))

Are you planning to control the stream under the Benzene Waste Operations NESHAP (40 CFR part 61 subpart FF)? If so, does that control or any exemption under subpart FF change the Group 1/Group 2 determination (i.e., is the stream exempt under part 61 subpart FF)? (see 40 CFR 63.641 and 40 CFR 63.647(b))

If the stream is managed in equipment subject to both subpart CC and NSPS subpart QQQ, have you documented which subpart you will comply with per the overlap provision (63.640(o)(1)) and prepared the applicable Notification of Compliance Status/recordkeeping to support that election?

Have you prepared or reviewed the procedures and records required to demonstrate Group 1 status (flow-weighted annual concentration calculations, sampling plan, number of samples, flow determinations) according to § 63.144 and § 63.132(c)/(d)?

If you will rely on performance testing or monitoring to demonstrate compliance, have you planned the tests and monitoring in accordance with subpart A general provisions (site-specific test plan, performance test notifications, and CMS performance evaluation requirements in §§ 63.7 and 63.8)?

Have you identified and prepared to submit any required notifications and reports (e.g., Notification of Compliance Status, Periodic Reports) and ensured the Notification will include identification of wastewater streams and management units and any elections (per §§ 63.655(f) and 63.2535)?

judge_text: {"score":2,"reason":"EPA's key point—that a refinery may designate a Group 2 wastewater stream as a Group 1 stream under the Refinery MACT—is reflected in the answer (references to Group 1 definition/designation, owner/operator election procedures in subpart G/CC, and the overlap rule that Group 1 streams managed in units subject to NSPS QQQ must comply with subpart CC). The criteria and checklist capture the essential reasoning and citations noted by EPA."}

candidates.title: National Emission Standards for Hazardous Air Pollutants for Chemical Recovery Combustion Sources

criteria.criterion: If the unit is an existing kraft or soda recovery furnace (or other affected process unit in the chemical recovery system at a kraft or soda pulp mill), then the owner/operator must conduct the initial and periodic performance tests and comply by the Subpart MM compliance date (existing sources: no later than March 13, 2004).

If the owner/operator seeks to demonstrate compliance with the PM emission limits in §63.862(a)(1)(ii)(A) or with the PM limits for recovery furnaces/smelt dissolving tanks/lime kilns, then the PM testing and procedures specified in §63.865(a)(1)-(2) and the test methods/procedures in §63.865(b) must be used.

If a performance test is used to demonstrate compliance or to set monitoring/operating limits, then the performance test must be conducted under representative normal operating conditions (excluding startup, shutdown, and malfunction), the owner/operator must record and retain process information showing representativeness, and make such records available to the Administrator upon request.

candidates.title: General Provisions

criteria.criterion: If a relevant standard requires performance testing, then the owner/operator must perform the required performance tests within 180 days of the compliance date unless an approved waiver or other exception applies.

If construction or reconstruction began between the proposal and promulgation dates and the promulgated standard is more stringent than the proposed standard, then the owner/operator may initially demonstrate compliance using the proposed standard but must conduct a second performance test within 3 years and 180 days after the effective date (or startup) to demonstrate compliance with the promulgated standard.

If the owner/operator intends to rely on a previously conducted performance test in lieu of conducting a new required initial performance test, then that reliance is subject to Administrator review/acceptance, applicable QA/site-specific test plan and reporting requirements, and any waiver provisions in §63.7.

candidates.title: National Emission Standards for Hazardous Air Pollutants: Ore crushing and related units (RRRRR)

criteria.criterion: If an initial performance test for an affected source in this subpart was conducted between October 30, 2003 and no later than 180 days after the compliance date specified for that source, then that test may be used for the initial compliance demonstration provided the test meets the initial performance testing requirements of this subpart.

candidates.title: National Emission Standards for Hazardous Air Pollutants for Reciprocating Internal Combustion Engines (RICE)

criteria.criterion: If a performance test has been previously conducted on a unit and the prior test meets the subpart's conditions (same specified methods followed correctly; test not older than 2 years; test reviewed and accepted by the Administrator; either no process/equipment changes since the test or the owner/operator demonstrates the test still reliably demonstrates compliance despite changes; and for certain units the test was conducted at load within ±10% of 100% load), then the owner/operator is not required to conduct a new initial performance test.

checklist: Confirm the unit type: is the unit an existing kraft or soda recovery furnace (or other Subpart MM 'process unit' such as SDT or lime kiln) at the kraft/soda pulp mill?

Record the applicable Subpart MM compliance date for your source (Subpart MM: existing sources compliance date in §63.863(a) is March 13, 2004) and determine whether the November 2003 test date is before that compliance date.

Verify the exact date(s) of the November 2003 particulate (PM) test(s) and compare to any relevant windows (e.g., between promulgation and compliance date, or the Oct 30, 2003 — 180 days-after window noted in 40 CFR 63.9620 for that subpart).

Confirm which test methods and procedures were used (e.g., Method 5, Method 29, or Method 17 with the specified modification, and oxygen and flow correction methods such as Method 3A/3B) and that sampling times and sample volumes met Subpart MM requirements (sampling time ≥60 minutes and volume ≥0.90 dscm for Methods 5/17/29 per 63.865(b)(1)).

Verify that PM results were corrected to the appropriate oxygen concentration and volumetric flow was corrected per the equations/procedures in §63.865(b)(2) and (4) and that Method 3A/3B (or ANSI/ASME alternative) was used concurrently as required (63.865(b)(3)).

Document that the November 2003 test runs were conducted under representative normal operating conditions (not during startup, shutdown, or malfunction) and retain the process data and explanation demonstrating representativeness as required by §63.865.

Check whether a site-specific test plan was submitted (or the Administrator was notified) per §63.7(b)/(c) at least as required, and whether the Administrator reviewed/accepted the site-specific test plan and/or the test report.

Verify whether the November 2003 test report and raw data were submitted to the Administrator (or permitting authority) within required reporting timelines (see §63.7(g)(1) and Subpart MM reporting provisions).

Determine whether any process, control device, or equipment changes have occurred since November 2003 that could affect the representativeness or validity of the test (Subpart MM §63.864(j)(2) and Subpart A §63.7(h) considerations).

If relying on criteria/precedent from other subparts (e.g., acceptance criteria in 63.6610/63.6612 or 63.6110), verify whether the November 2003 test satisfies those subparts' conditions: same methods, ≤2 years old (where applicable), Administrator review/acceptance, no changes or demonstration of continued representativeness, and load condition requirements (±10% of 100% load when specified).

If relying on tests performed between promulgation and compliance date, determine whether the relevant subpart explicitly allows those tests to be used (e.g., see 40 CFR 63.9620(a)(2) for the Oct 30, 2003 — 180-day allowance) and whether the Subpart MM text or Administrator guidance contains an analogous provision or requires a test within 180 days after the compliance date per 40 CFR 63.7(a)(2).

As needed, prepare to request Administrator acceptance/approval (or a waiver) of the November 2003 test for initial compliance demonstration and assemble QA documentation (site-specific test plan, Method 301 validation if alternative methods were used, performance audit results, chain-of-custody, raw data, and any AASP audit sample results) per §63.7(c) and §63.7(f).

judge_text: {"score":2, "reason":"The EPA's basis (conditional approval of the Nov 2003 tests) is that those tests met Subpart MM/Subpart A requirements — timing (after promulgation/before compliance), required PM test methods/procedures, representative normal operating conditions, QA/site‑specific test plan and Administrator review/acceptance — and those key reasons are reflected in the submitted criteria and checklist."}

candidates.title: Portland Cement Manufacturing (Subpart LLL)

criteria.criterion: If the emissions are from an affected source listed in §63.1345 (each new or existing raw material, clinker, or finished product storage bin; conveying system transfer point; bagging system; bulk loading or unloading system; raw and finish mills; and each existing raw material dryer) then those emissions are subject to a 10 percent opacity limit.

If the emissions are from a kiln or a clinker cooler (the affected sources addressed separately in §63.1343 and §63.1340), then §63.1345 does not itself establish a 10 percent numeric opacity limit for kilns or clinker coolers.

If you are subject to the limitations on opacity under §63.1345 then you must demonstrate compliance by performance testing using Method 9 (per §63.1349(b)(2)) and use the maximum 6-minute average opacity exhibited during the performance test period to determine compliance.

candidates.title: General Provisions (Subpart A)

criteria.criterion: If emissions from two or more affected sources are combined before being released to the atmosphere, then the owner/operator may install an applicable continuous monitoring system (CMS) either on each emission stream or on the combined stream provided the monitoring is sufficient to demonstrate compliance with the relevant standard.

If you choose to use a continuous opacity monitoring system (COMS) to demonstrate opacity compliance, then the COMS must be installed and operated so it completes at least one sampling/analysis cycle every 10 seconds and compliance data must be reduced to 6-minute averages for comparison to the opacity standard.

If a performance test is required to establish compliance or an operating limit, then you must follow the performance testing procedures and schedules in §63.7 (including notification and test-plan provisions) when conducting opacity or other performance tests.

checklist: Confirm whether the facility is subject to Subpart LLL (portland cement plant that is a major source or area source) (40 CFR 63.1340).

List every emission source that feeds the common stack (kiln, clinker cooler, inline raw mill, inline coal mill, alkali bypass, raw mill, finish mill, storage bins, conveying transfer points, bagging/bulk systems).

Determine which of those sources are the specific items enumerated in §63.1345 (raw material/clinker/finished product storage bin; conveying system transfer point; bagging system; bulk loading/unloading system; raw and finish mills; existing raw material dryer) — if any of those are present in the commingled stream the 10% opacity limit may apply to those emissions.

Verify whether the clinker cooler itself is being treated as a source listed in §63.1345 (note: §63.1340 lists clinker coolers as affected sources but §63.1345's 10% opacity list does not explicitly include clinker coolers).

Document the fraction of clinker cooler exhaust that bypasses the inline kiln/raw mill (you stated an average of 20%); keep the measurement basis and period for that 20% and any flow rates used to characterize commingling.

Identify whether any kiln bypasses, coal mills, or other separate stacks are part of the commingled configuration (these affect how emissions are apportioned and how testing/monitoring is done under §63.1343 and §63.1349).
Decide whether you will monitor the combined stack or install monitoring on individual streams; ensure the monitoring approach is sufficient to demonstrate compliance per §63.8(b)(2).

If relying on monthly visible emissions (Method 22) and follow-up Method 9 testing per Subpart LLL opacity monitoring (§63.1350(f)), confirm test frequency, the procedures to follow when visible emissions are observed, and whether a COMS is installed as an alternative.

If subject to §63.1345 opacity limits, plan Method 9 performance tests and use the maximum 6-minute average to evaluate compliance per §63.1349(b)(2) and §63.1348(b)(2); prepare and (if requested) submit site-specific test plan and notifications per §63.7.

If using a COMS to demonstrate opacity compliance at the combined stack, verify COMS performance and QA operation (sampling cycle, drift checks, performance evaluation) consistent with Subpart A requirements (§63.8) and include COMS location to be representative of the control device outlet or combined effluent.

Review title V and permitting obligations (§63.1340(d)) to ensure federally enforceable permit terms reflect which emissions points and limits (including opacity) apply to the common stack configuration.

judge_text: {"score":1,"reason":"The EPA note’s key rationale — that the more stringent opacity limit must be applied when streams are commingled — is not explicitly stated in OUR ANSWER. The answer does identify which sources are in §63.1345, notes kilns/clinker are treated separately, and describes monitoring options for combined streams (§63.8), so some relevant elements are present. However it fails to include a clear criterion or citation saying that, where multiple standards could apply to a common stack, the more stringent opacity limit governs (the core point in the EPA Notes)."}

candidates.title: Surface Coating of Miscellaneous Metal Parts and Products

criteria.criterion: If you perform surface coating of miscellaneous metal parts and products and your facility uses 946 liters (250 gal) per year or more of coatings that contain HAP and is a major source or part of a major source, then the affected source is subject to Subpart MMMM.

If the coating contains heat-activated polymer systems that, when applied to metal substrates, dry to a non-tacky surface and react chemically with the rubber and metal during a vulcanization process, then the coating operation is in the rubber-to-metal coatings subcategory of Subpart MMMM.
If a coating operation does not meet the definition of rubber-to-metal coatings in §63.3981, then the operation is in the general use coating subcategory of Subpart MMMM.

If the facility uses only coatings, thinners and other additives, and cleaning materials that contain no organic HAP as determined according to §63.3941(a), then the coating operation is not subject to Subpart MMMM.

candidates.title: Surface Coating of Plastic Parts and Products

criteria.criterion: If you perform surface coating of plastic parts and products and your facility uses 378 liters (100 gal) per year or more of coatings that contain HAP and is a major source or part of a major source, then the affected source is subject to Subpart PPPP.
If the coating operation is not an automotive lamp, TPO, or assembled on-road vehicle coating operation, then it is part of the general use coating subcategory of Subpart PPPP.

If the facility uses only coatings, thinners and other additives, and cleaning materials that contain no organic HAP as determined according to §63.4541 (or the subpart's applicable test/method), then the coating operation is not subject to Subpart PPPP.

candidates.title: General Provisions

criteria.criterion: If a source is subject to a relevant standard under part 63 (for example Subpart MMMM or Subpart PPPP), then the General Provisions in Subpart A apply to that source.

If a relevant standard requires performance testing or monitoring, then the owner or operator must comply with the performance testing requirements in §63.7 and the monitoring requirements in §63.8 of Subpart A.

checklist: Is the substrate you coat metal (miscellaneous metal parts/products) or plastic parts/products?
Obtain manufacturer formulation data for the coating: does the coating contain a heat-activated polymer system?
Does the applied coating dry to a non-tacky surface and, during your heating/bonding step, chemically react with rubber and metal in a vulcanization process (i.e., is rubber vulcanization occurring)?
Describe the heating/bonding process in detail and confirm whether it involves vulcanization of rubber or only a heat-bond/curing step that does not vulcanize rubber.
How many liters (or gallons) per year of coatings that contain organic HAP does the facility use for the operation (compare to 946 L/yr for MMMM and 378 L/yr for PPPP)?
Is the facility a major source of HAP (potential to emit ≥ 10 tpy of any single HAP or ≥ 25 tpy combined HAP)?
Do the coatings, thinners, additives, and cleaning materials qualify as non-HAP (i.e., contain no organic HAP per the subpart's non-HAP definition)?
If you have multiple coating activities, quantify solids used (liters or kg of solids) to determine predominant activity or to calculate a facility-specific emission limit per the subpart procedures.
Check current permits/title V status to see whether Subpart A testing/monitoring and notification/reporting (performance tests, CMS, notifications) will be required.

judge_text: {"score":2,"reason":"Yes. The answer includes the specific criterion requiring the coating to chemically react with rubber and metal during a vulcanization process (§63.3981) and checklist items asking whether the heating/bonding step involves vulcanization vs. non‑vulcanizing heat‑bonding, which capture the EPA’s key reason that the bonding was not performed during vulcanization."}

candidates.title: Wool fiberglass manufacturing (Subpart NNN)

criteria.criterion: If the owner or operator of a wool fiberglass manufacturing facility is a major source or is located at a facility that is a major source, then the requirements of Subpart NNN apply to that facility.
If a new or existing glass-melting furnace is located at a wool fiberglass manufacturing facility, then emissions from that furnace are subject to this subpart.

If a new or existing rotary spin wool fiberglass manufacturing line is producing a bonded wool fiberglass building insulation product, then emissions from that rotary spin line are subject to this subpart.
If a new or existing flame attenuation wool fiberglass manufacturing line is producing a bonded product, then emissions from that flame attenuation line are subject to this subpart.
If the owner or operator demonstrates to the Administrator that the wool fiberglass manufacturing facility is not a major source, then the requirements of this subpart do not apply to that facility.

If a bonded wool fiberglass product has a loss on ignition (LOI) of less than 8 percent and a density of less than 32 kilograms per cubic meter, then the product meets this subpart's definition of 'building insulation'.

candidates.title: General Provisions (Subpart A)

criteria.criterion: If a relevant standard (for example Subpart NNN) requires performance testing, then the owner or operator must conduct performance tests in accordance with §63.7.
If a relevant standard requires monitoring (including continuous monitoring systems), then the monitoring installation, operation, maintenance, and data handling requirements of §63.8 apply.

If a facility emits or has the potential to emit, considering controls, 10 tons per year or more of any single HAP or 25 tons per year or more of combined HAPs, then it meets the part 63 definition of a 'major source' used to determine applicability of part 63 standards.

checklist: Measure the product loss on ignition (LOI) using the method in Appendix A to Subpart NNN and confirm whether LOI < 8%.
Measure product density using the method in Appendix C to Subpart NNN and confirm whether density < 32 kg/m^3.
Confirm the product is 'bonded wool fiberglass' (i.e., wool fiberglass with a phenol-formaldehyde binder applied).
Identify the manufacturing process for this product: rotary spin or flame attenuation (and which manufacturing line produced it).
If produced on a rotary spin line, confirm that the line is producing the bonded building insulation product in question at the times of concern.
Determine whether the facility has any glass-melting furnace(s) on site.

Calculate the facility's potential to emit (and actual emissions) of each hazardous air pollutant and combined HAPs to determine whether the facility is a major source (≥10 tpy single HAP or ≥25 tpy combined HAPs).
If relying on the 'not a major source' demonstration, confirm documentation and basis that would be provided to the Administrator to show the facility is not a major source.

If applicable, determine whether the product or line is classified under special line categories (e.g., aerospace, HVAC, OEM, pipe, heavy-density) per Subpart NNN definitions (for lines where 75% or more of annual operating hours produce those product types).

judge_text: {"score":2,"reason":"The EPA note’s sole key reason—that the metal building insulation production “meets the definition of building insulation” under Subpart NNN—is reflected in the answer: the criteria include the Subpart NNN definition elements (bonded wool fiberglass with LOI <8% and density <32 kg/m3) and the applicability linkage to Subpart NNN. Other supporting applicability criteria (major source, line type, bonded product) are also included."}

candidates.title: Polyether polyol manufacturing NESHAP (Subpart PPP)

criteria.criterion: If a process unit manufactures a polyether polyol as its primary product and is located at a plant site that is a major source, then that process unit is a polyether polyol manufacturing process unit (PMPU) and the PMPU and its associated equipment are part of an affected source subject to this subpart.

If a PMPU does not use or manufacture any organic HAP during the production of one or more products, then that PMPU is not subject to any provisions of this subpart except that the owner/operator must retain documentation of that determination and demonstrate it when requested by the Administrator.

If tetrahydrofuran (THF) is used to produce one or more polyether polyol products at a PMPU that is part of an affected source, then process vents for that PMPU must comply with the HON process vent requirements in §§ 63.113 through 63.118 as modified by § 63.1425(f).

If epoxides are used in the production of polyether polyols at an affected source, then the process vent control requirements for epoxide emissions in § 63.1425(b) (and related provisions such as § 63.1425(g) for ethylene oxide service) apply to those process vents.

candidates.title: Miscellaneous organic chemical manufacturing (Subpart FFFF)

criteria.criterion: If you own or operate a miscellaneous organic chemical manufacturing process unit (MCPU) located at or part of a major source and the MCPU (1) produces materials described in the cited NAICS/SIC scopes, (2) processes, uses, or generates organic HAP listed in section 112(b) of the CAA (or hydrogen halide/halogen HAP), and (3) is not an affected source or part of an affected source under another subpart of part 63, then the MCPU is subject to subpart FFFF.
If the equipment or process unit is an affected source or part of an affected source under another subpart of part 63, then subpart FFFF does not apply to that equipment or process unit.

candidates.title: General Provisions (Subpart A)

criteria.criterion: If a relevant standard requires performance testing, then the owner or operator must perform the performance tests in accordance with § 63.7 within the timeframes specified (generally within 180 days of the compliance date unless otherwise provided).

If a relevant standard requires a continuous monitoring system (CMS) or other monitoring, then the monitoring provisions of § 63.8 apply and the owner/operator must conduct monitoring as set forth in that section and the relevant standard.

If the plant site qualifies as a 'major source' under the definition in § 63.2 (10 tpy of any single HAP or 25 tpy of combined HAP), then that status is a necessary factor in determining whether PMPUs at the site are part of an affected source under Subpart PPP.

checklist: Confirm whether the plant site is a major source (calculate potential to emit in tpy for each HAP and combined HAP against the 10/25 tpy thresholds).
Determine the primary product of the process unit (is the primary product a polyether polyol per § 63.1420(e) rules for primary product determination?).
Verify whether tetrahydrofuran (THF) is intentionally used (not just impurity) in the PMPU for making polyether polyols.

Determine whether any organic HAP (as defined for this subpart, i.e., compounds listed in table 4 of Subpart PPP) are used or manufactured in the PMPU (including whether THF is listed as an organic HAP for this subpart).

If no organic HAP are used or manufactured during the production step in question, compile and retain documentation (purchase records, stream analyses, engineering calc, process knowledge) supporting that determination as required by § 63.1420(b)(1)(i).
Determine whether epoxides (e.g., ethylene oxide, propylene oxide, etc.) are used anywhere in the process unit or associated unit operations.
Inventory unit operations and identify any process vents, storage vessels, wastewater streams, equipment leaks, or heat exchangers associated with the PMPU.
If THF is used, identify process vents from the PMPU and assess what HON process vent provisions (63.113–63.118 as modified by § 63.1425(f)) would be triggered for those vents.

If any process vents or control devices are used to comply with Subpart PPP, calculate or estimate uncontrolled and controlled HAP emission rates per § 63.1426 procedures to determine group status and whether percent-reduction, outlet concentration, flare, or emission factor options apply.

Determine whether the unit/process meets the Subpart FFFF MCPU criteria (NAICS/SIC scope and whether the process uses/generates organic HAP) and whether the unit is already subject to another Part 63 subpart.

If subject to testing/monitoring per any applicable standard, identify required performance tests and monitoring systems and note the timing and notification requirements under §§ 63.7 and 63.8 (e.g., 60-day notice for tests, 180-day testing deadlines).
If you intend to rely on the 'PMPU without organic HAP' exemption, be prepared to demonstrate it upon request and retain the supporting records on-site as required.

If using Extended Cookout (ECO) as a control technique (or planning to), identify product classes/pressure decay curves and gather data required by § 63.1427 (reactor liquid epoxide concentration, reactor vapor samples, ECO timing/parameters).

judge_text: {"score":1,"reason":"The answer captures the 63.1420(b)(1) no‑HAP demonstration/recordkeeping requirement (and the need to compile supporting documentation) so EPA’s concern about lack of information is reflected, and it includes epoxide‑specific control citations. However it does not explicitly capture the critical point in the EPA notes that the 63.1420(d)(3) exemption is limited to epoxide polymerization and therefore does not cover THF polymerization; that explicit limitation is missing."}

candidates.title: National Emission Standards for Hazardous Air Pollutants for Paper and Other Web Coating

criteria.criterion: If the facility is a major source of HAP and operates web coating lines, then the provisions of Subpart JJJJ apply to the facility.

If a process meets the definition of a web coating line (a number of work stations applying a continuous layer of liquid or semi-liquid coating across a web between an unwind/feed station and a rewind/cutting station), then that process is included in the affected source for this subpart.

If a web coating line falls into one of the categories listed in § 63.3300(a)–(g) (for example, stand-alone equipment or certain presses covered under subpart KK, web coating subject to subpart EE, subpart SSSS, subpart OOOO, or is research/laboratory equipment), then that web coating line is not part of the affected source under Subpart JJJJ.

If a web coating line coats both paper (or another web) and a different substrate, then the subpart that applies is determined by the predominant activity test (90 percent or more of the mass of substrate coated during the compliance period), and Subpart JJJJ applies when paper/web is the predominant substrate.

If all subject web coating lines at the facility utilize non-HAP coatings meeting the thresholds in § 63.3370(s) and you submit the one-time report required by § 63.3370(s), then you can become exempt from the reporting requirements of this subpart (per § 63.3300(j)).

If a web coating line is modified to include printing activities but the owner/operator elects to continue demonstrating compliance with this subpart (including the 5 percent monthly mass threshold for materials applied to print stations), then the line may remain subject to Subpart JJJJ in lieu of Subpart KK under the conditions in § 63.3300(i).

candidates.title: General Provisions (definitions and monitoring/performance testing requirements)

criteria.criterion: If the facility emits or has the potential to emit ≥10 tons per year of any single HAP or ≥25 tons per year of any combination of HAP, then the facility meets the definition of a 'major source' in § 63.2 for applicability of Part 63 standards.

If the facility is not a major source (i.e., an area source under § 63.2), then the applicability criterion in § 63.3290 for Subpart JJJJ (which applies to major sources with web coating lines) would not be met.

If performance testing or monitoring is required by the relevant subpart, then the owner/operator must follow the performance test notification, quality assurance, testing, and monitoring procedures and timelines in §§ 63.7 and 63.8.

checklist: Calculate the facility's actual and potential annual HAP emissions (tons/year) by HAP and in total to determine whether the facility is a 'major source' (≥10 tpy single HAP or ≥25 tpy combined HAP).

Identify each process line and confirm whether it meets the 'web coating line' definition (continuous application of liquid or semi-liquid coatings across a web between an unwind/feed and a rewind/cutting station).

List all coating materials used (including adhesives/glues, hot melts, primers, solvents) and obtain as-purchased formulation data or Method 311/24 results to determine organic HAP content, VOC, and coating solids.

Determine whether any web coating line is already regulated under or included in another Part 63 subpart listed in § 63.3300(a)–(g) (e.g., subpart KK, EE, SSSS, OOOO) or qualifies as research/laboratory equipment.

For any lines that coat multiple substrates, quantify the mass of each substrate coated over a representative period (≥1 year or at least a period expected to represent future operation) to apply the 90% predominant-activity test.

If claiming non-HAP coating status, verify each coating meets the thresholds in § 63.3370(s) (≤0.1% by mass for OSHA-defined carcinogens and ≤1.0% by mass for other organic HAP) and prepare the one-time report to the permitting authority per § 63.3370(s).

If planning to demonstrate compliance using control devices, identify control type (solvent recovery, oxidizer, other) and be prepared to meet the monitoring and testing requirements in §§ 63.3350 and 63.3360 (CEMS/CPMS, performance tests, capture efficiency, operating limits).

If printing stations are present or will be added, determine the monthly mass of materials applied to print stations and compare to the 5% threshold in § 63.3300(i) to decide whether to elect Subpart JJJJ or Subpart KK compliance.

Document whether any work stations are never-controlled, intermittently-controlled, or always-controlled (as defined in § 63.3310) because compliance demonstration procedures differ for these configurations.

Assemble records and be ready to follow §§ 63.7 and 63.8 for performance test notifications, site-specific test plans, audit/sample requirements, and CMS/CPMS quality assurance if testing/monitoring will be used for compliance.

judge_text: {"score":2,"reason":"EPA's note hinges on applicability when the activity occurs at a major HAP source; OUR ANSWER includes the major‑source thresholds (≥10 tpy single/≥25 tpy combined) and the Subpart JJJJ applicability tied to web coating lines and the web‑coating definition, so the key reasons are captured."}

candidates.title: Wood Furniture Manufacturing NESHAP

criteria.criterion: If the facility is engaged, either in part or in whole, in the manufacture of wood furniture or wood furniture components and is located at a plant site that is a major source, then the affected source is subject to subpart JJ.

If the owner or operator meets the definition of an incidental wood furniture manufacturer (primarily engaged in manufacture of products other than wood furniture and uses no more than 100 gallons per month of finishing material or adhesives for wood furniture), then the source is not subject to subpart JJ.

If the source meets any of the area-source limits/criteria in § 63.800(b) (for example, uses no more than 250 gallons per month for every month as specified in paragraph (b)(1), or no more than 3,000 gallons per rolling 12-month period as specified in paragraph (b)(2), or emits no more than 4.5 Mg of any one HAP and no more than 11.4 Mg of combined HAP and at least 90 percent of plantwide emissions are from wood furniture as specified in paragraph (b)(3)), then the source is an area source and is not subject to other provisions of subpart JJ.

If the surface coating activity is surface coating of metal parts and products other than metal components of wood furniture that meets the applicability criteria for subpart MMMM (miscellaneous metal parts and products), then that surface coating activity is not subject to subpart JJ.

If the surface coating activity is surface coating of metal furniture (or other categories listed in § 63.800(d)(4)) that meets the applicability criteria for subpart RRRR, then that surface coating activity is not subject to subpart JJ (except that surface coating of metal components of wood furniture performed at a wood furniture facility remain subject to JJ).
If the owner or operator is an affected source under subpart JJ, then the owner or operator must also comply with the General Provisions in subpart A as identified in this subpart.

candidates.title: Metal Furniture Surface Coating NESHAP

criteria.criterion: If you perform surface coating of metal furniture (as defined) and you own or operate an affected source that is a new, reconstructed, or existing affected source and that is a major source, is located at a major source, or is part of a major source, then you are subject to subpart RRRR.

If the surface coating is of metal components of wood furniture and that operation is subject to the wood furniture manufacturing NESHAP (subpart JJ), then the surface coating operation is not subject to subpart RRRR.
If the surface coating conducted at the affected source uses only coatings, thinners, and cleaning materials that contain no organic HAP, then the source is not subject to subpart RRRR.

If the surface coating is limited to repair or maintenance of metal furniture used by a major source and not for commerce (and the organic HAP emissions are below the major source thresholds), then that coating is not subject to subpart RRRR.

candidates.title: Surface Coating of Miscellaneous Metal Parts and Products NESHAP

criteria.criterion: If you perform surface coating of miscellaneous metal parts and products (as defined) and you use 946 liters (250 gallons) per year or more of coatings that contain HAP in that surface coating and you are a major source, are located at a major source, or are part of a major source, then you are subject to subpart MMMM.

If the surface coating operations occur at research or laboratory facilities, are part of janitorial/facility maintenance, or are hobby/noncommercial, then those operations are not subject to subpart MMMM.

If individual coatings are used in volumes of less than 189 liters (50 gallons) per year and the total volume of coatings exempt under that provision does not exceed 946 liters (250 gallons) per year at the facility, then those coatings may be exempt from subpart MMMM.

If the surface coating is of metal components of wood furniture that meet the applicability criteria for wood furniture manufacturing (subpart JJ), then that surface coating is not subject to subpart MMMM.

candidates.title: General Provisions (Subpart A)

criteria.criterion: If a source is an affected source subject to a subpart standard, then the General Provisions in subpart A apply to that source as specified by the relevant subpart.

If the owner or operator is required by a relevant standard to perform performance testing, then the owner or operator must conduct performance tests and meet the performance testing requirements and deadlines in § 63.7.
If the relevant standard requires continuous monitoring systems or other monitoring, then the monitoring requirements and procedures in § 63.8 apply.

If the plant meets the definition of a major source (emits or has the potential to emit 10 tons per year or more of any single HAP or 25 tons per year or more of any combination of HAP), then it is a major source for part 63 purposes.

checklist: Determine whether the plant site meets the part 63 major source definition (≥10 tpy single HAP or ≥25 tpy combined HAP) (40 CFR 63.2).
Confirm whether the facility performs manufacture of wood furniture or wood furniture components (activity-based determination for subpart JJ) (40 CFR 63.800(a), 63.801).

Determine whether the metal parts you coat/refinish are metal components of wood furniture (i.e., parts used in the manufacture of wood furniture) or are separate miscellaneous metal parts/equipment (affects JJ vs MMMM/RRRR applicability) (40 CFR 63.800(d)(4), 63.3881(c)(6), 63.4881(c)(2)).

Measure/record volumes of all coatings, thinners, cleaning, gluing, and washoff materials used plantwide (include non-wood activities) by month and rolling 12-month periods to check: ≤250 gal/month every month (63.800(b)(1)); ≤3,000 gal per rolling 12 months (63.800(b)(2)); and ≥946 L (250 gal)/year HAP-containing coatings for miscellaneous metal parts (63.3881(b)).
Verify whether metal-coating/refinishing coatings used contain organic HAP (if coatings contain no organic HAP the activity may be excluded) (63.4881(c)(1), 63.3881(c)(1)).

Calculate plantwide HAP emissions (rolling 12 months) to check whether single-HAP ≤4.5 Mg (5 tons) and combined ≤11.4 Mg (12.5 tons) and that ≥90% of emissions are from wood furniture to evaluate subpart JJ area-source criterion (63.800(b)(3)).
Check whether metal coating activities are solely facility maintenance/repair not for commerce (possible exclusion under RRRR/MMMM) (40 CFR 63.4881(c)(5), 63.3881(c)(2)).

If claiming incidental wood furniture manufacturer status, keep purchase/usage records demonstrating ≤100 gallons per month of finishing material/adhesives used for wood furniture (63.800(a); 63.801 definition) and retain records as specified.

Maintain monthly records of gallons used (coating, gluing, cleaning, washoff) and retain for five years if relying on the 250 gal/month or 3,000 gal/rolling-12-month area-source criteria (63.800(b)(1),(b)(2)).

If multiple surface-coating NESHAPs could apply, determine whether one activity constitutes ≥90% of coating activity or whether to comply with each NESHAP separately or use a facility-specific limit as allowed under MMMM (if relevant) and document the basis (63.3881(e)).

If subject to a subpart, identify performance testing and monitoring obligations under subpart A and the relevant subpart, and prepare to meet performance test/monitoring deadlines and recordkeeping requirements (40 CFR 63.7, 63.8, and the relevant subpart provisions).

candidates.title: National Emission Standards for Hazardous Air Pollutants for Printing, Coating, and Dyeing of Fabrics and Other Textiles

criteria.criterion: if you own or operate an affected source that performs printing, coating, slashing, dyeing, or finishing of fabric or other textiles and the affected source is a major source, is located at a major source, or is part of a major source, then subject

if your coating, printing, slashing, dyeing, or finishing operations meet any of the criteria in paragraphs (c)(1) through (5) of §63.4281 (for example, use only regulated materials that contain no organic HAP, are research/laboratory/janitorial operations, are noncommercial, are conducted at ambient temperatures without drying/curing equipment, or are performed on-site by the U.S. Armed Forces), then not subject

if a web coating line at your facility is part of an affected source under another NESHAP (e.g., subpart JJJJ, subpart XXXX, synthetic fiber manufacturing where fibers are final product, or subpart KK for flexible packaging) as listed in §63.4281(d)(1)–(4), then that web coating line is not part of the affected source of this subpart

if your operations fall into the web coating/printing, slashing, or dyeing/finishing subcategory, then the affected source consists of the collection of equipment, containers, conveyance systems, waste storage/conveying equipment, and wastewater conveyance/treatment devices listed for that subcategory in §63.4282

candidates.title: General Provisions (applicability, performance testing, and monitoring requirements)

criteria.criterion: if you are subject to a relevant standard under part 63 (for example, a subpart such as OOOO), then Subpart A provisions apply to you as part of the relevant standard

if a relevant standard requires performance testing, then you must perform the required performance tests within the timeframes and subject to the notification, QA, and conduct requirements in §63.7 unless a waiver or extension applies
if a relevant standard requires use of a continuous monitoring system (CMS) or other monitoring, then you must follow the monitoring design, operation, QA/QC, and reporting provisions in §63.8

checklist: Determine whether the shoelace tipping operation is considered 'coating', 'printing', 'finishing', 'slashing', or 'dyeing' under the definitions in 40 CFR 63.4371 (e.g., does the application form a continuous solid film, impregnate fibers, or apply color/pattern).
Verify whether the substrate you process (shoelaces/thread) falls within the regulatory definitions of 'fabric' or 'textile' (note: 'fabric' definition in §63.4371 includes thread).
Confirm whether the affected source (the collection of equipment/activities) is a major source of HAP (potential to emit ≥10 tpy single HAP or ≥25 tpy combined HAP) per 40 CFR part 63 definitions.

Determine the composition of the methanol solution and any other regulated materials (coating/printing/thinning/cleaning/slashing/dyeing/finishing materials) and whether they contain organic HAP (e.g., methanol or other organics) at the mass fractions used to decide applicability or exemptions.

Establish whether the tipping operation involves drying/curing equipment (ovens, dryers, tenter frames, steam cans) or occurs at ambient temperature without such equipment (ambient-temperature operations may be excluded per §63.4281(c)(4)).
Confirm whether the operations are solely research/laboratory, janitorial/maintenance, or noncommercial (internal use) activities that meet the exemptions in §63.4281(c)(2)–(3).

If your web coating/printing line also coats other substrates (paper, tire cord, etc.), determine the predominant activity (mass of substrate coated) to identify which subpart governs per §63.4281(e).

Identify whether any portion of the affected source includes storage, mixing, conveyance, waste handling, or wastewater treatment equipment for the coating/printing/slashing/dyeing/finishing activities as described in §63.4282.

If subject to Subpart OOOO, determine which compliance option you would use (compliant material, emission rate with/without add‑on controls, organic HAP overall control efficiency, or equivalent emission rate for dyeing/finishing) and whether you will need capture/control systems or monitoring per §§63.4291–63.4341.
If subject to any relevant standard, confirm performance testing and monitoring obligations and scheduling (notifications, site-specific test/QA plans, CMS requirements) under §§63.7 and 63.8.

candidates.title: National Emission Standards for Halogenated Solvent Cleaning (Subpart T)

criteria.criterion: If a device is a batch vapor, in-line vapor, in-line cold, or batch cold solvent cleaning machine that uses any of the listed halogenated HAP solvents (methylene chloride, perchloroethylene, trichloroethylene, 1,1,1-trichloroethane, carbon tetrachloride, or chloroform) in a total concentration greater than 5 percent by weight as a cleaning and/or drying agent, then the machine is subject to Subpart T.
If the cleaning activity is wipe cleaning (for example, use of a rag containing halogenated solvent or a spray cleaner containing halogenated solvent), then that activity is not covered by Subpart T.

If the cleaning machine does not have a solvent/air interface, then the machine falls under the 'without a solvent/air interface' provisions (including the alternative standards in §63.464(a)(2) for batch vapor machines without a solvent/air interface) and cleaning capacity must be determined as specified in the rule.

If the unit is a continuous web cleaning machine, then Subpart T applies but the machine may be subject to the separate continuous-web provisions and alternative standard (e.g., §63.464(d)) and the different compliance timing in §63.460(g).

If the cleaning machines at the plant constitute an 'affected facility' as defined in §63.471(a) (i.e., the collection of solvent cleaning machines at a major source or certain combinations at an area source), then the facility-wide emission limits and monthly/annual calculation procedures in §63.471 apply.

If you elect to use the alternative standards in §63.464 for a batch vapor or in-line solvent cleaning machine, then you must follow the logkeeping and emissions-calculation or cleaning-capacity-based limits specified in §63.464.

candidates.title: General Provisions (Subpart A)

criteria.criterion: If you are an owner or operator of a solvent cleaning machine meeting the applicability criteria of §63.460(a), then the General Provisions of Subpart A apply to you except as noted for Subpart T (see appendix C to Subpart T).

If a relevant standard (including Subpart T) requires performance testing, then the performance testing requirements in §63.7 apply (including notification, site-specific test plan, QA, timing, and reporting obligations).
If a relevant standard (including Subpart T) requires monitoring, then the monitoring conduct, QA, operation, and recordkeeping provisions of §63.8 apply to the required CMS or monitoring activities.

If you are determining applicability or interpreting terms used in Subpart T, then the definitions and terms in §63.2 (and other applicable Subpart A definitions) apply unless Subpart T defines a term differently.

checklist: Identify the solvent(s) used in each degreaser and confirm whether any listed halogenated HAP (methylene chloride, PCE, TCE, 1,1,1-TCA, carbon tetrachloride, chloroform) are present at >5% by weight (use MSDS, Method 18, or engineering calculations).
Determine the machine type for each unit: batch vapor, batch cold (immersion or remote reservoir), in-line vapor, in-line cold, continuous web, or other (use definitions in 40 CFR 63.461).

Establish whether each machine has a solvent/air interface (for vapor machines the midline of the primary condenser; for cold machines the liquid surface) or whether the unit is effectively 'without a solvent/air interface'.
If a machine lacks a solvent/air interface, measure/calculate the cleaning capacity (internal volume) per §63.461 and §63.464 procedures.
Record whether cleaning is performed by wiping or spray (if wipe cleaning, Subpart T may not apply).
If subject to Subpart T, determine whether you will comply under §63.463 design/operational requirements or elect the alternative standards in §63.464 (and which option within §63.464).

For units potentially subject to §63.463 controls, inventory existing control features (covers, freeboard ratio, freeboard refrigeration/chiller, primary condenser, carbon adsorber, dwell capability, superheated vapor/part technology, automated handling/hoist speeds) and measure freeboard ratio and solvent/air interface area as defined in §63.461 and §63.463.
If claiming 'no solvent/air interface', document how the solvent/air interface is absent and preserve records used to calculate cleaning capacity (for enforcement or equivalency requests).

Determine facility status: whether the facility is a major source or area source for HAPs and whether the collection of cleaning machines meets the 'affected facility' definition in §63.471(a) so facility-wide limits may apply.
Maintain solvent addition/deletion logs and monthly solvent-consumption records as required for §63.464, §63.471, and recordkeeping/reporting provisions in Subpart T and Subpart A.

If performance testing, monitoring, or CMS will be used, prepare to follow Subpart A §§63.7 and 63.8 procedures (notify Administrator, prepare site-specific test/QA plans, perform required QA and monitoring, and retain records).

If planning to rely on equivalency or alternative control/monitoring methods, document and prepare the demonstration or request to the Administrator per the equivalency/evaluation procedures in Subpart T (e.g., §63.464, §63.469 where referenced).
