candidates.title: Pulp and Paper (kraft/soda) — monitoring for recovery furnaces, lime kilns, and smelt dissolving tanks

criteria.criterion: If you operate a kraft or soda smelt dissolving tank equipped with a wet scrubber that is an affected source under Subpart MM, then you must install, calibrate, maintain, and operate a CPMS to determine and record the pressure drop across the scrubber and the scrubbing liquid flow rate at least once every 15 minutes and establish operating limits during the initial or periodic performance test.

If you want to set or revise a minimum scrubber pressure drop operating limit under Subpart MM, then you must base the operating limit on values recorded during the initial or periodic performance test or on values recorded during previous performance tests (or conduct additional performance tests), provided the data were obtained using the test methods and procedures required in this subpart and you certify that control techniques/processes were not modified since testing.

If the smelt dissolving tank uses a dynamic wet scrubber that operates at ambient pressure or is a low-energy entrainment scrubber where fan speed does not vary, then as an alternative to pressure-drop monitoring you may use fan amperage or fan RPM monitoring and set the minimum operating limit using the methods specified for fan amperage, percent full load amperage, or RPM.

If you monitor pressure drop with a CPMS under Subpart MM, then the pressure-drop monitoring device must be certified by the manufacturer to be accurate to within ±500 pascals (±2 inches water gauge pressure).

candidates.title: General Provisions (performance testing and monitoring procedures)

criteria.criterion: If a relevant subpart requires a performance test to establish operating limits, then you must perform the performance test within 180 days of the compliance date (unless a waiver or Administrator-approved extension applies).

If you propose to use an alternative test method or an alternative monitoring procedure to establish or revise operating limits, then you must notify the Administrator and validate/seek approval following the procedures in §63.7(f) (alternative test methods) and §63.8(f) (alternative monitoring methods) before relying on those alternative methods for compliance determinations.

If you wish to waive a required performance test, then you must apply for and obtain a waiver from the Administrator under §63.7(h) before the test deadline in order to be relieved of the testing requirement.

candidates.title: Wet-scrubber operating limits and CPMS requirements (operating limits established by performance tests)

criteria.criterion: If a wet scrubber is used to meet particulate matter, PM10, chlorine, hydrochloric acid, or dioxins/furans emission limits under Subpart TTTTT, then you must maintain the hourly average pressure drop and scrubber liquid flow rate at or above the minimum level established during the initial or subsequent performance test.

If your wet scrubber is subject to Subpart TTTTT operating limits for pressure drop and scrubber water flow rate, then you must use the CPMS during each run of the particulate matter performance test to measure and record pressure drop and water flow at least every 15 minutes and set site-specific operating limits as the lowest average individual pressure drop and scrubber water flow rate among the compliant test runs.

candidates.title: Procedures to change compliance levels of monitored parameters (require notification and performance tests)

criteria.criterion: If you want to change control device or process operating parameter levels established during performance tests under Subpart DDD, then you must notify the Administrator of the request and, upon approval, conduct additional performance tests at the proposed new operating parameter levels to verify that emissions still meet the applicable emission limits before operating at the new levels.

checklist: Is the unit a kraft or soda smelt dissolving tank that is an 'affected source' under Subpart MM (i.e., subject to Subpart MM compliance obligations)?
Is the control device a wet scrubber (dynamic wet scrubber or low-energy entrainment scrubber) or another type of scrubber?
Does the scrubber operate at ambient pressure or qualify as a low-energy entrainment scrubber where fan speed does not vary (to determine if fan-amperage/RPM alternative applies)?
Was an initial or prior performance test (three runs) conducted that measured pressure drop and scrubber liquid flow using the CPMS, and are those certified test records available?
Have any control techniques, scrubber hardware, or process conditions been modified since the last performance test (you must certify no modifications if relying on prior test data)?
Is a CPMS installed that measures pressure drop with manufacturer-certified accuracy ±500 pascals (±2 inches water gauge) and records at required intervals (at least every 15 minutes)?

Do you have or intend to submit a written notification/request to the Administrator for conducting a new performance test or for approval to use alternative monitoring or alternative test methods (60 days or as required)?
Have you reviewed whether your facility is subject to Subpart TTTTT, Subpart DDD, or other subparts (in addition to Subpart MM) that contain scrubber operating-limit establishment/change procedures?

If you plan to lower the pressure-drop limit without a new performance test, have you confirmed eligibility for any Administrator-approved waiver or an alternative monitoring approach and obtained written approval?

judge_text: {"score":2,"reason":"EPA's note: 63.864(j) allows revised parameter ranges only if a performance test is conducted at the new limit. OUR ANSWER includes the MM criterion requiring revised limits be based on initial/previous performance tests or additional performance tests (citing 63.864(j)(1),(j)(2)) and related checklist items and A‑part notification/waiver criteria, so the key reason is captured."}

candidates.title: National Emission Standards for Hazardous Air Pollutants for Steel Pickling and Hydrochloric Acid Regeneration Plants

criteria.criterion: If the owner or operator of a new, reconstructed, or existing steel pickling facility or acid regeneration plant is subject to this subpart, then performance tests to measure HCl mass flows or HCl concentration at the control device inlet and outlet must be conducted on the schedule required by the subpart.

If a wet scrubber is used as the emission control device at a source subject to this subpart, then the owner or operator must install, operate, and maintain systems that measure and record the scrubber makeup water flow rate and, if applicable, the recirculation water flow rate, with those flow rates monitored continuously and recorded at least once per shift while the scrubber is operating.

If establishing scrubber operating parameters during a performance test, then each operating parameter must be monitored continuously and recorded with sufficient frequency to establish a representative average but no less frequently than once every 15 minutes during the test runs used to establish the parameters.
If any required operating parameter listed in paragraph (a)(2) is not recorded, then that failure is a violation of the monitoring requirements of this subpart.

If monitoring devices are used to measure scrubber flow rates for compliance with this subpart, then each device must be certified by the manufacturer to be accurate to within 5 percent and calibrated per the manufacturer's instructions but not less frequently than once per year.

If the owner or operator uses a wet scrubber and performance testing establishes minimum makeup and recirculation flow rates, then operation with excursions below those minimum values requires initiation of corrective action as specified in the subpart's maintenance requirements.

If subject to this subpart, then the owner or operator must retain required records (including scrubber makeup and recirculation water flow rates) for 5 years and keep the most recent 2 years of records onsite.

candidates.title: General Provisions

criteria.criterion: If a continuous monitoring system (CMS) is required by a relevant standard (such as Subpart CCC), then the CMS is subject to the monitoring provisions of § 63.8 of this part.

If a CMS is used to meet a monitoring requirement, then the CMS must be operated and maintained consistent with good air pollution control practices, be installed to obtain representative measures, and be verified operational prior to or in conjunction with performance testing.

If data are collected by CEMS or other CMS for non-opacity pollutants, then data must be reduced to 1-hour averages computed from four or more equally spaced data points per hour (unless the relevant standard specifies otherwise).

If a CMS is required, then performance evaluations, QA/QC plans, and notification/submission requirements for CMS performance evaluations and performance tests must be followed as specified in § 63.7 and § 63.8.

checklist: Is the facility an affected steel pickling facility or hydrochloric acid regeneration plant subject to Subpart CCC?
Are the two continuous pickling lines and the acid regeneration plant controlled by wet scrubbers for HCl emissions?
Do the wet scrubbers have recirculation capability (i.e., is recirculation water flow rate applicable)?

Have initial and/or subsequent performance tests been conducted that established site-specific minimum scrubber makeup and (if applicable) recirculation flow rates? (If so, obtain the performance test reports and the established minimum values.)

During performance test runs, were scrubber flow rates monitored and recorded at least once every 15 minutes and were the averages used to set the operating parameter values? (collect raw monitoring data from test runs)
When operating normally, are the scrubber makeup and recirculation flow rates monitored continuously (CMS/CPMS installed and running)?
While the scrubber is operating, are scrubber flow rates recorded at least once per shift (shift definition used by facility)?
Are monitoring devices manufacturer-certified to ±5% accuracy (obtain certificates) and calibrated at least annually per manufacturer instructions?
Does the CMS meet general §63.8 requirements (representative sensor location, QA/QC plan, performance evaluation scheduling and notification per §63.7 and §63.8)?
Are records of scrubber makeup and recirculation flow rates and related maintenance/inspections being retained for 5 years, with the most recent 2 years onsite?
If an excursion below the minimum flow rates occurs, does the operation initiate corrective actions within 1 working day per the maintenance plan, and are those actions documented?
If relying on performance-test-derived averages, confirm the averaging period and method used to calculate the compliant operating parameter values from the test runs.

judge_text: {"score":2,"reason":"The EPA note’s key points—that Subpart CCC requires continuous monitoring of scrubber flow rates and that recording is required only once per shift—are explicitly reflected in the provided criteria (notably the criterion citing 40 CFR 63.1162(a)(2) stating continuous monitoring and at least once-per-shift recording)."}

candidates.title: General Provisions

criteria.criterion: if a collection of equipment and activities is within a single contiguous area and under common control and is included in a section 112(c) source category or subcategory for which a section 112 standard is established, then that collection is an 'affected source' under this part

if a relevant standard requires performance testing, then the owner or operator must perform performance tests as specified (generally within 180 days of the compliance date) and follow the procedures in § 63.7
if a relevant standard requires continuous monitoring systems (CMS) or other monitoring, then the monitoring requirements and procedures in § 63.8 apply

candidates.title: National Emission Standards for Hazardous Air Pollutants for Miscellaneous Coating Manufacturing Operations

criteria.criterion: if you own or operate miscellaneous coating manufacturing operations that (1) are located at or are part of a major source of HAP, (2) manufacture coatings, (3) process, use, or produce HAP, and (4) are not part of an affected source under another subpart, then the operations are subject to this subpart

if a tank or other vessel is stationary or portable, has a capacity greater than or equal to 250 gallons, and is used for mixing, blending, diluting, dissolving, temporary holding, or other processing steps in the manufacturing of a coating, then that tank is a 'process vessel' for this subpart
if a tank or other vessel has a capacity less than 250 gallons, then it is not a 'process vessel' as defined in this subpart

candidates.title: National Emission Standards for Hazardous Air Pollutants: Miscellaneous Metal Parts and Products Surface Coating Operations

criteria.criterion: if you own or operate a new, reconstructed, or existing affected source that uses 946 liters (250 gallons) per year or more of coatings that contain HAP in the surface coating of miscellaneous metal parts and products and the source is a major source or is located at/part of a major source of HAP, then this subpart applies

if an individual surface coating operation uses less than 189 liters (50 gallons) per year and the total volume of coatings exempt under that paragraph does not exceed 946 liters (250 gallons) per year at the facility, then that coating operation is exempt from this subpart's applicability

if you have storage containers and mixing vessels in which coatings, thinners and/or other additives and cleaning materials are stored or mixed for surface coating of miscellaneous metal parts and products, then those containers and mixing vessels are included in the affected source for this subpart

candidates.title: National Emission Standards for Hazardous Air Pollutants: Surface Coating of Large Appliances

criteria.criterion: if you operate a large appliance surface coating facility (new, reconstructed, or existing) then this subpart applies to the collection of items that are part of that facility

if you have storage containers and mixing vessels in which coatings, thinners, and cleaning materials are stored or mixed as part of a large appliance surface coating facility, then those containers and mixing vessels are part of the affected source covered by this subpart
if your operations are not part of a large appliance surface coating facility, then Subpart NNNN does not apply

checklist: Is the 125-gallon mixer stationary at one location or is it truly portable (moveable between sites)?
What is the mixer’s maximum liquid capacity in gallons (confirm 125 gal)?
Is the mixer used for mixing, blending, diluting, dissolving, temporary holding, or other processing steps in the manufacturing of a coating (process activity vs. purely storage)?
Does the facility manufacture coatings as defined in 40 CFR 63.8105/63.3981 (i.e., blending/mixing to produce a coating product)?
Is the facility a major source of HAP (potential to emit >=10 tpy of any single HAP or >=25 tpy of combined HAP)?
How many gallons per year of HAP-containing coatings does the facility use in surface coating activities (gal/year)?
Are the coatings used in surface coating of miscellaneous metal parts/products or large appliances (determine applicable source category)?
Is the mixer part of an affected source already regulated under another subpart (e.g., MMMM or NNNN) or claimed as ancillary/exempt (research & development, QA/QC lab, etc.)?
If evaluating emissions controls or compliance options, does the relevant standard require performance testing or CMS monitoring (triggering §§ 63.7 and 63.8 requirements)?

judge_text: {"score":2,"reason":"EPA's determination rests on the mixer being under 250 gallons and thus not meeting the subpart HHHHH 'process vessel' definition; OUR ANSWER explicitly includes the ≥250-gallon threshold and the <250-gallon exclusion for process vessels (40 CFR 63.8105(g)), so the key reasons are captured."}

candidates.title: National emissions limitations and work practice standards for site remediation

criteria.criterion: If you own or operate a facility at which you conduct a site remediation, then this subpart may apply to you.
If your site remediation cleans up a remediation material (i.e., material that contains one or more HAP listed in Table 1 of this subpart), then this subpart may apply to that remediation.

If your site remediation is co-located at your facility with one or more other stationary sources that emit HAP and meet an affected-source definition specified for a source category regulated by another subpart under 40 CFR part 63, then this subpart may apply.
If your facility is a major source of HAP as defined in § 63.2, then your site remediation is subject to this subpart (subject to the specified exceptions and aggregation rules).
If the site remediation only cleans up material that does not contain any of the HAP listed in Table 1 of this subpart, then the site remediation is not subject to this subpart.

If the site remediation is conducted at a gasoline service station to clean up remediation material from a leaking underground storage tank, or is conducted at a farm or residential site, or is conducted at a research and development facility that meets CAA section 112(c)(7) requirements, then the site remediation is not subject to this subpart.

If the total quantity of the HAP listed in Table 1 contained in remediation material removed during all site remediations at your facility is less than 1 megagram (Mg) annually, then the site remediation activities are not subject to the requirements of this subpart except for the recordkeeping requirement.

If all remediation activities at your facility that would be subject to this subpart are completed and you have notified the Administrator in writing that all such remediation activities are completed, then the subpart's requirements do not apply to those completed activities (but records must be maintained and future remediations that meet applicability would be subject).

If your site remediation includes affected sources as designated in § 63.7882 (process vents; remediation material management units; equipment leaks meeting the component concentration and hours-in-service tests; pressure relief devices), then those affected sources are the units regulated under this subpart and must meet the applicable standards for those affected-source types.

candidates.title: General provisions (performance testing, monitoring, definitions)

criteria.criterion: If you are subject to a relevant standard established under this part (i.e., a section 112 relevant standard), then Subpart A (the General Provisions) applies to you and supplements that relevant standard.

If a relevant standard requires performance testing, then, unless a waiver or extension applies, the owner or operator must perform performance tests within 180 days of the compliance date for the affected source.

If a relevant standard requires a continuous monitoring system (CMS) or otherwise requires monitoring, then the monitoring is subject to the provisions of § 63.8 (operation, maintenance, quality control, data reduction, and performance evaluation) and any CMS performance specifications in the relevant standard.

checklist: Do you (the current owner/operator) actually conduct any site remediation activities at the property, or does another entity conduct and remain legally and operationally responsible for the remediation units?

Who owns and who operates the remediation units (tanks, surface impoundments, containers, separators, transfer systems, process vents, equipment components)? (confirm legal ownership and operational control)

Are the remediation units located on contiguous or adjoining property under common control with your facility (i.e., would they be considered part of your 'facility' per the definition in 40 CFR 63.7957)?
Do the remediation materials managed/treated contain one or more HAP listed in Table 1 of Subpart GGGGG (determine by sampling/speciation methods referenced in the subpart)?

Is the site remediation co-located with one or more other stationary sources at the site that emit HAP and meet an affected-source definition for a category regulated by another subpart under part 63?

Is your facility a major source of HAP (any single HAP ≥ 10 tpy or combined HAP ≥ 25 tpy) per 40 CFR 63.2, taking into account the aggregation rules and the special aggregation provisions in 40 CFR 63.7881(a)(3)(i)-(ii)?

What is the total annual quantity (Mg/yr) of the HAP listed in Table 1 contained in remediation material excavated/extracted/removed at the facility (to determine the <1 Mg/yr exemption under § 63.7881(c))?
Are the remediation activities limited to exempt categories (e.g., gasoline service station UST cleanup; farm or residential sites; qualifying R&D under CAA 112(c)(7))?
Have all remediation activities that would be subject to Subpart GGGGG been completed and has written notification been sent to the Administrator under § 63.7881(d)?

For equipment-leak applicability: do individual equipment components contact remediation material with total HAP ≥ 10% by weight and are they intended to operate ≥ 300 hours per calendar year (per § 63.7882(a)(3))?

For process-vent or remediation-material-management-unit options: what is the VOHAP concentration (ppmw) of the remediation material and do process vent flow rates meet any exemption thresholds referenced in the subpart (e.g., <10 ppmw, <500 ppmw, or flow rate exemptions in § 63.7885/§ 63.7886)?

If subject to a relevant standard, does the facility need to schedule performance tests or CMS performance evaluations (confirm compliance dates and whether tests are required within 180 days per § 63.7 and monitoring requirements per § 63.8)?

judge_text: {"score":2,"reason":"EPA's sole key reason—another party (Boeing) is legally responsible for and conducts the remediation— is captured by the submitted criteria and checklist (e.g., the applicability criterion ‘If you own or operate a facility at which you conduct a site remediation…’ with citations to 63.7881(a) and 63.7957, and checklist items asking who owns/operates and who is legally/operationally responsible)."}

candidates.title: National Emission Standards for Hazardous Waste Combustors (Subpart EEE)

criteria.criterion: If you operate a hazardous waste incinerator (including all associated firing systems and air pollution control devices), then Subpart EEE applies to your unit.

If your combustor has multiple combustion chambers (for example, a rotary kiln plus a secondary combustion chamber), then you must measure temperature and establish a minimum combustion chamber temperature limit for each combustion chamber as part of the operating parameter limits.

If you seek to waive or eliminate an operating parameter limit (including a minimum combustion chamber temperature), then you must submit an application with the comprehensive performance test plan justifying the waiver and describing an alternative monitoring/limit that provides equivalent assurance of compliance.

If the minimum combustion chamber temperature is an operating parameter interlocked to the automatic waste feed cutoff (AWFCO), then AWFCO requirements apply and you may not ramp down pumpable hazardous waste beyond the limits specified when AWFCO is triggered by exceedance of minimum combustion chamber temperature.

If an operating parameter (such as minimum combustion chamber temperature) is applicable to multiple emission standards, then the most stringent limit derived from the independent performance tests applies.

candidates.title: General Provisions (Subpart A)

criteria.criterion: If your unit qualifies as an 'affected source' under the part 63 definitions, then you are subject to the performance testing requirements and deadlines in § 63.7.

If you intend to use alternative test methods or alternative/modified monitoring procedures (including requests to waive or substitute an operating parameter limit), then you must follow the alternative test/method and alternative monitoring approval procedures in § 63.7(f) and § 63.8(f).

If you will conduct or change performance testing and/or rely on alternate monitoring or waivers, then you must submit the site-specific test plan and required notifications on the timelines and with the content required by § 63.7(b) and § 63.7(c).

checklist: Confirm the unit is a hazardous waste incinerator as defined in §63.1201(a) (that the rotary kiln and associated firing systems are part of an incinerator affected source).

Confirm how many distinct combustion chambers exist (document whether the rotary kiln and the secondary combustion chamber are physically and operationally separate combustion chambers and where hazardous waste is introduced in each).
Document measurement locations for bulk gas temperature for each combustion chamber (record the locations you will use as required by §63.1209(j)(1)(i) and §63.1209(k)(2)(i)).
Verify whether minimum combustion chamber temperature is currently an AWFCO‑interlocked operating parameter and identify the AWFCO interlock logic and ramp‑down procedures (per §63.1206(c)(3)).

Assemble data and justification you would include in a waiver/alternative monitoring application and confirm you will submit it with the comprehensive performance test plan (timing: not later than with the test plan) as described in §63.1209(g)(1)(iii).

Identify whether performance tests for DRE, dioxin/furan, and other applicable pollutants will be conducted simultaneously or separately and determine which test yields the most restrictive operating limits (per §63.1209(i)).

Confirm existing and planned continuous monitoring systems (CEMS/CMS) and whether you will propose alternative monitoring methods (and be prepared to follow §63.7(f) and §63.8(f) procedures for approval).

Document each hazardous waste feed location and whether hazardous waste is fed in the normal flame zone or at locations other than the normal flame zone (impacts applicability of DRE demonstration per §63.1206(b)(7)).

Prepare the site-specific comprehensive performance test plan content required by §63.1207(f) (feedstream analyses, test schedule, operating conditions, and proposed alternative monitoring/waiver materials).

The EPA note’s sole key reason — that the rotary kiln and secondary combustion chamber are separate combustion chambers and therefore require a minimum combustion chamber temperature limit for each — is directly captured by the Subpart EEE criterion and checklist items in the provided answer (measurement/limit required for each distinct chamber)."}

candidates.title: National Emission Standards for Hazardous Air Pollutants for Surface Coating of Metal Furniture

criteria.criterion: If you conduct surface coating of metal furniture (application of coatings to a substrate, e.g., by spray guns or dip tanks), then your operations fall within the source category addressed by this subpart.

If you own or operate an affected source as defined in §63.4882 and that affected source is a major source, is located at a major source, or is part of a major source of HAP emissions, then this subpart applies to that affected source.
If the surface coating conducted at the affected source uses only coatings, thinners, and cleaning materials that contain no organic HAP, then this subpart does not apply to that surface coating.

If the surface coating activity meets any of the exemption conditions in paragraphs (c)(2) through (c)(6) (e.g., coating of metal components of wood furniture subject to subpart JJ, research/laboratory or janitorial/maintenance operations, coating only small non-furniture items, in-house repair/maintenance not for commerce unless HAP emissions meet major thresholds, or Armed Forces installations), then that surface coating is not subject to this subpart.

If you claim to be using only HAP-free coatings, thinners, and cleaning materials for the compliant material option, then you must determine and document the mass fraction of organic HAP for each coating, thinner, and cleaning material (by supplier data or specified test methods) and demonstrate each thinner and cleaning material contains no organic HAP as required for compliance demonstrations.

If you choose to demonstrate compliance using a compliant material option on an ongoing basis, then use of any coating, thinner, or cleaning material that contains organic HAP is a deviation that must be reported.

candidates.title: General Provisions

criteria.criterion: If your stationary source emits or has the potential to emit 10 tons per year or more of a single HAP or 25 tons per year or more of a combination of HAP, then it is a major source for purposes of determining whether a Part 63 subpart (such as RRRR) applies.

If your collection of equipment and activities within a single contiguous area and under common control is included in a section 112(c) source category, then that collection is the 'affected source' for the relevant Part 63 standard.

If a relevant subpart requires performance testing or monitoring, then the owner or operator must follow the performance testing (§63.7) and monitoring (§63.8) requirements and schedules specified in that subpart unless a waiver or alternative is approved.

checklist: Do you perform surface coating of metal furniture or components (e.g., cabinetry, shelving, fixtures) as defined in 40 CFR 63.4881(a)?

Are the coatings, thinners, and cleaning materials you currently use free of organic HAP in the condition received from the supplier (verify via manufacturer's formulation data or testing per 40 CFR 63.4941(a) and (b))?
Do you use any reclaimed cleaning materials on-site; if so, were those materials shown as HAP-free when received (see 40 CFR 63.4941(a) last sentence)?
Is your facility (or the contiguous group of sources under common control) a major source of HAPs based on actual and potential to emit (≥10 tpy single HAP or ≥25 tpy combined) per 40 CFR 63.2?

Does your affected source include the items listed in 40 CFR 63.4882(b) (all coating operations, storage/mixing vessels, conveying equipment, and waste conveyance) so you can identify the full affected source boundary?
Does any exemption in 40 CFR 63.4881(c)(2)–(c)(6) apply (e.g., coatings limited to research/lab, janitorial, small items only, in-house noncommercial repairs, or Armed Forces installations)?

If claiming the compliant material option, have you documented initial and ongoing records and calculations required to show each coating's organic HAP content and that thinners/cleaning materials contain no organic HAP as required by 40 CFR 63.4941 and 63.4942?

If you were previously using methylene chloride adhesives or organic-HAP-containing coatings, have you removed all such materials from the affected source and documented current material inventories and supplier data showing no organic HAP content?

judge_text: {"score":2,"reason":"EPA's sole stated reason—that the facility meets 40 CFR 63.4881(c)(1) (surface coating uses only coatings/thinners/cleaners with no organic HAP, so RRRR does not apply)—is explicitly included in the candidate criteria (RRRR criterion citing 63.4881(c)(1)) and reflected in the checklist."}

candidates.title: National Emission Standards for Hazardous Air Pollutants for Secondary Lead Smelting

criteria.criterion: if you own or operate any of the listed affected sources (blast, reverberatory, rotary, or electric furnaces; refining kettles; agglomerating furnaces; dryers; process fugitive emissions sources; buildings containing lead-bearing materials; or fugitive dust sources) at a secondary lead smelter then you are subject to this subpart

if your facility recycles lead-bearing scrap material into elemental lead or lead alloys by smelting (i.e., meets the definition of a secondary lead smelter) and you own or operate any of the affected sources listed in §63.541(a) then you are subject to this subpart
if you are a primary lead processor, a lead refiner, or a lead remelter then you are not subject to this subpart

if you own or operate an affected source at a secondary lead smelter then the fact that measured lead emissions are below the numerical emission limits in §63.543 does not by itself determine whether the subpart applies (applicability is based on presence/operation of affected sources at a secondary lead smelter)

candidates.title: General Provisions

criteria.criterion: if a relevant standard (e.g., the Secondary Lead Smelting standard) applies to your affected source then the General Provisions of Part 63 (Subpart A) apply as specified by the relevant subpart

if you are subject to Subpart X then you must follow those portions of Subpart A identified for Subpart X (e.g., testing, monitoring, recordkeeping and reporting requirements) as specified in Table 1 to Subpart X
if required by the relevant standard to perform performance testing then you must follow the timing, notification, QA, and test conduct requirements in §63.7
if a continuous monitoring system (CEMS/CMS) is required by the relevant standard then you must follow the monitoring design, operation, QA, and data handling requirements in §63.8

checklist: Do you recycle lead-bearing scrap (e.g., lead-acid batteries, reverberatory furnace slag, flue dust) into elemental lead or lead alloys by smelting? (See definition of "secondary lead smelter" in 40 CFR 63.542.)

Do you own or operate any of the affected source types listed in §63.541(a): blast, reverberatory, rotary, or electric furnaces; refining kettles; agglomerating furnaces; dryers; process fugitive emission sources; buildings containing lead-bearing materials; or fugitive dust sources?
Is your facility instead a primary lead processor, lead refiner, or lead remelter? (If yes, §63.541(a) indicates Subpart X does not apply.)
Are your operations located within a single contiguous area under common control that would constitute the 'affected source' for Part 63 purposes? (See 40 CFR 63.2.)
Have you measured lead concentrations and flow rates for your process vents, and have you calculated the monthly and 12-month rolling flow-weighted average lead concentration per §63.543(a)(1)-(4)?
What are the dates construction or reconstruction of the affected sources commenced relative to May 19, 2011 (see compliance dates in §63.546)?

Do you have control devices, enclosures, baghouses, HEPA or wet ESP, CEMS, or other capture/control systems in place for process vents or total enclosures that would invoke the monitoring/operation requirements in §§63.543–63.548?

Are fugitive dust sources and materials storage/handling areas managed consistent with the total enclosure and fugitive dust control requirements in §§63.544 and 63.545 (e.g., negative-pressure total enclosures vented to controls, paved roadways, cleaning, vehicle washes)?
Do you currently hold or require a Title V permit (40 CFR parts 70/71) as indicated by §63.541(c)?

If you have CEMS or are considering relying on alternate monitoring/test methods, have you reviewed the Subpart A procedures for performance testing (§63.7) and CMS requirements (§63.8) and the Subpart X citations that specify which Subpart A sections apply (Table 1 to Subpart X per §63.541(b))?

judge_text: {"score":2,"reason":"EPA's key reason—that the facility recycles lead-bearing scrap and therefore meets the definition of a secondary lead smelter subject to the Secondary Lead Smelting MACT—is explicitly captured in OUR ANSWER (criterion citing 40 CFR 63.542/63.541 and the checklist question about recycling lead-bearing scrap)."}

candidates.title: General Provisions — Recordkeeping and Reporting Requirements

criteria.criterion: If an owner or operator is subject to the recordkeeping requirements of this part for an affected source, then they must maintain files of all information required by this part and retain them for at least 5 years with the most recent 2 years kept on site.

If records include measurements needed to demonstrate compliance (including raw performance test measurements, raw monitoring measurements, and other ‘‘raw data’’ used to demonstrate compliance), then those measurements and raw data must be retained and made available as specified for performance tests and monitoring (including the 5-year retention requirement for performance test records).

candidates.title: Recordkeeping requirements for floating roof storage vessels (§63.1065)

criteria.criterion: If you own or operate storage vessels subject to §63.1065(a), then you must keep a record of the dimensions of the storage vessel, an analysis of capacity, and an identification of the liquid stored for as long as the liquid is stored.

If you perform floating roof inspections or external floating roof (EFR) seal gap measurements under this section, then you must retain inspection results (including descriptions of failures, repairs, dates) and a record of EFR seal gap measurements including the raw data obtained and any calculations performed, with the records required in paragraphs (b), (c), and (d) kept at least 5 years and maintained so they can be readily accessed within 24 hours.

candidates.title: Subpart DD — Recordkeeping requirements (§63.696)

criteria.criterion: If an owner or operator is subject to Subpart DD, then they must comply with the recordkeeping requirements in §63.10 of Subpart A as specified in Table 2 of this subpart.

If an owner or operator uses an external floating roof to comply with the tank control requirements of this subpart, then they must prepare and maintain records for each seal gap inspection that include the date measurements are performed, the raw data obtained, and the calculations of the total gap surface area (and, if measurements do not conform, a description of repairs and repair dates).

candidates.title: Subpart G — Storage vessel provisions: recordkeeping (§63.123)

criteria.criterion: If an owner or operator elects to comply with the Subpart G provision that requires seal gap measurements (§63.119(c)), then they must keep records describing the results of each seal gap measurement that include the date of the measurement, the raw data obtained, and the calculations described in the referenced measurement procedure.

If an owner or operator owns a Group 1 or Group 2 storage vessel, then they must keep readily accessible records showing the vessel dimensions and an analysis of vessel capacity for as long as the storage vessel retains Group 1 or Group 2 status and is in operation.

checklist: Determine which subpart(s) apply to each storage tank (is each tank regulated under Subpart WW, Subpart DD, Subpart G, or only subject to general provisions in Subpart A?).
Confirm whether each tank is an external floating roof (EFR) and whether you perform EFR seal gap measurements or the inspections described in the cited subparts.
Identify the types of records you generate in the field (field data sheets): do they contain raw measurement values, instrument readings, and the calculations used to produce the electronic entry?
Verify where records are stored now: are field data sheets retained on site, scanned and saved off site, or discarded after electronic entry?

Verify retention periods needed: are vessel dimension records to be kept for as long as the liquid is stored, and are inspection/seal-gap/raw data records to be kept for at least 5 years (and most recent 2 years on site)?
Confirm that the most recent 2 years of required records are physically on site or readily accessible on site (e.g., via network) and that records can be produced within 24 hours if inspected.

If you perform performance tests or other compliance measurements, confirm you retain raw performance-test and monitoring raw data and supporting documentation for at least 5 years as required by §63.7/§63.10.

If you currently discard original field sheets after entering electronic forms, confirm the electronic record contains the same raw values and calculations (not just summaries) and that the electronic files are retained and retrievable per the applicable on-site/off-site and retention requirements.

If relying on electronic-only copies, verify whether any relevant subpart or delegated authority requires original hardcopy retention or specific formats (and whether an on-site accessible electronic system meets the 'readily accessible' requirement).
If unsure about subpart applicability or interpretation, prepare an applicability determination and retain it on site for 5 years (signed and with supporting analysis) as required by §63.10(b)(3).

judge_text: {"score": 1, "reason": "The answer captures the statutory requirement to retain raw measurement/raw data (multiple citations including 63.123(d), 63.1065, and 63.10/63.7), but it does not incorporate the EPA QA guidance point (Letter 2008-02-15) that original field records must be preserved—the checklist only advises to 'verify' whether hardcopy/originals are required rather than citing or adopting the guidance requiring preservation."}

candidates.title: Area Source Standards for Plating and Polishing Operations

criteria.criterion: If you own or operate a plating and polishing facility that is an area source and is engaged in one or more of the listed plating/polishing processes and uses or emits compounds of cadmium, chromium, lead, manganese, or nickel, then the facility is subject to this subpart.
If a specific process unit is subject to the chromium electroplating/anodizing standards in 40 CFR part 63 subpart N, then that process unit is excluded from this subpart.

If the plating or polishing process materials contain cadmium, chromium, lead, or nickel as the metal in amounts less than 0.1 percent by weight (or manganese less than 1.0 percent by weight) in the materials as used, then that plating or polishing process is not subject to this subpart.

If you own or operate a non-cyanide electrolytic (electroplating, electroforming, or electropolishing) tank that contains one or more plating and polishing metal HAP and operates at a pH less than 12, then that tank is an affected source and is subject to the equipment standards and management practices in this subpart.

candidates.title: National Emission Standards for Chromium Emissions from Hard and Decorative Chromium Electroplating and Chromium Anodizing Tanks

criteria.criterion: If you own or operate a chromium electroplating or chromium anodizing tank at a facility performing hard chromium electroplating, decorative chromium electroplating, or chromium anodizing, then subpart N applies to that affected source.

If a tank contains a chromium solution but no electrolytic process occurs (for example, a chrome conversion coating tank where no electrical current is applied), or if the tank is an etching, rinse, or cleaning tank in which neither chromium electroplating nor chromium anodizing is taking place, then that tank is not subject to subpart N.

If the process is chromium anodizing as defined (part acts as the anode in a chromic acid solution), then the tank meets the subpart N definition of chromium anodizing and is within the scope of subpart N.

candidates.title: General Provisions (Subpart A)

criteria.criterion: If your stationary source emits or has the potential to emit 10 tons per year or more of any single HAP or 25 tons per year or more of combined HAP, then it is a major source (not an area source) under these general provisions.
If a relevant subpart requires performance testing, then you must perform such tests within 180 days of the compliance date (unless a waiver or extension applies under the provisions of § 63.7).
If a relevant standard requires a continuous monitoring system (CMS) or other monitoring, then the monitoring provisions and required CMS quality/operation/recordkeeping in § 63.8 apply.

checklist: Confirm whether the tank process is chromium electroplating or chromium anodizing (is chromic acid used and is an electrical current applied with the part acting as the anode?)
If chromic acid is present, confirm whether an electrolytic current is applied (i.e., is the operation electrolytic vs non-electrolytic conversion coating?).
Determine whether the tank is being used for etching/cleaning/rinsing (examples listed as not subject to Subpart N) or for electroplating/anodizing.

Determine whether the bath contains plating and polishing metal HAP (cadmium, chromium, lead, manganese, nickel) and the concentration of the metal(s) in the bath (compare to 0.1% for Cd/Cr/Pb/Ni and 1.0% for Mn thresholds).
Measure and record bath pH to determine if it is a cyanide/pH ≥12 process or a non-cyanide (pH <12) electrolytic process.
Establish whether the facility is an area source or a major source by calculating actual and potential to emit HAP (tons per year) for single and combined HAP.
Determine whether the tank/unit is covered by Subpart N (chromium electroplating/anodizing) or would fall under the Area Source Plating and Polishing subpart (WWWWWW) based on the above facts.

Identify whether the process is batch, continuous (reel-to-reel), or short-term/flash plating and note startup dates (compare construction/startup dates to subpart new/existing source cutoff dates in the relevant subparts).

If subject to WWWWWW and using electrolytic non-cyanide tanks, decide which compliance approach you would use (wetting agent/fume suppressant, capture+control device, or covers) and verify applicable tank cover/capture/control availability and manufacturer's instructions.

If subject to subpart N, verify whether any exclusions apply (research/laboratory, educational, or process tanks where no electroplating/anodizing occurs) and check the specific subpart N definitions for chromium anodizing/electroplating.
Document whether the operation is research and laboratory (potential exemption) or is conducted for commercial production.
Record whether any process materials or final bath compositions include chromic acid (CrO3) or so-called hexavalent chromium (contains hexavalent chromium per definitions).

judge_text: {"score":2, "reason":"EPA's key reason is that the process meets the definition of electropolishing (40 CFR 63.11504(a)(vi)). OUR ANSWER explicitly includes electropolishing in the WWWWWW criteria (non‑cyanide electrolytic tanks including electropolishing at pH <12) and also references the general plating/polishing process listing and metal HAP thresholds, so the EPA's rationale is captured by the provided criteria."}

candidates.title: Area Sources: Carbon Black Production

criteria.criterion: If you own or operate a carbon black production facility that is an area source of hazardous air pollutant (HAP) emissions, then you are subject to this subpart.
If your facility is a research and development facility as defined in section 112(c)(7) of the Clean Air Act, then this subpart does not apply to you.

candidates.title: Source category-specific applicability, definitions, and requirements (including Carbon Black Production)

criteria.criterion: If a carbon black production process unit is located at a major source (as defined in section 112(a) of the Act), then that process unit is an affected source under the carbon black production provisions of this subpart.

If your process produces carbon black by the furnace, thermal, acetylene decomposition, or lampblack processes, then it meets the definition of 'carbon black production' for purposes of these requirements.

If the HAP concentration of a carbon black production main unit filter process vent (or other process vent as determined by the applicability procedures) is greater than or equal to 260 parts per million by volume, then the process vent is subject to the control requirements listed in Table 8 to § 63.1103(f) (e.g., route to a flare or achieve 98 wt% reduction or 20 ppmv), and you must follow the applicability assessment procedures in this paragraph.

candidates.title: General Provisions

criteria.criterion: If a relevant standard (or this subpart) requires performance testing, then the performance testing requirements of § 63.7 apply.
If a relevant standard requires continuous or other continuous parameter monitoring systems (CMS), then the monitoring requirements of § 63.8 apply.

If you need to determine whether your source is an 'area source' or a 'major source' for applicability purposes, then use the definitions and rules in § 63.2 (including the definition of 'area source' = any stationary source that is not a major source).

If Subpart MMMMMM applies to your facility, then the General Provisions specified as applicable to that subpart (40 CFR part 63, subpart A, §§ 63.1–63.5 and §§ 63.11–63.16) apply as noted in § 63.11404.

candidates.title: Applicability and designation of affected sources for certain off-site material recovery/management operations

criteria.criterion: If the plant site is a major source of HAP emissions and the site contains a recovery or waste-management operation that receives off-site material (waste, used oil, or used solvent) as specified in § 63.680(a)(2), then the provisions of this subpart apply to the plant site affected source.

If the total annual quantity of HAP contained in the off-site material received at the plant site is less than 1 megagram per year, then the owner or operator is exempted from the requirements of §§ 63.682 through 63.699 of this subpart (facility-wide exemption), provided the determinations and documentation requirements are met.

checklist: Do you perform carbon black production (i.e., produce carbon black) by furnace, thermal, acetylene decomposition, or lampblack processes?
Is your facility an area source or a major source of HAPs (calculate potential to emit and compare to 10 t/yr single HAP or 25 t/yr total HAP per § 63.2)?

Do you receive off-site materials (waste tires) for treatment, recycling, or recovery at the plant site (check the § 63.680(b) test: waste/used oil/used solvent delivered from outside the plant site and containing HAPs at point-of-delivery)?
If you receive off-site materials, what is the total annual quantity of HAP in those off-site materials (is it ≥1 megagram/year)?

Are any carbon black process vents present (main unit filter vents, process/product vents, dryer vents)? Measure or estimate HAP concentration of the main unit filter and representative process vents (is any vent ≥260 ppmv HAP?) per the process vent applicability procedures in § 63.1103(f)(3)(iv)-(v) and § 63.1104.
Was construction or reconstruction of the affected source commenced on or before April 4, 2007 (existing) or after April 4, 2007 (new) (per § 63.11400(b))?
Is the facility operated primarily as a research and development operation (R&D) as defined in CAA § 112(c)(7) (if yes, Subpart MMMMMM may not apply)?
If subject to the rule, will you need to perform performance testing (prepare to comply with § 63.7 notification, test-plan, and timing requirements)?
If subject to the rule, will you need continuous monitoring/CPMS/CEMS (prepare to comply with § 63.8 monitoring, QA/QC, and reporting requirements)?
If subject to Subpart MMMMMM, will you need a title V (part 70/71) permit as required by § 63.11400(d)?

judge_text: {"score":2,"reason":"EPA's key reason—that the facility process is materially different from the carbon black production process defined in Subpart MMMMMM—is reflected in the answer: the criteria and checklist explicitly require the process to be furnace, thermal, acetylene decomposition, or lampblack carbon black production. Therefore the notes' rationale is captured."}

candidates.title: National Emission Standards for Hazardous Air Pollutants: Surface Coating of Plastic Parts and Products

criteria.criterion: If the facility performs surface coating of plastic parts or products and uses 378 liters (100 gallons) or more per year of coatings that contain HAP and the affected source is a major source (or located at/part of a major source), then the source is subject to this subpart.
If the surface coating operation uses only coatings, thinners and other additives, and cleaning materials that contain no organic HAP, then the operation is not subject to this subpart.

If you elect to comply using the emission rate with add-on controls option for a controlled coating operation (except solvent recovery systems using liquid-liquid material balances), then you must meet the operating limits in Table 1 to this subpart as established during performance tests and maintain them at all times.

If you use an add-on control device other than those listed in Table 1 to this subpart, or wish to monitor an alternative parameter and comply with a different operating limit, then you must apply to the Administrator for approval of alternative monitoring under § 63.8(f).

If you use the emission rate with add-on controls option and your add-on control device is not a solvent recovery system using liquid-liquid material balances, then you must calculate organic HAP emission reductions using capture efficiency and destruction/removal efficiency (DRE) (and treat deviations as zero efficiency unless approved otherwise).

If the control equipment is a device that reduces pollution in an airstream by destruction or removal (for example, a thermal oxidizer or carbon adsorber), then that device is an 'add-on control' as defined in this subpart.
If you use the emission rate with add-on controls option, then you must implement and document the work practice plan required for controlled coating operations.

candidates.title: General Provisions (Part 63, Subpart A)

criteria.criterion: If you plan to use an alternative monitoring method or an alternative set of monitoring parameters for a control device, then you must apply to the Administrator for approval under § 63.8(f) with the information required by that provision.

If the relevant standard requires performance testing for establishing operating limits or demonstrating control device performance, then you must perform performance tests within the timeframes and follow the notification, site-specific test plan, QA, and reporting procedures in § 63.7.

If emissions from multiple affected sources are combined before release or if a single affected source vents through multiple points, then monitoring installation and scope must follow the CMS/location rules in § 63.8 unless the Administrator approves an alternative.

checklist: Confirm the operations are surface coating of plastic parts or products (see § 63.4481(a)).
Quantify annual usage (liters or gallons per year) of coatings that contain HAP (exclude coatings that meet the 'non-HAP coating' definition) to determine if use is ≥ 378 L/yr (100 gal/yr).
Determine whether the affected source is a major source (≥ 10 tons/yr single HAP or ≥ 25 tons/yr combined HAP) or located at/part of a major source.
Verify whether all coatings, thinners, additives, and cleaning materials contain zero organic HAP (if yes, Subpart PPPP does not apply under § 63.4481(c)(1)).
Check whether the coating work falls into an exclusion or another NESHAP subcategory (e.g., automotive lamp, TPO, assembled on-road vehicle, or other subpart applicability per § 63.4481(c) and (e)).
Identify which compliance option you intend to use (compliant materials; emission rate without add-on controls; or emission rate with add-on controls) per § 63.4491.

If choosing the emission rate with add-on controls option: document which coating operations will be controlled and whether any are solvent recovery systems using liquid-liquid material balances (§ 63.4561(j)).

Specify the proposed add-on control device type (e.g., boiler) and whether it is listed in Table 1 to Subpart PPPP (if not listed, plan to apply for alternative monitoring approval under § 63.8(f) per § 63.4492(c)).
Confirm whether the proposed boiler will receive emissions routed from the coating capture system (i.e., is the boiler downstream of the capture system and thus serving as the add-on control).

Assess ability to measure or test capture efficiency and DRE for the capture+control train (plan for performance testing per § 63.4561(h) and methods/procedures required by the subpart), and identify methods/equipment to demonstrate efficiencies.

Determine whether the proposed control approach can meet the operating limits that would be established during performance tests (Table 1 limits or alternative limits if approved) and your ability to continuously monitor and maintain those parameters.
Prepare to develop and implement the work practice plan required for controlled coating operations under the emission rate with add-on controls option (see § 63.4493(b)).
Plan for performance test scheduling and notifications (notify Administrator 60 days before testing) and QA/QC and audit sample requirements per § 63.7.
Confirm you can provide required performance testing facilities/access (sampling ports, platforms, utilities) per § 63.7(d) if testing of the control device/stack is needed.

If the boiler/combustion unit would receive multiple emission streams or serve multiple sources, determine monitoring points and whether additional CMS or alternative monitoring arrangements must be proposed under § 63.8.

judge_text: {"score":2,"reason":"EPA's note hinges on the boiler being an approvable 'add-on control' under Subpart PPPP. OUR ANSWER includes the add-on control definition (devices that destroy/remove pollutants), directs evaluation of whether the boiler is listed in Table 1, and cites the §63.8(f) approval path and performance-testing/monitoring requirements for unlisted add-on controls — so the key EPA reasoning is captured."}

candidates.title: Engine Test Cells/Stands (Engine test cells and stands NESHAP)

criteria.criterion: if you own or operate an engine test cell/stand that is located at a major source of HAP emissions then you are subject to this subpart

if the collection of equipment and activities associated with engine test cells/stands commenced construction or reconstruction on or before May 14, 2002 then the affected source is existing, and if construction of the affected source was commenced after May 14, 2002 then the affected source is new
if you meet the definition of reconstruction in § 63.2 and reconstruction was commenced after May 14, 2002 then the affected source is a reconstructed affected source

if changes were made to an existing affected source primarily for the purpose of complying with revisions to engine testing requirements under 40 CFR parts 80, 86, 89, 90, 91, or 92 then those changes are not considered a modification or reconstruction for this subpart

if passive measurement and control instrumentation and electronics were installed or replaced then those items and their costs are not included as part of any affected source reconstruction evaluation

if any portion of a new or reconstructed affected source is used exclusively for testing internal combustion engines with rated power less than 25 horsepower then that portion does not have to meet the requirements of this subpart except for the initial notification requirement

if any portion of the affected source is used exclusively for testing combustion turbine engines, rocket engines, research and teaching (not engaged in commercial development), or is operated to test or evaluate fuels/transmissions/electronics then that portion does not have to meet the requirements of this subpart

if a new or reconstructed affected source is used in whole or in part for testing internal combustion engines with rated power of 25 hp (19 kW) or more and is located at a major source then the source must comply with the emission limitations in Table 1 to this subpart

if you use add-on control devices on any new or reconstructed affected source then you must meet the operating limits specified in Table 2 to this subpart and establish those limits during the performance test

if you have a new or reconstructed affected source then the specific compliance dates and notification obligations in § 63.9295 and § 63.9345 apply (including initial notification and Notification of Compliance Status deadlines)

candidates.title: General Provisions

criteria.criterion: if an owner or operator has undertaken a continuous program of construction or reconstruction or has entered into a contractual obligation to undertake and complete, within a reasonable time, a continuous program of construction or reconstruction then construction or reconstruction is considered commenced

if the replacement of components results in fixed capital cost of the new components exceeding 50 percent of the fixed capital cost that would be required to construct a comparable new source (and it is technologically and economically feasible to meet relevant standards) then that replacement meets the definition of reconstruction

if required by a relevant standard the owner or operator of a new or reconstructed affected source must perform performance testing within 180 days of the compliance date and must notify the Administrator of intent to conduct a performance test at least 60 calendar days before the test

if continuous monitoring systems (CMS) are required by a relevant standard then they must be installed, operated, quality-assured, and performance-evaluated in accordance with § 63.8 and the timelines in that section (including submitting performance evaluation plans and meeting installation/verification prior to or in conjunction with performance tests)

candidates.title: Subpart KK (compliance-dates / reconstruction-cost treatment provision)

criteria.criterion: if affected sources have undergone reconstruction then they are subject to requirements for new affected sources, and the costs associated with the purchase and installation of air pollution control equipment are not considered in determining whether the affected source has been reconstructed
if equipment retrofitting or replacement was installed specifically to comply with this subpart then the costs of that retrofitting or replacement are not considered reconstruction costs

checklist: Confirm whether the plant is a major source of HAPs (emit or potential to emit ≥10 tpy of any single HAP or ≥25 tpy combined); if so, identify that determination record
List every engine test cell/stand and whether each is used for uninstalled engines and the rated power of engines tested (document any cells that test <25 hp engines only)
Assemble a chronological list of all component replacements, additions, and modifications to the test cells/stands (dates, vendors, invoices, POs, scope of work)

Determine whether the changes were part of a continuous program of construction/reconstruction or the result of a single contractual obligation (documentation of contracts, project plans, or continuous work programs)

Calculate the fixed capital cost of the replaced/new components and obtain an engineering estimate of the fixed capital cost to construct a comparable new affected source (show math and supporting quotes/estimating basis)

Identify and segregate costs and items that are passive measurement and control instrumentation and electronics (describe why each instrument is passive vs active control) and collect purchase/installation costs for those items

Determine whether any changes were made primarily to comply with revisions to engine testing requirements in 40 CFR parts 80, 86, 89, 90, 91, or 92 (document intent, specifications, purchase orders, or engineering memos showing regulatory-driver rationale)

Identify any air pollution control equipment purchases/installation and document whether they were installed specifically to comply with this subpart (invoices, engineering change requests, compliance-driven scopes)

For any reconstruction-cost calculation, document whether you included or excluded costs for: (a) passive measurement/control instrumentation, (b) air pollution control equipment purchased/installed to comply with the subpart

If claiming any portion is excluded (e.g., turbine, rocket, research/teaching, fuels/transmissions/electronics testing, or <25 hp testing), document how that portion is used exclusively and provide supporting operational logs or test schedules
Assemble startup dates for the affected source and for any major reconstructed portions to determine whether construction/reconstruction commenced before or after May 14, 2002
If you use add-on controls, list the control devices and be prepared to establish operating limits during a performance test (identify planned monitoring parameters and any existing monitoring)

Collect records of prior notifications, any initial notifications filed under §63.9345, and be prepared to file required notifications (Initial Notification, Notification of Compliance Status) per the timelines in §63.9295 and §63.9345
Gather contracts, engineering estimates, or vendor quotes that support the comparable-new-source cost basis used in the >50% fixed capital cost reconstruction test
Prepare documentation describing whether passive instrumentation was treated as part of the reconstruction cost calculation (and retain invoices to support inclusion or exclusion)

judge_text: {"score":2,"reason":"EPA's sole key reason is that the replacement/addition costs did not meet the reconstruction (>50% fixed capital cost) threshold. OUR ANSWER explicitly includes the §63.2 reconstruction (>50% fixed capital cost) criterion, the requirement to calculate/compare fixed capital costs, and the exclusions for passive instrumentation and control-equipment costs (§63.9290(a)(3), §63.826(c)), so the EPA rationale is fully captured."}

candidates.title: Subpart LLLLL (Asphalt Processing and Asphalt Roofing Manufacturing NESHAP)

criteria.criterion: If you own or operate an asphalt processing facility or an asphalt roofing manufacturing facility that is a major source (or is located at, or is part of a major source), then this subpart applies to your facility.

If a control device (including a mist eliminator) is used to comply with the particulate matter, THC, opacity, or visible emission standards of this subpart, then you must conduct periodic performance tests and demonstrate continuous compliance as specified in § 63.8691(e).

If you are required to monitor control device operating limits under this subpart, then you must install, operate, and maintain a continuous parameter monitoring system (CPMS) meeting the requirements in § 63.8688 and must develop and make available a site-specific monitoring plan per § 63.8688(g)–(h).

If the control device is used to comply with the particulate matter standards in Table 1 to this subpart, then you may establish operating limits for pressure drop (minimum and maximum) across the control device using manufacturers' specifications in lieu of the site-specific limit-establishment procedure in paragraph (b).

If the affected source is operating, then you must monitor and collect data at the required intervals (continuous monitoring while operating except for specified QA/calibration/malfunctions) in accordance with § 63.8690 and § 63.8688.

candidates.title: Subpart A (General Provisions — monitoring, CMS, opacity/visible emission rules)

criteria.criterion: If a relevant standard requires a continuous monitoring system (CMS, including CPMS or COMS), then the monitoring system is subject to the requirements of § 63.8 (installation, operation, QA/QC, performance evaluation, and data reduction).

If a continuous opacity monitoring system (COMS) is required to determine compliance with a numerical opacity emission standard, then compliance with the opacity standard shall be determined by using the results from the COMS.

If you propose to use parameters or monitoring methods other than those specified in the relevant standard (for example, daily visible checks and pressure-drop monitoring instead of a COMS), then you must apply to the Administrator for approval of an alternative monitoring plan under § 63.8(f).

If you install and use a CPMS or COMS for compliance, then you must operate and maintain it consistent with good air pollution control practices and perform the performance evaluations and QA activities required in § 63.8(c)–(e).

candidates.title: Subpart AAAAAAA (Monitoring requirements — CPMS/site-specific monitoring plan provisions)

criteria.criterion: If you are using a control device to comply with the emission limits of this subpart, then you must develop and make available a site-specific monitoring plan addressing probe placement, equipment specifications, and performance evaluation procedures per § 63.11563(b).

If you are using a control device to comply with the emission limits of this subpart, then you must install, operate, and maintain a CPMS that completes a minimum of one cycle every 15 minutes and meets the 3-hour averaging/data-validity rules specified in § 63.11563(c)(1)–(3).
If you are using a pressure measurement device as part of CPMS monitoring, then the device must meet the sensitivity and daily/quarterly/periodic check requirements specified in § 63.11563(e)(1)–(6).

If you are not using a control device for compliance under this subpart, then you must develop and make available a site-specific monitoring plan that specifies the process parameters and how they are monitored to demonstrate continuous compliance per § 63.11563(g).

checklist: Determine whether your facility is a major source as defined in 40 CFR 63.2 (i.e., emits or has potential to emit ≥10 tpy of any HAP or ≥25 tpy of combined HAPs).

Confirm the tank is a covered asphalt storage tank (stores asphalt flux, oxidized asphalt, or modified asphalt) and determine whether it is a Group 1 or Group 2 tank per 40 CFR 63.8698 definitions (record tank capacity and maximum storage temperature and maximum true vapor pressure).

Confirm whether the mist eliminator is the control device used to meet particulate matter and/or opacity/visible emission requirements for that tank (is it the last control device on the exhaust stream/on or downstream of the last control device?).
Verify whether the applicable subpart tables/standards for your tank require a CPMS or COMS for the control device (check Subpart LLLLL Tables 1–5 and any permit conditions).

If you plan to rely on a minimum pressure drop across the mist eliminator as an operating limit, assemble the manufacturer's recommended minimum and maximum pressure-drop specifications and confirm whether you intend to use those as your site-specific operating limits (permitted option under 63.8689(d) for PM control devices).

If you plan to use daily visible emissions checks (e.g., Method 22/visible checks) in place of a COMS, prepare an application/justification to the Administrator for an alternative monitoring method under 40 CFR 63.8(f) and identify how you will demonstrate equivalence and QA/QC.

Prepare or locate a site-specific monitoring plan that describes the CPMS/COMS probe location, performance and equipment specifications, performance evaluation procedures, QA/QC, and recordkeeping as required by 63.8688(g)–(h) (or § 63.11563(b) for subpart AAAAAAA).

Inventory existing monitoring equipment: pressure sensors/transducers (sensitivity in kPa or percent of range), calibration and inspection schedules, and spare parts to meet the sensitivity and check frequencies in 63.8688(c) and 63.11563(e).

Document current monitoring frequency and data handling: CPMS cycle time (15-minute cycles), requirements for valid hourly and 3-hour averages, and procedures for handling malfunctions/out-of-control periods per 63.8688(a)–(b) and 63.8690.
Check whether periodic performance testing has been performed or is required (scheduling of initial and subsequent periodic tests per 63.8691(e)); collect prior test reports and dates.

If relying on manufacturers' pressure-drop specs as operating limits, be ready to record and retain calibration, inspection, and validation records for each inspection, calibration, and validation check as required by 63.8688(a)(3) and related recordkeeping provisions.

Confirm who the permitting/delegated authority is (EPA vs. State of Minnesota) and whether Administrator/State approval will be needed for any alternative monitoring plan or for use of manufacturers' specifications in lieu of other initial limit-establishment procedures.

candidates.title: General Provisions

criteria.criterion: If an affected source is required to do performance testing by a relevant standard and a waiver or extension has not been obtained, then the owner or operator must perform the required performance tests within the timeframe specified in this section (e.g., within 180 days of the compliance date unless otherwise provided).

If the owner or operator applies in writing and the Administrator determines the source is meeting the relevant standard on a continuous basis or is under an extension of compliance, then the Administrator may waive individual performance tests upon written application.

If a force majeure delays testing beyond the regulatory deadline and the owner or operator notifies the Administrator and submits the required justification, then the Administrator may, in his/her discretion, grant an extension of the performance test deadline.

candidates.title: National Emission Standards for Hazardous Air Pollutants for Industrial, Commercial, and Institutional Boilers Area Sources

criteria.criterion: If a boiler has a heat input capacity of 10 million Btu per hour or greater, then it must conduct all applicable performance (stack) tests on a triennial basis (completed no more than 37 months after the previous performance test) except as specified in paragraphs (b)–(e).

If a boiler uses a continuous emission monitoring system (CEMS) for carbon monoxide (CO), then the boiler is exempt from the initial CO performance testing requirement in Table 4 to this subpart and from the oxygen concentration operating limit specified in Table 3 to this subpart.
If you must conduct performance testing under this subpart, then you must conduct the tests according to §63.7 (including developing a site-specific test plan) and the procedures in §63.11212.

If you intend to use results from a previously conducted emission test to document conformance with the emission standards and operating limits of this subpart, then you must include the date and a summary of the results in the Notification of Compliance Status.

checklist: For each boiler at each facility, confirm whether the facility is an "area source" (i.e., not a major source for HAPs) as used in this subpart (see 40 CFR 63.11194 and the definition of area source in 40 CFR 63.2).
For each boiler, record the maximum heat input capacity (MMBtu/hr) to determine whether it is >= 10 MMBtu/hr (triennial testing threshold per 40 CFR 63.11220(a)).
For each boiler, confirm fuel type/subcategory (coal per 40 CFR 63.11200(a)) and whether you plan to cease coal use (date of fuel cessation, here April 30, 2020).
For each boiler, determine whether a CO CEMS is installed and operating (exemption from initial CO performance test per 40 CFR 63.11212(b)).

For each boiler, note the date and results of the last CO performance test and retain summary information needed for Notification of Compliance Status if relying on a previous test (40 CFR 63.11225(a)(5)).

Determine the next scheduled performance test due date (triennial interval: no more than 37 months after prior test per 40 CFR 63.11220(a)) and whether a waiver application must be submitted at least 60 days before the scheduled test (see §63.7(h)(3)).

If seeking a waiver, prepare documentation showing continuous compliance (or other justification such as technical/economic infeasibility), and be prepared to submit a written application to the Administrator per 40 CFR 63.7(h)(3) and the timing requirements in 40 CFR 63.7(h)(2)–(4).

If coal use will cease before the next required test date, document the planned cessation date and determine whether notification of fuel switch/cessation to the Administrator is required under this subpart (see 40 CFR 63.11225(g) and the compliance/timing provisions of §63.7).

judge_text: {"score":2,"reason":"Yes. The answer cites 40 CFR 63.7(h) (waiver authority) and includes checklist items to document planned cessation of coal use, prepare a written waiver application, and demonstrate continuous compliance (and references notification/NOC requirements and use of prior test results). These capture the EPA Notes' key reasons (facility ceasing coal and meeting the §63.7(h) waiver conditions)."}
