candidates.title: Halogenated Solvent Cleaning Machines (Subpart T)

criteria.criterion: If an individual solvent cleaning machine uses any solvent containing methylene chloride, perchloroethylene, trichloroethylene, 1,1,1-trichloroethane, carbon tetrachloride, or chloroform in a total concentration greater than 5 percent by weight as a cleaning and/or drying agent, then that machine is subject to Subpart T.

If you are an owner or operator of a solvent cleaning machine that meets the applicability criteria in paragraph (a), then the provisions of Subpart A (General Provisions) apply to you except as noted in this subpart's appendices.

If you operate batch vapor or in-line solvent cleaning machines that are complying with the standards in § 63.463, then you must submit an annual report by February 1 of the year following the reporting year containing the operator training statement and an estimate of solvent consumption (annual reporting requirement).

If you operate batch vapor or in-line solvent cleaning machines that are complying with the alternative standards in § 63.464, then you must submit an annual solvent emission report every year containing machine size/type, average monthly solvent consumption, and 3-month rolling average emission estimates.

If you are an owner or operator of an affected facility as defined in § 63.471 (facility-wide aggregation of solvent cleaning machines), then you must submit a solvent emission report every year with average monthly solvent consumption and 12-month rolling total emissions and demonstrate compliance with facility-wide limits.

If you no longer have any solvent cleaning machines that meet the Subpart T definition in § 63.460(a) (i.e., you use no listed halogenated HAP solvents >5% by weight in any cleaning machines), then Subpart T does not apply to those machines and the Subpart T reporting requirements for those machines do not apply.
If the applicable facility-wide emission limit in Table 1 of § 63.471(b)(2) is not met, then an exceedance has occurred and must be reported as required in § 63.468(h).

candidates.title: General Provisions (Subpart A)

criteria.criterion: If you are the owner or operator of any solvent cleaning machine subject to Subpart T, then the General Provisions in Subpart A apply to the extent incorporated by Subpart T (except as Subpart T specifies otherwise).

If a relevant standard requires performance testing for your affected source, then you must perform required performance tests within the timeframes in § 63.7 (generally within 180 days of the compliance date) unless a waiver or extension applies.
If a relevant standard requires monitoring, then the monitoring requirements in § 63.8 apply, including conduct, QA/QC, and reporting provisions for any required continuous or parametric monitoring.

If you are required to submit reports or notifications under a relevant Subpart T requirement, then you must follow Subpart A reporting/notification procedures as incorporated by Subpart T (subject to any Subpart T exceptions).

checklist: Inventory all on-site solvent cleaning machines (batch vapor, batch cold, in-line cold, in-line vapor, continuous web) and record make/model/serial number and machine type.

For each machine, verify whether any solvent used contains any listed halogenated HAP (methylene chloride, PCE, TCE, 1,1,1-TCA, carbon tetrachloride, chloroform) and the concentration (confirm via MSDS, EPA Method 18, or engineering calculations) to determine if >5% by weight.
Confirm whether any remaining cleaning activities are only 'wipe cleaning' (rags, spray wipes) which are excluded from Subpart T applicability.
Determine whether any machine is a batch vapor or in-line unit (triggers the specific annual reporting paths in § 63.468(f)/(g) or facility-wide reporting under § 63.471).

If you previously were subject but have removed or converted machines, assemble and retain a dated on-site applicability determination record/documentation showing the change in operations and evidence that no machine now uses listed halogenated HAPs >5% by weight.

Check prior submissions: did you submit initial notifications, compliance reports, or compliance statements for Subpart T previously? If so, confirm whether any outstanding annual reports remain due (see § 63.468(f)/(g) and § 63.471(h)).
Confirm whether your facility qualifies as an 'affected facility' under § 63.471 (aggregation, major/area source distinctions, exclusions) and whether facility-wide limits or reporting apply.
Verify Title V / part 70/71 permit status and whether Subpart T status affects permitting obligations (note § 63.460(h) re: area source permit exemption conditions).

Document current and planned future solvent use (do you intend to use regulated halogenated solvents in the foreseeable future?), because future reuse would re-open applicability and reporting obligations.

Maintain solvent addition/deletion logs and waste solvent records (if any) or document that no halogenated solvent additions occurred during the reporting period to support a determination that annual reports are not required.

judge_text: {"score":2,"reason":"EPA's key reason (Subpart T no longer applies because all machines were removed or converted to use non‑regulated solvents) is explicitly captured in the candidate criteria: the criterion stating that if no machines use listed halogenated HAPs >5% by weight Subpart T does not apply (with citations) and the checklist items requiring documentation of removal/conversion and no halogenated solvent use."}

candidates.title: General Provisions

criteria.criterion: If a collection of equipment or activities at your plant is an "affected source" regulated by a section 112(d) or other relevant standard, then the definitions and general requirements in Subpart A apply to determine applicability and compliance obligations for that source.

If a relevant standard requires performance testing or continuous monitoring systems, then the owner or operator must follow the performance testing requirements in §63.7 and the monitoring requirements in §63.8.

candidates.title: National Emission Standards for Organic Liquids Distribution (Non-Gasoline) (OLD)

criteria.criterion: If you own or operate an organic liquids distribution (OLD) operation that is located at, or is part of, a major source of HAP emissions, then your OLD operation is subject to this subpart.

If transfer racks at your facility are used to unload organic liquids from transport vehicles and are part of the affected source at a major source, then those transfer racks and the transport vehicles while unloading are included in the affected source covered by this subpart.

If the storage tanks, transfer racks, transport vehicles, containers, or equipment leak components are part of an affected source under another 40 CFR part 63 NESHAP, then those items are excluded from the affected source for this subpart.

If the collection of transfer racks at your facility meets the total actual annual facility-level organic liquid loading volume criterion for control set in Table 2 (items 7–10), then the transfer racks must comply with the emission limits and control requirements of this subpart for transfer racks.

If you have a transfer rack that is subject to 40 CFR part 61, subpart BB and that transfer rack is in OLD operation, then you must meet all the requirements of this subpart for that transfer rack when it is in OLD operation during loading of organic liquids.

candidates.title: National Emission Standards for Solvent Extraction for Vegetable Oil Production

criteria.criterion: If you own or operate a vegetable oil production process that is a major source of HAP emissions (or is collocated within a plant site that is a major source) and that process removes oil from listed oilseeds by direct contact with an organic solvent (for example, a hexane isomer blend), then you are an affected source subject to this subpart.

If your vegetable oil production process processes any combination of the listed oilseeds (corn germ, cottonseed, flax, peanut, rapeseed, safflower, soybean, sunflower), then the process meets the oilseed-type applicability element of this subpart and is subject to it (provided the major-source criterion is also met).

If your process uses only mechanical extraction (no organic solvent) or uses only batch solvent extraction and batch desolventizing equipment, or processes only agricultural products not defined as listed oilseeds, then your vegetable oil production process is not subject to this subpart.

If equipment at your site (such as solvent extractors, desolventizer-toasters, solvent storage and working tanks, solvent recovery systems, mineral oil absorption systems, condensers, and vessels storing solvent-laden materials) is part of the defined vegetable oil production process, then that equipment is part of the affected source for this subpart.

If you exclusively use low-HAP solvent where each HAP comprises 1 percent or less by volume in each delivery and meet the requirements of §63.2840(e), then your vegetable oil production process may follow the low-HAP solvent option and be subject only to the specific elements required by paragraph (e).

checklist: Determine whether the plant is a major source of HAPs (potential to emit ≥ 10 tpy of any single HAP or ≥ 25 tpy combined HAP) (see 40 CFR 63.2 major source definition).
Confirm whether the operation on site is a solvent-based vegetable oil production process as defined in §63.2872 (direct-contact solvent extraction producing crude vegetable oil and meal).
Confirm which oilseeds (if any) are processed (corn germ, cottonseed, flax, peanut, rapeseed, safflower, soybean, sunflower) and amounts processed to satisfy §63.2832(a)(2).

Identify whether hexane (or hexane-isomer blend) is used as the extraction solvent and whether solvent storage/working tanks, extractors, desolventizers, mineral oil absorption system, condensers, or solvent recovery equipment are present and connected to the vegetable oil process (see §63.2872).

Identify whether the solvent transfer racks/ unloading equipment are operated as part of the vegetable oil production process (i.e., unload solvent into on-site solvent storage or recovery systems that feed the extractor) or as part of a separate organic liquids distribution (OLD) operation.
Check whether the transfer racks, storage tanks, transport vehicles, or leak components are already included as part of another 40 CFR part 63 NESHAP affected source (exclusion in §63.2338(c)(1)).

If evaluating applicability to Subpart EEEE, calculate the facility's total actual annual facility-level organic liquid loading volume through transfer racks (3-year rolling average) to see if it meets the Table 2 loading-volume control criterion referenced in §63.2346(b) and defined in §63.2406.

Determine whether the transfer racks are permanent (not non-permanent/special-situation) and whether they load into or unload from transport vehicles or containers as defined by §63.2338 and §63.2406.

If transfer racks unload transport vehicles, determine whether they unload organic liquids (hexane) into storage tanks or directly to process units and whether vapor balancing/closed-vent systems or DOT-certified vapor-tight transport vehicles are used (see §63.2338(b)(2),(4) and §63.2346(a)(4)).

Verify records or documentation showing whether transport vehicles delivering hexane are vapor-tight or have vapor collection equipment (Method 27 or DOT certification) as required by EEEE when transfer racks are subject to control (see §63.2390(c) and §63.2346(d)).

If considering Subpart GGGG low‑HAP solvent option, obtain solvent delivery HAP-content documentation for each delivery to determine if each HAP is ≤1% by volume and to meet the documentation and notification requirements in §63.2840(e).

Check whether any relevant performance testing or continuous monitoring would be required by the potentially applicable subpart(s) and prepare to follow §63.7 and §63.8 notification, testing, and monitoring procedures if applicable.

judge_text: {"score":2,"reason":"All key EPA reasons are present: the GGGG criteria state that equipment used as part of the defined solvent-extraction vegetable oil process is part of the affected source, the checklist explicitly directs determining whether transfer racks/unloading equipment operate solely to support the vegetable oil process, and the EEEE criteria/exclusion for items regulated by another Part 63 standard are included. These elements capture the EPA note that the equipment applies because it is used solely to support the vegetable oil production process."}

candidates.title: National Emission Standards for Hazardous Air Pollutants: Pulp and Paper Industry

criteria.criterion: If an owner or operator uses enclosure openings or closed-vent systems to comply with the standards referenced in this subpart, then each enclosure opening and each closed-vent system must be visually inspected at least once every 30 days.
If an owner or operator uses a pulping process condensate closed collection system to comply with §63.446(d), then that condensate closed collection system must be visually inspected every 30 days.

If an owner or operator wishes to use a control device, technique, or alternative monitoring parameter or change the monitoring frequency required by this section, then the owner or operator must install any required CMS and provide to the Administrator the rationale (including data and calculations) for the selected operating parameter value, monitoring frequency, and averaging time and obtain the Administrator's approval.

candidates.title: General Provisions

criteria.criterion: If an owner or operator wishes to use an alternative monitoring procedure (minor, intermediate, or major change) to monitoring requirements in this part, then the owner or operator must submit the application/description and any required performance evaluation/test plan to the Administrator and obtain approval under §63.8(f) (subject to the timelines and conditions in that paragraph) before relying on the alternative.

If a continuous monitoring system (CMS) is required by a relevant standard, then the CMS must be installed, operated, and maintained according to §63.8 (including continuous operation and QA/QC provisions) unless the Administrator approves an alternative under §63.8(f).

candidates.title: How do I monitor and collect data to demonstrate continuous compliance?

criteria.criterion: If a provision of this subpart defines required time periods as weekly, monthly, quarterly, or annually, then those terms refer to standard calendar periods, and the owner or operator may change time periods specified in this subpart by mutual agreement with the Administrator as provided in subpart A.

If the period specified for compliance is a standard calendar period and the initial compliance date occurs after the beginning of the period, then the owner or operator must comply before the end of the standard calendar period within which the compliance deadline occurs or may perform the required task at any reasonable time during the specified period relative to the prior period as allowed in paragraph (d)(2).

checklist: Determine whether your facility and the specific closed collection systems are covered by Subpart S (i.e., confirm applicability to the pulp/paper affected source and to the specific units referenced in 40 CFR 63.453).
Identify whether the closed collection system in question is a pulping process condensate closed collection system subject to §63.453(l) or another closed-vent/enclosure subject to §63.453(k).

Confirm the exact regulatory wording that applies at your site (e.g., 'at least once every 30 days' in §63.453(k)/(l)) and whether any permit or other subpart imposes a different (federally enforceable) inspection frequency.

Calculate and document the maximum calendar-day gap that would occur under 'once each calendar month' versus 'every 30 days' for each month (showing instances where a calendar-month inspection could result in >30 days between inspections).

Assemble evidence and rationale to justify the alternative schedule (safety/staffing constraints, equivalent environmental protection, engineering/operational data, historical inspection records showing no loss of control between 30-day intervals, and any risk assessment).

Decide which type of alternative request you will seek under §63.8(f) (minor, intermediate, or major change) and prepare the written application addressing the four elements of 'monitoring' in §63.2 and any required performance evaluation/test plan per §63.8(e)(3).

Prepare any site-specific performance evaluation test plan, quality control/QA procedures, and data or calculations that demonstrate the proposed monitoring frequency provides continuous compliance as required by §63.453(n)(4) and §63.8(e).

Check timing and submission requirements (e.g., submit alternative method request per §63.8(f)(4); be aware of Administrator review timelines in §63.8(f)(5) and any subpart-specific timing requirements).

Verify whether any other subpart or your title V permit contains inspection-frequency language or prohibits calendar-month scheduling; if so, include those authorities in your application to the Administrator.

Document any worker-safety rationale (if relying instead on 'unsafe to inspect' provisions to change interval) and prepare the written 'unsafe to inspect' plan and schedule required by the relevant subpart if that approach will be used.

judge_text: {"score": 2, "reason": "The answer includes the statutory 30‑day inspection requirement and identifies the regulatory pathways and prerequisites for an alternative (§63.453(m)/(n), §63.8(f)), the need to provide data/rationale and performance evaluation, and to address calendar‑period timing and permit/safety constraints — which capture the EPA’s conditional/partial approval rationale."}

candidates.title: National Emission Standards for Hazardous Air Pollutants: Polymers and Resins (Subpart JJJ)

criteria.criterion: if a process unit is designated as a thermoplastic product process unit (TPPU) at a plant site that is a major source, then the provisions of this subpart apply to that affected source (including associated waste management units and equipment)

if equipment (including pressure relief devices) associated with an affected source are in organic HAP service, then the equipment-leak provisions of this subpart require compliance with subpart H as incorporated and modified by §63.1331

if a storage vessel is assigned to an affected source, then the storage vessel provisions in this subpart (including applicability and applicable §63.119–63.123/§63.148 requirements as modified) apply to that vessel

candidates.title: Equipment Leaks: Pressure Relief Device Standards and Equipment Leak Applicability (Subpart H)

criteria.criterion: if a pressure relief device is intended to operate in organic HAP gas or vapor service and is not routed to a closed vent system to a control device, process, fuel gas system, or drain, then the operating, pressure-release, and pressure-release-management requirements of §63.165 apply (including the <500 ppm operating level, post-release monitoring or rupture-disk replacement, and pressure-release management prohibitions/monitoring)

if equipment (including pressure relief devices) is intended to operate in organic HAP service 300 hours or more during the calendar year at a source subject to a specific subpart referencing subpart H, then subpart H's provisions apply to that equipment

candidates.title: General Provisions (Subpart A)

criteria.criterion: if you propose to use an alternative test method for a required performance test, then you must follow the Method 301 validation/notification procedures and obtain approval as provided in §63.7(f)

if you propose to use an alternative monitoring procedure or alternative monitoring method in lieu of monitoring specified by a relevant standard, then you must apply for and obtain Administrator approval under the alternative monitoring provisions in §63.8(f)

checklist: Is your plant/site a major source (PTE ≥10 tons/yr of any single HAP or ≥25 tons/yr combined HAP)?
Does your process unit produce a thermoplastic product such that it is designated a TPPU under Subpart JJJ (review the primary product/TPPU definitions)?
Are the portable containers considered storage vessels under §63.1312 (e.g., permanent, capacity ≥38 m3, not mobile equipment)?
Are the portable containers or their PRDs operating in organic HAP gas or vapor service (i.e., do the fluids contacting the equipment meet the subpart's organic HAP definition and concentrations)?
Do the pressure relief devices operate in organic HAP service for 300 or more hours per calendar year?

Are the pressure relief devices routed to a closed vent system that sends all releases to a control device, process, fuel gas system, or drain (which would exempt them from the direct PRD requirements)?
Do any PRDs consist of or include rupture disks (affects post-release actions and replacement requirements)?
How many portable containers/PRDs do you have (confirm the ~200–300 count) and are any containers mobile equipment (which may be exempt)?

Do you intend to use an alternative monitoring plan/procedure instead of the prescribed Method 21/monitoring—if so, are you prepared to submit an alternative-monitoring application per §63.8(f) and, if performance testing is required, a Method 301 validation per §63.7(f)?

If PRDs release to atmosphere, do you have means to detect/record/notify (rupture-disk indicators, sensors, pressure/flow monitors) and the process knowledge/data needed to calculate quantity of organic HAP released for reporting?

candidates.title: National Emission Standards for Hazardous Air Pollutants for Pulp and Paper (Subpart S)

criteria.criterion: If the owner or operator uses a control device, technique, or monitors a parameter other than those specified in § 63.453(b) through (l), then the owner or operator must install a continuous monitoring system and establish appropriate operating parameters to demonstrate continuous compliance to the Administrator's satisfaction.

If the owner or operator proposes to establish or reestablish monitoring parameter values for parameters required by § 63.453 (including those in paragraphs (b)–(j), (l), or (m)), then the owner or operator must record the operating parameter during the initial or subsequent performance test, develop the parameter values using the procedures in § 63.453(n), and provide the rationale and data to the Administrator for approval.

If the owner or operator intends to use an alternative test method or monitoring method to determine total HAP or methanol concentrations (in vent gas or liquid streams), then the alternative method must be demonstrated to the Administrator's satisfaction (i.e., be an approved alternative) per the authorities in § 63.457 that allow ‘any other method’ demonstrated acceptable to the Administrator.

candidates.title: General Provisions (Subpart A)

criteria.criterion: If an owner or operator wishes to use an alternative monitoring procedure (including alternative monitoring parameters or an alternative CMS procedure), then the owner or operator must submit an application to the Administrator that describes the proposed alternative (addressing the elements of monitoring) and includes a performance evaluation test plan and justification, and the alternative monitoring may not be used until the Administrator approves it.

If an owner or operator wishes to use an alternative test method for performance testing, then the owner or operator must notify the Administrator (at least 60 days before the test), validate the alternative method using Method 301, submit validation results, and comply with the approval/notification provisions in § 63.7(f) (including the Administrator's review timeline and conditions to proceed).

candidates.title: National Emission Standards for Hazardous Air Pollutants for Major Sources: Kraft and Soda Recovery Furnaces, Lime Kilns, and Other Combustion Units (Subpart MM)

criteria.criterion: If the owner or operator of an affected kraft recovery furnace or other process unit subject to this subpart wishes to monitor alternative control device operating parameters instead of the specified CPMS/COMS parameters, then the owner or operator must obtain prior written approval from the Administrator and submit the alternative monitoring request describing the control device, proposed parameters, how limits are to be set, and the monitoring approach.

If the Administrator approves an alternative monitoring request under this subpart, then the owner or operator must install, calibrate, operate, and maintain the monitor(s) in accordance with the monitoring plan approved by the Administrator and must include proposed performance specifications and QA procedures as part of the submittal.

checklist: Confirm that the kraft pulping system at your Mississippi facility is an affected source under Subpart S and identify which specific equipment/systems are subject (e.g., bleach plant vents, oxygen delignification vents, condensate streams, steam strippers, recovery furnace).

List each emission point and its current control device (e.g., thermal oxidizer, RTO, scrubber, steam stripper, open biological treatment, ESP, wet scrubber) and whether each device is operated per the monitoring parameters specified in Subpart S (temperature, pH, flow rates, methanol/HAP concentration, BOD5, etc.).

Decide which monitoring parameter(s) or test methods you propose to replace or augment (e.g., methanol outlet concentration vs. steam/flow/temp; alternative condensate HAP measurement method; alternate scrubber parameter).

Collect recent and representative performance test data (initial performance test or most recent repeat test) showing the relationship between the proposed alternative parameter(s) and compliance with the applicable emission/treatment standard.

Prepare a site-specific monitoring plan and performance evaluation test plan documenting: description of the control technique, the proposed alternative monitors/parameters, supporting test data, rationale that the alternative provides equivalent or better assurance of compliance, proposed operating limits, averaging times, and QA/QC procedures.
For any alternative performance test method: document Method 301 validation (or plan to perform it) and be prepared to provide the 60-day pre-test notice to the Administrator per § 63.7(f).

For condensate or wastewater HAP measurements: verify which analyte basis is required (e.g., methanol for kraft condensates per § 63.457(g)) and whether you will use an accepted test method or must demonstrate an alternative method to the Administrator.

If the proposed alternative involves recovery furnace or wet-scrubber parameters, document the proposed performance specifications, calibration procedures, accuracy tolerances, and QA program consistent with Subpart MM expectations.

Identify whether any affected biological treatment systems are non-thoroughly mixed (if applicable) and assemble monitoring and archived sampling procedures (BOD5, mixed liquor VSS, inlet/outlet HAP samples) required to support excursions/performance tests under Subpart S.

Confirm the timing of submissions: prepare to submit the alternative monitoring application and supporting data early enough to obtain Administrator approval prior to using the alternative for the compliance demonstration or prior to the scheduled performance test (coordinate with required 60-day notices where applicable).

judge_text: {"score":2,"reason":"EPA's note that the alternative monitoring procedure is approved only under specific conditions is captured: the response cites Subpart A (requirement to submit alternative monitoring for Administrator approval and Method 301/60‑day notice), Subpart S (must demonstrate alternatives to the Administrator's satisfaction and establish parameters per §63.453(n)), and Subpart MM (prior written approval and adherence to approved monitoring plan), which together cover the conditional approval elements referenced by the EPA note."}

candidates.title: General Provisions

criteria.criterion: If the owner or operator of an existing affected source is unable to comply with a relevant standard because additional time is necessary for installation of controls, then the owner or operator may request up to a one-year extension of compliance for installation of controls.

If the owner or operator submits a nonfrivolous request for an extension of compliance no later than 120 days prior to the affected source's compliance date (or later if the need arose after that date due to circumstances beyond reasonable control and before the compliance date), then the request will stay the applicability of the rule as to the emission points in question until the request is granted or denied.

If an owner or operator requests an extension of compliance under this paragraph, then the request must include a description of the controls to be installed and a compliance schedule with dates for contract/order award, start of on-site construction/installation, completion of on-site construction/installation, and final compliance.

candidates.title: Lime Manufacturing (Subpart AAAAA)

criteria.criterion: If your facility contains an affected source subject to subpart AAAAA, then the compliance date applicable to your source is the date specified in § 63.7083 for your category (new or existing affected source) and that is the deadline for any extension request under § 63.6(i).

If a COMS is required for monitoring an add-on air pollution control device for your lime kiln under this subpart, then you must install the COMS at the outlet of the control device and install, maintain, calibrate, and operate the COMS as required by Subpart A and PS-1 of appendix B to part 60.

If you operate an existing lime kiln and one of the conditions in § 63.7121(f)(1) through (3) exists (positive-pressure FF with multiple stacks, control device exhausts through a monovent, or installation of a COMS per PS-1 is infeasible), then you may perform visual emissions (VE) checks in accordance with Method 9 in lieu of installing a COMS or PM detector.

candidates.title: Monitoring Requirements for Kraft/Soda Recovery Furnaces and Lime Kilns (Subpart MM)

criteria.criterion: If you operate a lime kiln equipped with an ESP that is an affected source under Subpart MM, then you must install, calibrate, maintain, and operate a COMS in accordance with PS-1 and the provisions of § 63.6(h), § 63.8, and § 63.864(d).

If a COMS is required under this section, then each COMS must complete at least one cycle of sampling and analyzing every 10 seconds and one cycle of data recording for each successive 6-minute period, and each 6-minute average must be calculated from 36 or more equally spaced data points as specified.

candidates.title: Extension and Monitoring Alternatives Procedures (Subpart YY)

criteria.criterion: If you are an existing source subject to Subpart YY and you are unable to comply with a section 112(d) standard because additional time is necessary to install controls, then you may request an extension of up to one additional year to comply.

If you request an extension under Subpart YY, then for sources not including emission points in an emissions average you must submit the extension request not later than 12 months before the compliance date (or 18 months before the compliance date if including emission points in an emissions average).

If you request an extension under Subpart YY, then the request must include the description of controls, a compliance schedule with milestone dates, a description of interim emission control steps during the extension, and whether you are also requesting extensions of other applicable requirements.

checklist: Determine whether your facility and specific kilns are an "affected source" under 40 CFR part 63 Subpart AAAAA (lime manufacturing) and identify whether each kiln is a new or existing affected source.
Identify the applicable compliance date for each affected kiln per 40 CFR 63.7083 (existing vs new and any subcategory-specific dates).
Confirm whether each kiln is controlled by an ESP or other add-on control device and whether a COMS is required under Subpart AAAAA § 63.7113(g) and/or Subpart MM § 63.864(d).
If a COMS exists, record the installation date and whether it was installed on or before February 6, 2001 (to determine grandfathering referenced in § 63.7113(g)(2)).

If COMS installation is not yet complete, prepare a detailed description of the controls/COMS to be installed and a compliance schedule with milestone dates (contracts/orders, on-site start, on-site completion, and final compliance date) as required by 40 CFR 63.6(i)(6)(i).
Verify whether any conditions of § 63.7121(f)(1)–(3) apply that would allow visual emissions (VE) checks in lieu of installing a COMS for existing lime kilns.
Decide which authority to submit the extension request to (EPA Administrator or State permitting authority if State has an approved part 70 program) and confirm any state-specific timing rules.

Check the applicable subpart deadline for submitting an extension request (generally no later than 120 days before the compliance date per 40 CFR 63.6(i)(4)(i)(B); note Subpart YY may require 12 or 18 months before the compliance date per 40 CFR 63.1112).

Assemble supporting materials for the extension request: control description, milestones/schedule, interim control steps and milestones to assure protection of health, statement whether waiver of performance testing or other waivers are also requested, and any justification why the need arose after the standard submittal deadline (if applicable).

Prepare or update the OM&M plan and the startup, shutdown, and malfunction plan (SSMP) per 40 CFR 63.7100(d) and 63.6(e)(3), and include procedures for installation, operation, calibration, and QA of the COMS in the plan.

Confirm technical specifications for the COMS to be installed (PS-1 compliance, 10-second sampling cycles, 6-minute averaging with 36+ points) per Subpart MM § 63.864(d) and Subpart A §§ 63.7113(g) and 63.8.

Decide whether to request any related waivers (e.g., waiver of initial performance test) and, if so, include the waiver request with the extension application in accordance with 40 CFR 63.7(h) and subpart procedures.

Document whether the need for an extension arose due to circumstances beyond your control (force majeure or late discovery) and the date you first learned of those problems if submitting after the standard deadline per 40 CFR 63.6(i)(4)(i)(C).
Plan for interim emission management steps during the extension period to assure protection of health and compliance with any conditions the Administrator may impose while the extension is in effect.

judge_text: {"score":1,"reason":"The EPA’s key rationale—that a COMS is monitoring equipment (not an add-on control) so the §63.6(i) extension for installation of controls does not apply—is only partially reflected. The answer cites the extension authority as limited to installation of “controls,” but it fails to state or apply the explicit rule/interpretation that COMS are monitoring devices excluded from that ‘‘installation of controls’’ extension, so the EPA’s decisive reasoning is not captured."}

candidates.title: National Emission Standards for Hazardous Air Pollutants: Phosphate Fertilizers Production Plants (Subpart BB)

criteria.criterion: If you own or operate a phosphate fertilizer production plant that is a major source, then the requirements of Subpart BB apply to your affected sources (process lines, storage buildings, evaporative cooling towers).

If you use a continuous monitoring system (CMS) to demonstrate compliance, then you must develop and keep a site-specific monitoring plan and conduct CMS performance evaluations in accordance with that plan.

If a performance test is required for an affected source, then the CMS performance evaluation must be conducted during the performance test (i.e., concurrently with the performance test) unless an alternative is approved by the Administrator.

If you use a control device to comply with the emission limits and monitor operating parameters with a CPMS, then you must establish the operating parameter value(s) (and allowable ranges) using the arithmetic average of operating parameter measurements recorded during the three test runs of the most recent performance test unless an alternative methodology is applied and approved.

candidates.title: General Provisions (Subpart A of Part 63)

criteria.criterion: If a relevant standard requires performance testing, then you must perform the performance test within 180 days of the applicable compliance date unless a waiver or extension is granted.

If you intend to conduct a performance test, then you must notify the Administrator in writing at least 60 calendar days before the performance test is initially scheduled to begin (to allow review/observer attendance).

If a CMS performance evaluation is required, then you must provide a site-specific performance evaluation test plan to the Administrator (upon request) at least 60 days before the performance evaluation is scheduled to begin and conduct the evaluation in accordance with §63.8(e).

If you wish to use an alternative monitoring method or alternative procedure for a performance evaluation, then you must submit an application describing the alternative and a performance evaluation/test plan at least 60 days before the performance evaluation (or as otherwise specified) for Administrator review and approval.

candidates.title: Extensions, waivers, and alternatives (Subpart YY, §63.1112)

criteria.criterion: If you request a waiver of an individual performance test, then you must apply in writing and the Administrator may waive the test if, in the Administrator's judgment, the source is meeting the relevant standard(s) on a continuous basis (or other stated conditions are met).

If you wish to use an alternative monitoring method, then you must submit a written application that includes a description of the proposed alternative and a performance evaluation test plan (if required), and the Administrator will notify approval or intention to deny within the timeframes specified.

checklist: Verify whether the facility is a major source (40 CFR 63.620(a); 40 CFR 63.2 definition of major source).
Identify which affected sources are present (phosphate fertilizer process lines, granular triple superphosphate process lines, storage buildings, evaporative cooling towers) (40 CFR 63.620(b)).
Determine whether the scrubbers to be performance-evaluated are monitored by a CMS or CPMS for compliance (40 CFR 63.628(c); 40 CFR 63.625(d)).
Confirm whether an approved site-specific monitoring plan exists on site and whether it contains the schedule for initial and subsequent CMS performance evaluations (40 CFR 63.628(c)(2) and (3)).

Check the date of the next required performance test and whether the Administrator received written notification at least 60 days before (or whether the site-specific test plan was submitted in time) (40 CFR 63.7(b)(1); 40 CFR 63.7(c)(4)(iv)).
Confirm whether the CMS performance evaluation is currently scheduled to be conducted during the performance test (concurrently) as required (40 CFR 63.8(e)(4); 40 CFR 63.626(h)).

If you plan to conduct the CMS performance evaluation on a different day (e.g., within a five-day window prior to the performance test), prepare an application for an alternative monitoring method and/or a request for approval of an alternative schedule and note submission timing (at least 60 days prior to the performance evaluation) (40 CFR 63.8(f)(4)(i); 40 CFR 63.7(f)(2)(i); 40 CFR 63.1112(c)(4)(i)).

Assemble the proposed alternative monitoring/performance-evaluation test plan contents and QA/QC documentation to support representativeness and data quality (site-specific performance evaluation test plan elements per 40 CFR 63.8(e)(3)(i) and site-specific monitoring plan contents per 40 CFR 63.628(c)(1)(ii)-(v)).

Confirm whether any CPMS operating limits were established from the arithmetic average of the three performance-test runs or whether an alternative methodology is claimed (40 CFR 63.625(d)(1)(i) and (ii)(A)-(B)).

Ensure records of prior site-specific monitoring plans, performance evaluations, and performance test reports are kept on site and available for inspection for the required retention periods (40 CFR 63.628(c)(3); 40 CFR 63.7(g)(3); 40 CFR 63.627(c)).
If seeking a waiver of the performance test instead of scheduling changes, prepare a waiver application with justification and submit according to the timelines in 40 CFR 63.1112(b)(3).

judge_text: {"score":2,"reason":"Yes. The answer includes the statutory basis for requesting an alternative (need to apply for Administrator approval), the requirement to submit a site‑specific performance evaluation/test plan and QA/QC documentation, the 60‑day submission/timing provisions, and that an alternative may be approved or denied — which captures the EPA’s key point that the alternative monitoring plan can be approved conditionally with specific requirements."}

candidates.title: Phosphate Fertilizer Production Plants (Subpart BB)

criteria.criterion: If your facility includes a phosphate fertilizer process line (e.g., diammonium and/or monoammonium phosphate process line) or granular triple superphosphate process line subject to Subpart BB, then you must install, calibrate, maintain, and operate a continuous monitoring system (CMS) with an accuracy of ±5 percent over its operating range that determines and permanently records the mass flow of phosphorus-bearing material fed to the process.

If your facility is subject to Subpart BB, then you must maintain a daily record of equivalent P2O5 feed calculated by determining the total mass rate of phosphorus-bearing feed using the procedures in §63.626(f)(3).

If you use a CMS to demonstrate compliance under Subpart BB, then you must develop and keep on-site a site-specific monitoring plan that documents probe/location justification, performance and equipment specifications, performance evaluation procedures, O&M, QA/QC, and recordkeeping/reporting procedures.

If installation or use of the CMS specified by this subpart would not provide accurate measurements due to liquid water, scaling, or other interferences, then you may request alternative monitoring requirements and must apply to the Administrator for approval of an alternative monitoring procedure per the procedures in §63.8(f).

If you seek an alternative to the monitoring requirements or other major monitoring changes under Subpart BB, then approval of alternatives to the requirements in §§63.620, 63.622, 63.625, 63.629, and 63.631 is retained by the Administrator (i.e., EPA authority to approve such alternatives is not delegable).

candidates.title: General Provisions (Subpart A)

criteria.criterion: If a relevant subpart requires a CMS, then the general CMS provisions in §63.8 apply, including CMS operation/maintenance, quality control program, and performance evaluation requirements.

If you wish to use an alternative monitoring procedure in lieu of a monitoring method specified by a relevant standard, then you must submit a written application containing the description of the alternative and a performance evaluation test plan (if required) and follow the submission timing requirements in §63.8(f)(4).

If you submit a request for an alternative monitoring procedure, then the Administrator will notify you of approval or intent to deny within 30 days after receipt of the request and any supplementary information (or approval of minor changes may be made via the site-specific plan).

If a CMS is required and you use it, then you must conduct a CMS performance evaluation per §63.8(e) and keep the performance evaluation plan and QA procedures on-site as part of your quality control program.

candidates.title: Wet-process Phosphoric Acid and Related Processes (Subpart AA)

criteria.criterion: If your facility includes a wet-process phosphoric acid process line or superphosphoric acid process line subject to Subpart AA, then you must install, calibrate, maintain, and operate a CMS with an accuracy of ±5 percent over its operating range that determines and permanently records the mass flow of phosphorus-bearing material fed to the process.

If your process is subject to Subpart AA, then you must maintain a daily record of equivalent P2O5 feed calculated by determining the total mass rate of phosphorus-bearing feed using the CMS and the procedures in §63.606(f)(3).

If you use a CMS under Subpart AA, then you must conduct a CMS performance evaluation consistent with §63.8(e) and include CMS QA/QC and bag-leak detection evaluations as specified in §63.606(m) and §63.605(f)/(g) where applicable.

If installation of the specified CMS would not provide accurate measurements due to interferences such as liquid water or severe scaling, then you may request alternative monitoring requirements under §63.8(f) and must follow the application and approval steps in §63.8(f)(4)-(5).

checklist: Identify which process lines are present at the site (e.g., diammonium/monoammonium phosphate process lines, granular triple superphosphate process or storage, wet-process phosphoric acid lines, phosphate rock dryer/calciner).
For each process line, verify whether it is an affected source subject to Subpart BB or Subpart AA (and whether it is existing or new as defined in §63.621/§63.2).

Document the current monitoring equipment used to determine phosphorus-bearing mass flow (device type, model, installation location) and whether it currently operates as a CMS per the relevant subpart(s).
Verify the documented accuracy of your flow/feeding measurement system (does it meet ±5% over operating range as required by §63.625(a)(1) / §63.605(a)(1)?).
Record evidence of measurement interferences (e.g., frequency/severity of magnetic flowmeter scaling, instances of inaccurate readings, maintenance records showing cleaning frequency and downtime).

Confirm whether you have an existing site-specific monitoring plan on-site that meets §63.628(c) (probe location justification, equipment specs, performance evaluation schedule, QA/QC, O&M, recordkeeping/reporting).

If you intend to use an alternative monitoring procedure, prepare application materials per §63.8(f)(4): description of the alternative monitoring system addressing the four elements of monitoring and a performance evaluation test plan (and submit at least 60 days before the CMS performance evaluation if the alternative will serve as the performance test).
Establish timing: note upcoming performance test dates and ensure 60-calendar-day notifications to the Administrator per §63.7(b) and CMS performance-evaluation scheduling per §63.8(e)(3).

Determine whether control devices or combined emissions streams are present that affect probe placement or monitoring approach and document representation/justification for measurement location per §63.628(c)(1)(i).

Check whether EPA or a delegated state/local authority implements/enforces the subpart for your facility (contact regional office) per §63.632(a) and identify the correct contact for submitting alternative-monitoring requests or site-specific plans.

candidates.title: Standards for Catalytic Cracking Units (metal and organic HAPs)

criteria.criterion: If you operate a catalytic cracking unit (FCCU) you must meet the emission limitations and site-specific operating limits in this subpart and install/operate monitoring per the subpart (e.g., CPMS/COMS/CEMS) to demonstrate compliance.

If your FCCU is controlled using a wet scrubber and you seek to change monitoring parameters or use alternative parameters, you must request Administrator approval and include the information specified in §63.1573(f).

If your FCCU regenerator vent is subject to the NSPS PM limit at 40 CFR 60.102(a)(1) and you have Administrator-approved alternative monitoring for the NSPS COMS, you may request alternative monitoring under this subpart using the provisions in §63.1573(g).

If you use continuous parameter monitoring systems and establish operating limits based on a performance test, you must base the CPMS operating limits on the performance test results and you may adjust monitored values only as allowed in §63.1571(d) and change limits only following §63.1571(e) (additional performance test or engineering assessment).

If you use an alternative (noncontinuous) procedure for monitoring pressure drop on certain wet scrubbers (jet ejector or atomizing nozzles), you may perform daily pressure checks and related recordkeeping instead of a CPMS per §63.1573(b).

If you modify your operation, maintenance, or monitoring plan or established operating limits, you must submit the plan and required notifications (e.g., Notification of Compliance Status) and include required plan elements per §63.1574(f).

candidates.title: General Provisions

criteria.criterion: If you want to use an alternative monitoring method or minor/intermediate/major change to monitoring, you must apply to the Administrator with the information required in §63.8(f)(4) and may not use the alternative until approval procedures in §63.8(f)(5) are satisfied.

If your affected source is required to conduct performance testing, you must notify and conduct tests in accordance with the performance testing requirements of §63.7 (site-specific plan, notifications, timing, QA), and retain test records per §63.7(g).

If you install and operate any CMS (COMS, CEMS, CPMS) you must install, operate, maintain, and perform QA/QC per the general CMS requirements in §63.8 (including operational frequency, out-of-control procedures, and quality control program).

candidates.title: Changing compliance levels of monitored parameters

criteria.criterion: If you wish to change control device or process operating parameter levels established during performance tests, you must notify the Administrator of your desire and, upon approval, conduct additional performance tests at the proposed new levels before operating at those levels.

candidates.title: General monitoring requirements for control and recovery devices

criteria.criterion: If your control device is subject to monitoring under a referencing subpart, monitoring must be conducted as set forth in that subpart unless the Administrator approves minor methodological changes or alternatives as provided in §63.996(b) or (d).

If you use CPMS for control devices, you must install, calibrate, maintain, and operate monitoring equipment according to manufacturer specifications or written procedures providing adequate assurance of accurate monitoring and maintain parts/maintenance per §63.996(c)(1)-(2).

If you will establish a monitored-parameter range indicating proper operation (i.e., revised parametric limits), you must provide the information required in §63.999(b)(3) in your Notification of Compliance Status or operating permit application as required by §63.996(c)(6).

checklist: Is the FCCU (catalytic cracking unit) at your facility an affected source under Subpart UUU?
Is the FCCU catalyst regenerator vent controlled by a wet scrubber (wet gas scrubber)?
Is the regenerator vent subject to the NSPS PM limit at 40 CFR 60.102(a)(1) (i.e., NSPS applicability)?
Do you already have Administrator-approved alternative monitoring requirements under the NSPS (e.g., for COMS per 40 CFR 60.105)?

Which monitoring systems are currently installed on the wet scrubber/regenerator vent (CPMS/COMS/CEMS) and which parameters are they measuring (pressure drop, liquid-to-gas ratio, gas flow, pH, CO, opacity, etc.)?
Are your current CPMS/COMS/CEMS installed, operated, and maintained per manufacturer specs and the CMS requirements in 40 CFR part 63 (e.g., calibration/QA records)?
Were your existing parametric operating limits established from a performance test, and do you propose to change those limits (if so, document original performance-test values and rationale)?
Do you have an approved Operation, Maintenance, and Monitoring plan (OM&M) per §63.1574(f) that lists monitored parameters and operating limits?

Will you submit a request to the Administrator (or permitting authority in Texas) to approve alternative monitoring or changed operating limits, and can you provide the information required in §63.1573(f) and/or §63.8(f)(4)?
Who is the permitting authority for your facility (State of Texas agency vs. EPA Region), and will you need to coordinate approval/notifications with them as required in the subpart?

candidates.title: National Emission Standards for Hazardous Air Pollutants for Steel Pickling and Hydrochloric Acid Regeneration Plants (Subpart CCC)

criteria.criterion: If the facility is a new, reconstructed, or existing steel pickling facility or acid regeneration plant, then the owner or operator must install, operate, and maintain systems for continuous measurement and recording of the scrubber makeup water flow rate (and recirculation water flow rate, if applicable) while the scrubber is operating.

If a wet scrubber is used to achieve compliance, then during the performance test the owner or operator must establish site-specific operating parameter values for the minimum scrubber makeup water flow rate (and minimum recirculation flow rate for scrubbers that recirculate) which become the basis for ongoing monitoring and corrective action if excursions occur.

If the owner or operator seeks to use an alternative monitoring approach in place of the required makeup water flow rate monitoring, then such alternative monitoring requirements may be developed and implemented only with approval by the Administrator.

candidates.title: General Provisions (Subpart A)

criteria.criterion: If an owner or operator wishes to use an alternative monitoring procedure for a CMS or other monitoring required by a relevant subpart, then they must apply to the Administrator for approval under the alternative monitoring provisions and, until approval is granted, remain subject to the existing monitoring requirements.

If the alternative monitoring procedure will serve as or be used during a performance test to demonstrate compliance, then the owner or operator must follow the alternative test/method validation and submittal requirements and timing for alternative methods under the performance testing provisions.

If requesting approval to use an alternative monitoring procedure, then the application must include a description addressing the monitoring elements (indicator(s) of performance, measurement techniques, monitoring frequency, averaging time) and, if required, a performance evaluation test plan.

candidates.title: Monitoring Installation, Operation, and Maintenance Requirements (Subpart NNNNN)

criteria.criterion: If you are required by the referencing subpart to monitor one or more operating parameters with a CMS, then you must install, operate, and maintain each CMS according to the CMS data collection, sampling frequency, data validation, averaging, and recordkeeping requirements specified in §63.9025(a).

If you seek to monitor parameters other than those specified for scrubber control devices under the referencing subpart, then you must request approval in accordance with §63.8(f) and submit a monitoring plan that (1) identifies the operating parameter, (2) explains why it is appropriate to demonstrate compliance, and (3) identifies the specific monitoring procedures.

candidates.title: Control Device Continuous Parameter Monitoring and Alternatives for Process Vents (Subpart HHHHHHH)

criteria.criterion: If you are using an absorber or acid gas scrubber to meet an emission limit that requires CPMS, then you must install and operate either a liquid flow meter (and optionally gas flow) or other specified devices and, if the scrubbing liquid is a reactant, you may use a conductivity monitoring device to monitor scrubber liquid effluent.

If you are required to use the CPMS specified in this subpart but wish to use alternative monitoring parameters or procedures, then you may request approval to use alternatives under the procedures in §63.11985 and §63.8, and until permission is granted you remain subject to the subpart's monitoring requirements.

checklist: Confirm whether your facility is an affected source under Subpart CCC (steel pickling facility or hydrochloric acid regeneration plant).
Confirm whether the emission control for the pickle line is a wet scrubber used to achieve compliance (and whether it uses recirculation).

Confirm current scrubber monitoring: whether makeup water flow rate (and recirculation flow rate) are monitored continuously and recorded (frequency, instrumentation accuracy, manufacturer certification).
Record the minimum scrubber makeup water flow and recirculation flow values established during the most recent performance test (or plan to reestablish them during the next performance test).

Determine whether the scrubbing liquid is a reactant (e.g., caustic or other reactive scrubbing media) or plain water, since some subparts allow conductivity monitoring when the scrubbing liquid is a reactant.

Prepare a technical demonstration linking conductivity measurements to the parameter required by Subpart CCC (show correlation to makeup water flow or to control performance), including test data, supporting calculations, and proposed operating limits derived from performance tests.

Assemble an alternative monitoring application/plan per §63.8(f) that: (a) describes the affected source and parameter(s), (b) explains why conductivity is appropriate, (c) provides methods and procedures to demonstrate the parameter's adequacy (performance evaluation plan), (d) specifies monitoring, recording, and reporting frequency and averaging time, and (e) includes supporting calculations and QA/QC procedures.

If the alternative monitoring will be used in or as the basis for performance testing, prepare to validate any alternative test method per Method 301 and submit at least 60 days before the performance evaluation as required.

Identify the permitting authority (EPA or State) to which the alternative monitoring request and monitoring plan will be submitted, and confirm any state/title V permit implications or additional approval requirements.

Ensure proposed monitoring system meets CMS data requirements if applicable (e.g., data collection frequency, minimum valid-data percent, hourly/daily averaging and recordkeeping per §63.9025(a) or relevant CMS provisions).

Verify instrumentation specifications and calibration plan (manufacturer accuracy, calibration frequency, QA/QC, and startup/shutdown/malfunction plan) to satisfy Subpart A and the referencing subpart requirements.

candidates.title: Polyvinyl Chloride Production Unit (PVCPU) process vents — CPMS for scrubbers

criteria.criterion: If you use an absorber or acid gas scrubber to meet an emission limit in Table 1 or 2 to this subpart and are required to use CPMS under §63.11925(c), then you must install and operate monitoring for the scrubber (including pressure gauges at the inlet and outlet to monitor pressure drop) unless an alternative monitoring parameter is approved.

If you request approval to monitor a different CPMS parameter (for example, substitute ambient pressure for outlet pressure) or to set unique monitoring parameters, then you must request approval under the procedures in this subpart and §63.8 and may not use the alternative until the Administrator (or authorized representative) approves it.

If you must establish operating limits for monitored parameters for a process vent control device, then those operating limits must be based on values recorded during a performance test demonstrating compliance (supplemented by engineering assessment or manufacturer recommendations) and submitted in the notification of compliance status.

candidates.title: General Provisions — alternative monitoring, performance testing, and Administrator authority

criteria.criterion: If you wish to use an alternative monitoring procedure or monitor an alternative parameter, then you must apply to the Administrator per the alternative-monitoring procedures in §63.8(f) and may not implement the alternative for compliance until approval is granted.

If the permitting/approval authority has been delegated to a State or other authorized representative, then Administrator-level approvals or reviews referenced in the alternative-monitoring and testing procedures may be performed by the Administrator's authorized representative.

checklist: Confirm the scrubber is an absorber or acid gas scrubber used to meet an emission limit in Table 1 or 2 of Subpart HHHHHHH (i.e., is within the PVCPU affected-source scope).
Verify whether the scrubber is subject to CPMS requirements under §63.11925(c) (i.e., CPMS is required for that control device).
Document which CPMS parameter(s) are currently required for that scrubber (specifically whether pressure-drop monitoring by inlet/outlet pressure gauges is required under §63.11940(c)(2)(i)).

Prepare a written description of the proposed alternative parameter (ambient pressure substituted for measured outlet pressure) including engineering rationale showing how ambient pressure will provide an equivalent indicator of pressure drop or scrubber performance.

Assemble performance-test data and calculations from the control-device performance test(s) that demonstrate the control device met the applicable emission limit under the operating conditions used to set monitoring limits (these data form the basis for the operating limit per §63.11935(d)(1)).

Develop a site-specific monitoring plan addressing monitoring design, sample location, QA/QC, data collection, frequency, averaging, accuracy, calibration, and the proposed operating limit(s) as required by §63.11935(c) and §63.11935(d).

Confirm monitoring equipment capabilities meet general CPMS requirements (capable of recording at least once every 15 minutes and measuring over a range extending at least 20% beyond normal operating range per §63.11935(c)(2) and (c)(6)).

Prepare the information required for a request to monitor alternative parameters per §63.11985(c)(5) (description of parameter, methods to demonstrate parameter indicates proper operation, schedule for demonstration, and statement to establish operating limits) and per §63.11985(c)(4) if submitting prior to initial notification.

Identify the correct approval recipient (EPA or delegated State/local authorized representative) and include documentation of any prior similar approval (the Texas prior approval) to support rationale and consistency; confirm whether the prior approval was issued by the Administrator or the delegated State authority.

Confirm that you will not implement the substitute ambient-pressure monitoring for compliance until the Administrator (or authorized representative) approves the alternative monitoring method in writing, and plan to continue required existing monitoring until approval is granted.

Specify the proposed calibration, accuracy, and maintenance schedule for the ambient-pressure measurement and any calculations used to derive pressure drop, ensuring these meet the CPMS QA/QC expectations in §63.11935(c)(1) and §63.8(c).

Prepare to include the established operating limit(s), rationale and supporting data/calculations, and monitoring plan in your Notification of Compliance Status or Title V permit application as required by §63.11935(d)(2) and §63.11985(a)(4).

Verify data reduction and averaging approach (CPMS data recorded at ≥15-minute frequency, reduced to required averaging periods per §63.11935(e) and §63.8(g) where applicable) so the proposed parameter will support required compliance calculations.

candidates.title: Polymerization and monomer recovery for acrylonitrile (AN) — standards and compliance requirements

criteria.criterion: If you operate polymerization process equipment or monomer recovery process equipment that collect AN and use a wet scrubber as the control device, then you must operate and maintain capture/enclosure and a CPMS that measures and records the wet scrubber water flow rate at least every 15 minutes and determines the daily average.

If the daily average water flow rate to a wet scrubber used to control polymerization process equipment is below 50 l/min (or below 30 l/min for a wet scrubber used to control monomer recovery equipment), then you are not meeting the subpart's wet scrubber operating limits and must take the actions (monthly determination, quarterly summary reporting, and written notification of exceedance) specified by the subpart.

If you do not use a wet scrubber control device for the polymerization or monomer recovery process equipment, then you must submit a monitoring plan to EPA (or delegated authority) that includes a device description, performance test results (per §63.1104 of subpart YY), an O&M and CPMS plan, the list of operating parameters to be monitored, and proposed operating parameter limits.

candidates.title: General monitoring requirements for control and recovery devices (Subpart SS)

criteria.criterion: If you are the owner or operator of a regulated source required to monitor under this subpart, then monitoring shall be conducted as set forth in this section and the referencing subpart unless the Administrator specifies or approves minor methodology changes or approves alternatives to any monitoring requirements or procedures.

If you seek alternatives to the continuous operating parameter monitoring or to monitor different parameters than those listed, then you may request approval as provided in paragraph (d) of this section and the Administrator may grant approval pursuant to the procedures referenced in this section.

candidates.title: Process vent monitoring requirements (Subpart PPP)

criteria.criterion: If you use an absorber/scrubber to comply with the process vent control requirements in this subpart, then you must install and operate a scrubbing liquid flow rate meter or a pressure monitoring device (with continuous recorder) and, if an acid or base absorbent is used, a pH monitoring device for the scrubber effluent.

If you want to monitor parameters other than those listed for the combustion, recovery, or recapture devices in paragraph (a), then you must request approval to monitor alternative parameters as specified in paragraph (b) and submit the request per the referenced process vent reporting/alternative-parameter procedures.

candidates.title: General provisions — monitoring and alternative monitoring procedures (Subpart A)

criteria.criterion: If you wish to use an alternative monitoring procedure (minor, intermediate, or major change) in place of a monitoring method specified in a relevant subpart, then you must submit an application to the Administrator describing the proposed alternative, the monitoring plan/performance evaluation plan, and justification per §63.8(f) (and follow the submission/timing requirements in §63.7 where the alternative is used for performance testing).

If permission to use an alternative monitoring procedure has not been granted by the Administrator, then the affected source remains subject to the monitoring requirements of the relevant standard and this part until approval is received.

checklist: Is the facility an affected source for acrylonitrile polymerization/monomer recovery subject to Subpart LLLLLL (i.e., polymerization or monomer recovery equipment that emits AN)?
Which control device(s) route polymerization and solvent recovery emissions (wet scrubber, absorber, condenser, carbon adsorber, incinerator, etc.) and which process vents are routed to each device?
If you use a wet scrubber for AN control: is there a CPMS installed that measures and records wet scrubber water (liquid) flow rate at least every 15 minutes and calculates daily averages?
What are the measured daily average water flow rates for each wet scrubber (document monthly determinations) and do any fall below 50 l/min for polymerization or 30 l/min for monomer recovery?

If not using a wet scrubber for any AN control point, do you have (or plan to prepare) the monitoring plan elements required by §63.11395(i) (device description, performance-test data per §63.1104 subpart YY, O&M and CPMS plan, list of parameters, operating limits)?
What is the scrubbing liquid chemistry (is the scrubbing liquid an acid, base, or reactant) and does that trigger pH or caustic/ conductivity monitoring per the applicable subpart?
Have you performed a performance test for the control device(es) (date, methods used, and whether results support alternative operating limits per subpart LLLLLL(k))?

Do you intend to monitor a different parameter (e.g., pressure drop, liquid flow vs L/G ratio, pH strips vs CPMS, or an organic monitoring device) than the subpart-specified parameter for your scrubber, and can you prepare the application (description, demonstration method, QA/QC, averaging time, operating limit) required by §63.8(f) and the referencing subpart?

Do you have existing monitoring quality assurance/operation & maintenance procedures and spare parts to support continuous monitoring as required by the relevant subparts (installation, calibration, QA, response to out-of-control conditions)?
Are you prepared to follow the Administrator approval timelines and to continue existing required monitoring until any alternative monitoring procedure is explicitly approved?

candidates.title: NESHAP for Taconite Iron Ore Processing (Subpart RRRRR)

criteria.criterion: If you operate a dynamic wet scrubber to meet any particulate matter emission limit in Table 1 to this subpart, then you are subject to operating limits requiring maintenance of the daily average scrubber water flow rate and the daily average fan amperage (or prior to certain dates, fan amperage or pressure drop) at or above minimum levels established during the initial performance test.

If you are subject to the dynamic wet scrubber operating limits, then you must establish site-specific operating limits by measuring and recording scrubber water flow rate and fan amperage every 15 minutes during each performance test run and setting the operating limits as the lowest average scrubber water flow rate and lowest average fan amperage corresponding to any of the three test runs (subject to specified exceptions).

If a dynamic wet scrubber is subject to the operating limits in §63.9590(b)(2), then you must install, operate, and maintain a continuous parameter monitoring system (CPMS) and monitor the daily average scrubber water flow rate and daily average fan amperage according to the CPMS and monitoring requirements.

If the daily average scrubber water flow rate or daily average fan amperage for a dynamic wet scrubber is below the operating limits established during the initial or subsequent performance test, then you must follow the corrective action procedures required for dynamic wet scrubbers.

candidates.title: Wet Scrubber Operating Limits and Test Procedures (Subpart TTTTT)

criteria.criterion: If you set minimum fan-amperage based operating limits for a dynamic (or similar) wet scrubber under that subpart's test-based operating-limit procedures, then you may set the minimum percent full load amperage (PFLA) to the fan motor as the percent of full load amperage under no-load plus 10 percent, with the no-load amperage determined from manufacturer specifications or by a no-load test.

If you establish operating limits during the performance test for a wet scrubber subject to pressure drop and scrubber liquid flow rate limits, then you must measure and record those parameters at least every 15 minutes during each run and set the operating limits as the lowest average 1-hour (or run) values associated with runs that meet the emission limit.

candidates.title: Changing Compliance Levels of Monitored Parameters (Subpart DDD)

criteria.criterion: If you want to change control device or process operating parameter levels that were established during performance tests and are used to monitor compliance, then you must notify the Administrator of the desire to expand the range and, upon Administrator approval, conduct additional performance tests at the proposed new parameter levels to verify compliance with the applicable emission limits.

candidates.title: General Provisions (Subpart A)

criteria.criterion: If you seek approval to use alternatives to monitoring methods or alternative test methods (including alternative procedures to set parametric limits), then you may petition or request approval from the Administrator under the alternative monitoring and alternative test method provisions.

If you install and operate a continuous monitoring system (CMS) such as a CPMS, then you must operate and maintain the CMS in accordance with the general CMS operation, quality assurance, and data reduction/averaging requirements set forth in the general provisions.

checklist: Confirm that each of the 12 dynamic wet scrubbers is used to meet a particulate matter emission limit in Table 1 of Subpart RRRRR (i.e., is part of an affected source under Subpart RRRRR).

Document the dates of construction or reconstruction for the affected source and each scrubber to determine which timing provisions apply (e.g., construction/reconstruction on or before Sept 25, 2019 vs after, and dates referenced in §63.9590 and §63.9631).

Verify whether an initial performance test has been conducted for each scrubber and obtain the CPMS/monitoring raw data: 15-minute measurements of scrubber water flow rate and fan amperage (or pressure drop) for each test run.

Calculate the average scrubber water flow rate and average fan amperage for each individual test run and identify the lowest average values used to establish site-specific operating limits per §63.9622(b)(2).
Obtain manufacturer specifications for each fan motor no-load amperage or plan and perform a documented no-load amperage test for each fan if you intend to use the PFLA (no-load + 10%) method.

Confirm that a CPMS is installed, commissioned, and maintained to measure and record daily average scrubber water flow rate and daily average fan amperage per §63.9631(c) (or plan to install one before relying on parametric limits).

If you intend to set the minimum fan-amperage limit as percent full load (PFLA no-load + 10%), prepare to demonstrate and document how the no-load amperage and full-load values were determined (manufacturer spec or no-load test and test-run full-load amperage values).

If you propose to change existing operating-limit values or use an alternative parameter-setting method, prepare a notification and, if required, an application to the Administrator (per §63.1186 and §§63.7/63.8) and plan additional performance tests at the proposed new levels to verify compliance.

Ensure procedures and records are in place to operate the CPMS continuously, reduce data to daily averages as required, and to initiate and document corrective actions within the timeframes required if daily averages fall below established operating limits (see §63.9634(l)).

Check your Title V permit or applicable permitting authority requirements for any site-specific monitoring plans, approval processes, or implementation-plan submittals that may be required before changing monitoring approaches or operating limits.
