candidates.title: National Emission Standards for Hazardous Air Pollutants for Automobile and Light-Duty Truck Surface Coating (Subpart IIII)

criteria.criterion: If you seek to use a previously conducted transfer efficiency test in lieu of conducting a new initial transfer efficiency test, then you must obtain approval to use the results of the previous test.

If the previous transfer efficiency test was not conducted using the methods and conditions specified in this subpart (e.g., ASTM D5066 or the incorporated Protocol), then you may not use those previous results in lieu of a required test.

If any process or equipment changes have been made since the previous test, then you must demonstrate that the previous test results still reliably demonstrate compliance despite those changes before you may use the previous results.

If the previous test did not establish the required operating parameters or did not collect sufficient data to establish the required operating parameters, then you may not rely on the previous results in lieu of establishing operating limits via testing.

If you intend to rely on prior test results, then you must retain and be prepared to provide the previous test reports, raw data, and supporting documentation required by the subpart as part of the initial compliance demonstration and recordkeeping requirements.

If your affected coating operations use add-on control devices subject to periodic performance testing, then periodic performance tests and reestablishment/confirmation of operating limits are required within 5 years following the previous performance test (subject to the exceptions in §63.3163(c)(3)).

candidates.title: General Provisions (Subpart A) — performance testing, notification, QA, monitoring, and waiver procedures

criteria.criterion: If you intend to use previous performance test results or request a waiver of a performance test, then you must follow the notification, site-specific test plan, quality-assurance, and waiver procedures in §63.7 (including the 60-calendar-day notification and site-specific plan submission if requested).

If you rely on previous performance test results or a granted waiver, then you must retain and make available the performance test records and related data for at least the period required by §63.7 and the subpart (including retaining test reports for at least 5 years after the test), and submit performance test results or supporting documentation as required.

If continuous parameter monitoring systems or other CMS/CPMS are required by the applicable subpart or operating limits, then monitoring must be conducted, maintained, and documented in accordance with the procedures, QA/QC, and reporting requirements in §63.8.

checklist: Confirm whether your facility and the primer-surfacer/topcoat operations are subject to Subpart IIII (e.g., automobile or light‑duty truck assembly plant or operations added under §63.3082(c)).
Locate the December 2004 transfer efficiency test report(s) and raw data (complete test report, run data, chain-of-custody, lab reports).

Verify the exact test methods and conditions used in the 2004 test (e.g., ASTM D5066, Protocol EPA‑453/R‑08‑002, panel test procedures) and compare to the Subpart IIII methods required by §63.3161(g) and §63.3164/§63.3165.

Document whether the 2004 test established the required operating parameters (transfer efficiency values, any operating limits) or collected sufficient data to establish operating parameters per §63.3160(c)(3).

Inventory any process or equipment changes since December 2004 that could affect transfer efficiency (e.g., changes to spray guns/type, application method, booth configuration, waterwash, exhaust flow, bake oven/sequencing, line speed, automation, part size/fixture), and for each change note installation date and justification why it would or would not affect transfer efficiency.

Determine whether capture system or add-on control device performance (capture efficiency or DRE) was measured in 2004 and whether those tests met the Subpart IIII capture/control test methods; record dates of any subsequent periodic control-device tests (to evaluate 5‑year periodic test applicability under §63.3163(c)(3)).

Assemble documentation you would submit to the Administrator to request approval to use the prior test results (test methods used, raw data, demonstration of no changes or rationale/data showing results still reliable despite changes), per §63.3160(c) and the §63.7 site-specific/test-plan and QA expectations.

Verify that you have maintained the records required by §63.3130 (monthly material usage, mass fraction organic HAP, densities, volume fraction solids, transfer efficiency calculations, and all raw data and algorithms) to support demonstrating that the previous test results apply to current operations.

Confirm whether a previous approval/waiver to use the 2004 results was already obtained from the Administrator or permitting authority; if not, prepare to submit the approval request and follow §63.7 notification (≥60 days) and §63.7(c) QA/site‑specific plan requirements if requested.

Check whether any state or local permit or the facility's title V permit contains different/stricter requirements or specific due dates for performance or periodic testing that would affect reliance on the 2004 test results.

candidates.title: Subpart A (General provisions—monitoring and alternative approval)

criteria.criterion: If an owner or operator wishes to use an alternative monitoring procedure (minor, intermediate, or major change), then the owner or operator must submit an application describing the proposed alternative that addresses the monitoring elements and a performance evaluation test plan as required by 40 CFR 63.8(f)(4) and obtain Administrator approval as provided in 40 CFR 63.8(f)(5).

If an owner or operator intends to use an alternative test method for a required performance test, then the owner or operator must notify the Administrator at least 60 days before the test, validate the alternative using Method 301, and submit the Method 301 validation results as required by 40 CFR 63.7(f)(2).

candidates.title: Subpart NNNNN

criteria.criterion: If you are required by §63.9020(e) to monitor an operating parameter for a scrubber control device, then you must install, operate, and maintain each continuous monitoring system and collect data according to the requirements in 40 CFR 63.9025(a).

If you want to monitor parameters other than those specified in §63.9020(e) for a scrubber control device, then you may request approval under 40 CFR 63.8(f) and must submit a site-specific monitoring plan meeting the requirements of 40 CFR 63.9025(b)(1)–(3) (identify parameter, justify appropriateness, and specify procedures).

If you use a caustic scrubber or a water scrubber to meet the emission limits in Table 1 to this subpart, then you must keep records of the daily average scrubber inlet liquid or recirculating liquid flow rate and daily average scrubber effluent pH as specified in 40 CFR 63.9035(b)(1)–(2).

candidates.title: Subpart SS (General monitoring requirements for control and recovery devices)

criteria.criterion: If your regulated source is required to monitor under this subpart, then monitoring must be conducted as set forth in this subpart unless the Administrator specifies or approves minor changes or approves alternatives as provided in 40 CFR 63.996(b)(1)(i)–(ii) and 40 CFR 63.996(d)(1)–(2).

If you use a continuous parameter monitoring system (CPMS) for a control or recovery device, then you must install, calibrate, maintain, and operate the monitoring equipment according to manufacturer's specifications or other written procedures and ensure CPMS are installed and operational to obtain representative measurements as required by 40 CFR 63.996(c)(1), 63.996(c)(3), and 63.996(c)(4).
If you wish to monitor a different parameter than those established for the subpart (or set unique monitoring parameters), then you may request approval to do so as provided in 40 CFR 63.996(d)(2).

If you install CPMS, then you must establish a range for monitored parameters that indicates proper operation of the control or recovery device and submit the information required to establish that range as specified in 40 CFR 63.996(c)(6).

candidates.title: Subpart HHHHHHH (CPMS requirements for control devices for process vents)

criteria.criterion: If you are using an absorber or acid gas scrubber to meet an emission limit in the subpart and are required to use CPMS, then you must install and operate monitoring equipment as specified in 40 CFR 63.11940(c)(1) — either a flow meter for scrubber influent liquid flow or both liquid influent and gas flow monitoring to determine the liquid‑to‑gas ratio.

If you are using an absorber or acid gas scrubber and are required to use CPMS, then you must install and operate pressure gauges at the inlet and outlet to monitor pressure drop or use the alternate temperature/specific gravity monitoring options where applicable, as specified in 40 CFR 63.11940(c)(2).

If the scrubbing liquid is a reactant (e.g., lime, ammonia hydroxide), then you must install and operate one of a pH monitoring device, a caustic strength monitoring device, or a conductivity monitoring device on the scrubber effluent per 40 CFR 63.11940(c)(3).
If you wish to request approval to use alternative monitoring parameters or procedures for control devices subject to this subpart, then you may request approval as provided in 40 CFR 63.11940(h).

checklist: Identify which specific NESHAP subpart(s) apply to your HCl-containing vent and scrubber (confirm whether your source is covered by the HCl NESHAP provisions cited here, by Subpart NNNNN, or by another subpart).

Confirm whether the scrubber is being used as an emission control device subject to an emission limit (control device) or solely as an acid/recovery device and determine whether the applicable subpart treats recovery devices differently.
Determine the scrubber type and scrubbing media (caustic, water, reactive scrubbing reagent such as lime or ammonia hydroxide, or other).
Document whether a CPMS/CMS is required by the applicable subpart for your control device (and which parameters are specified in the relevant standard for your source).
Gather the results and operating conditions from the initial or most recent performance test (including the monitored parameters and the operating limits established during the test).

Verify which operating parameters your current monitoring system measures (e.g., liquid influent flow, recirculation flow, effluent pH, effluent temperature, pressure drop, gas flow, scrubber base temperature) and the measurement accuracy/calibration records.

Verify monitoring data frequency and availability capabilities (e.g., at least four equally spaced readings per hour, hourly and daily averaging, and >75% data availability as required by the CMS rules cited).

If you plan to request alternative monitoring, prepare a monitoring plan that: (a) identifies the alternative parameter(s) to be monitored to ensure control efficiency is maintained; (b) explains why the parameter(s) adequately demonstrate ongoing compliance; and (c) specifies the monitoring procedures, data collection frequency, averaging times, and QA/QC—consistent with the plan content requirements in 40 CFR 63.9025(b) / 63.8(f).

Assemble supporting demonstration materials: calculations, rationale linking the proposed parameter(s) to control performance (e.g., correlation of scrubber base temperature and flow indicators to HCl removal), and any prior performance-test data that establish operating ranges.

Confirm recordkeeping and reporting obligations you would have if alternative monitoring is approved (e.g., daily averages of flow and pH if using caustic/water scrubbers per 40 CFR 63.9035(b)), and ensure you can meet those recordkeeping frequencies.

Confirm whether Administrator approval is via EPA or a delegated State permitting authority in your state (West Virginia), and whether prior approvals or permit amendments (e.g., Title V) will be required.

Prepare to document and submit any site-specific performance evaluation or validation plan required by the Administrator (and be ready to perform any required performance tests or Method 301 validation if an alternative test method is proposed).

candidates.title: Ethylene Oxide Emissions Standards for Sterilization Facilities

criteria.criterion: If you own or operate a sterilization facility that has any affected source (each SCV, ARV, CEV, the collection of Group 1 room air emissions, or the collection of Group 2 room air emissions) then the requirements of this subpart apply to those affected sources

If your facility is a beehive fumigator, a research or laboratory facility as defined in section 112(c)(7) of the Clean Air Act, or an EtO sterilization operation at a hospital/clinic/medical or dental facility, then the subpart does not apply to those operations

If you are required to demonstrate continuous compliance using EtO CEMS, then you must install and operate EtO CEMS and follow the certification, performance specification, and QA procedures referenced in this subpart (including Appendix A requirements and PS-19 references) for measuring EtO mass emissions and reporting lb/hr and 30-operating-day sums

If your facility uses less than 100 pounds per year of EtO, then you may elect to demonstrate continuous compliance by periodic performance testing (and follow the test methods and monitoring/operating limit requirements specified in §63.365 and §63.364) instead of using EtO CEMS

If you propose to use an alternative monitoring method or instrumentation in lieu of the EtO CEMS performance specification requirements (for example, a vendor gas sensor instead of an analyzer meeting PS-19/appendix requirements), then you must apply for approval of the alternative monitoring procedure under the Administrator-approval provisions and follow the alternative-method application and validation procedures in the General Provisions

candidates.title: General Provisions (Subpart A)

criteria.criterion: If you intend to use an alternative test method for a required performance test, then you must notify the Administrator at least 60 days before the test, validate the alternative using Method 301 (as required), and submit the validation results with the notification

If you intend to use an alternative monitoring procedure in place of the monitoring method specified in a relevant subpart, then you must submit an application to the Administrator that includes a description addressing the monitoring elements and a performance-evaluation test plan (including data quality objectives) as required in §63.8(f)(4) and §63.8(e)(3)

If the Administrator approves an alternative monitoring method, you must use that alternative until further approval; if the Administrator disputes the alternative method results the specified method(s) in the relevant standard will prevail

If you are operating a continuous emission monitoring system (CEMS) for measuring emissions (including EtO CEMS), then the CEMS must complete at least one cycle of operation for each successive 15-minute period and monitoring data must be reduced to hourly averages (and handled per the CMS operation and QA requirements in §63.8)

checklist: Confirm whether your facility is a 'sterilization facility' and whether the specific emission points you operate meet the affected-source definitions (SCV, ARV, CEV, Group 1 collection, Group 2 collection) in §63.360(b) and §63.361.

Verify facility exclusions: determine if your operation qualifies as a beehive fumigator, research/laboratory facility, or a hospital/clinic medical sterilization operation (exemptions in §63.360(f)-(h)).

Calculate and document EtO use: daily, 30-operating-day rolling total, and annual totals to determine applicability and whether you qualify for the <100 lb/yr alternative (see §63.364(i) and §63.363(a)).

Identify exactly which exhaust streams (aeration room vents/ARVs) you plan to monitor, whether streams are combined with other sources, and whether monitoring is required before or after combination per §63.364(f)(2)(i)-(iii) and §63.362(i).

Decide whether you will use an EtO CEMS certified to PS-19 (Appendix B to Part 60) to demonstrate compliance; if so, verify the proposed analyzer/system can be certified and can produce continuous data reduced to hourly averages and convert to lb/hr (CEMS cycle time, hourly averaging, and lb/hr conversion requirements in §63.8(g)(2) and §63.363/§63.364).

If proposing a non-PS19 gas detection sensor (e.g., CEA ET-6200R U series), assemble documentation from the vendor/manufacturer on: continuous sampling capability, cycle time (≤15 min), measurement range and linearity, method detection limit and LOD/SADL, interference test data, response time, and ability to output recorded data suitable for hourly averaging and mass conversion.

Determine whether the proposed sensor can meet the certification and QA tests required for EtO CEMS (daily calibration drift/error tests, 7-day CD, RATAs/RAAs, ME/LOD/interference tests, quarterly audits) as described in Appendix A and PS-19 referenced in §63.363/§63.364.

Prepare to perform Method 301 validation (or the validation required by §63.7(f)) if you plan to rely on an alternative test method for performance testing; plan a 60-day pre-test notification and submit validation results per §63.7(f).

If you intend to use the sensor as an alternative monitoring procedure instead of the required CEMS approach, prepare an application per §63.8(f) that: (a) describes monitoring elements (indicator, measurement technique, frequency, averaging time), (b) includes a site-specific performance evaluation test plan and data quality objectives, and (c) documents technical justification and QA/QC procedures.

Confirm who will review/approve the alternative: approvals for major alternatives to monitoring are retained by EPA (not delegable) per §63.368(c)(3); contact the EPA Regional Office early to confirm submission routing and whether the request is a major or minor change.

Assemble a monitoring plan and QA/QC program that includes written procedures for calibrations, preventive maintenance, recordkeeping, and the specific QA tests and reporting required by Appendix A/§63.364 and §63.8 (5-year record retention, CEDRI reporting requirements).

Verify the proposed device's data output format and capability to meet electronic reporting and recordkeeping needs (hourly ppbv values with required precision, hourly lb/hr conversions, daily and 30-operating-day sums) per Appendix A recordkeeping and §63.366/§63.364 reporting requirements.

Obtain or prepare evidence of interference testing, LOD and response time testing, and (if extractive) capability to perform dynamic spiking and standard addition procedures required for acceptance in Appendix A/PS-19 QA tests.

Plan for certification/recertification triggers: replacement/modification of analyzer, sampling probe, or changes that affect accuracy require recertification per Appendix A (see recertification procedures) and §63.365/Appendix A recertification language.

Prepare to demonstrate, during any requested performance test or RATA, that the alternative instrument produces data of equivalent quality to the reference method; have test protocols, raw data, and QA documentation ready for submission in the performance evaluation or performance test report.

candidates.title: Subpart HH (Natural gas processing plants — test methods and equipment-leak applicability)

criteria.criterion: If a piece of equipment is an ancillary equipment or a compressor located at a natural gas processing plant and operates in VHAP service equal to or greater than 300 hours per calendar year, then it is subject to the equipment leak standards of this subpart.

If the percent VHAP content of the process fluid that is contained in or contacts a piece of ancillary equipment or compressor can be reasonably expected never to exceed 10.0 percent by weight, then that piece may be considered not in VHAP service (i.e., may be excluded from VHAP equipment-leak obligations under this subpart).
If you determine the percent VHAP content of a process fluid, then you shall use Method 18 of 40 CFR part 60, appendix A, or ASTM D6420-99 (2004) subject to the conditions in 63.772(a)(1)(ii)(A)-(D).
If a piece of equipment contains or contacts the field gas before the extraction of natural gas liquids, then it is considered to be in wet gas service (and is treated accordingly under the subpart).

If ancillary equipment and compressors are subject to and controlled under 40 CFR part 61, subpart V, subpart H, or 40 CFR part 60, subpart OOOO, then the applicability and control obligations in this subpart may not apply as specified in §63.769(b).

candidates.title: Subpart A (General Provisions)

criteria.criterion: If you intend to use an alternative (intermediate or major change) test method instead of the test method specified in a relevant standard, then you must notify the Administrator at least 60 days before the performance test, validate the alternative according to Method 301 in appendix A of this part, submit the validation results, and obtain Administrator approval (or follow the timing provisions in §63.7(f)).

If a continuous monitoring system (CMS) or CEMS is required by a relevant standard, then monitoring, operation, quality assurance, and performance-evaluation requirements in §63.8 apply (including installation, daily drift checks, performance evaluations, and recordkeeping).

candidates.title: Subpart EEEE (Performance test methods and allowed analytical methods for total organic HAP and HAP content determinations)

criteria.criterion: If you need to determine the HAP content of an organic liquid, then you may use Method 311 of appendix A to this part, ASTM D6886-18 (using Method B or Method B with Method C as described in ASTM D6886-18 section 4.3), or another Administrator-approved method, and if a method provides HAP-content ranges you must use the upper end of each range for compliance determinations.

If you use Method 18 or Method 320 (or ASTM D6420-18 under its conditions) to determine compliance with a TOC or total organic HAP emission or percent-efficiency limit, then you must first determine which organic HAP are present in the inlet gas stream and analyze the inlet and/or outlet as specified in the performance-test provisions (i.e., quantify the same organic HAP species at inlet and outlet when determining percent reduction or analyze outlet species when determining outlet concentration).

candidates.title: Subpart HHH (Test procedures and compliance demonstrations for glycol dehydration units)

criteria.criterion: If determining actual average benzene or BTEX emissions from a glycol dehydration unit by direct measurement, then you must perform three runs of Method 18 (40 CFR part 60, appendix A) or ASTM D6420-99 (2004) (or an equivalent approved method) and average the results to compute the average mass rate and annual emissions.

If using a no-detect instrument for leak monitoring or no-detect demonstrations, then you must conduct Method 21-style measurements with the instrument performance and calibration criteria adjusted to the average composition of the stream as specified in §63.1282(b) (e.g., calibration gases, instrument response-factor treatment, and 500 ppmv threshold for 'no detectable emissions').

checklist: Confirm that your facility is a natural gas processing plant as defined in 40 CFR 63.761 (i.e., engaged in extraction of NGLs or fractionation prior to custody transfer).
List all pieces of ancillary equipment and compressors at the plant and verify whether each is intended to operate in VHAP service and whether each operates in VHAP service ≥ 300 hours/year.
For each equipment/stream, determine whether the fluid contacts field gas before NGL extraction (i.e., wet gas service).

For each process fluid (gas or liquid) that may contact ancillary equipment or compressors, determine whether the total VHAP concentration can be reasonably expected never to exceed 10.0 percent by weight.

Decide which analytical approach you will use to determine VHAP%: gas-phase Method 18 (40 CFR part 60, appendix A) or ASTM D6420 variant, and verify that ASTM D6420 target compounds and concentration ranges (150 ppbv–100 ppmv) and its subsection requirements (continuing calibration checks, amenable-to-MS restrictions) are met when using ASTM D6420 (see 63.772(a)(1)(ii)(A)-(D)).

If fluids are liquids, evaluate using Method 311 or ASTM D6886 (using Method B or B with C per ASTM D6886-18 section 4.3) to determine HAP content of the liquid and, if an alternate method or SDS/certified data are used, be prepared to use the method results if EPA requires testing (per 63.2354(c)).

If you plan to use an alternative test method (not Method 18 or the listed methods), prepare to validate it per Method 301, notify the Administrator at least 60 days before testing, and submit validation results as required by §63.7(f).

If any equipment/streams are already subject to 40 CFR part 61 subpart V, 40 CFR part 63 subpart H, or 40 CFR part 60 subpart OOOO, document those controls and records, because those may change applicability under §63.769(b).

Collect representative samples (no less than the number required by the chosen method) and document sampling protocols and chain-of-custody; for ASTM D6420, ensure target concentrations fall within the method's validated range and that any non-Table 1 targets are amenable to MS or follow the extra calibration-check steps.

Maintain records of concentration determinations, sampling dates/times, method used, and the rationale that the VHAP% 'can be reasonably expected never to exceed 10.0%' (kept per subpart recordkeeping requirements and available for inspection).

If you will rely on 'knowledge' or supplier data (SDS, certified product data) for HAP fractions, document the basis, and use the upper end of any HAP-content ranges when calculating total VHAP concentration as required by applicable test-method provisions.

If you will perform no-detect (Method 21-style) leak demonstrations, ensure the portable instrument calibration gases, daily calibration, response-factor treatment for average composition, and 500 ppmv threshold are met per the referenced provisions.

candidates.title: General provisions

criteria.criterion: If an owner or operator is required by a relevant standard to perform a performance test, then the owner or operator must perform the test within 180 days of the compliance date unless an approved extension applies.

If a force majeure event is about to occur, occurs, or has occurred that may delay testing beyond the regulatory deadline, then the owner or operator must notify the Administrator in writing as soon as practicable (and before the deadline unless the force majeure delays notice), provide a written description and rationale attributing the delay, describe measures taken to minimize the delay, propose a date to conduct the performance test, and await the Administrator's discretionary decision on any extension.

candidates.title: National Emission Standards for Hazardous Air Pollutants: Iron and Steel Foundries (NESHAP)

criteria.criterion: If you are an iron and steel foundry subject to this subpart and a performance test is required to demonstrate initial compliance with applicable emissions limits, then you must conduct the performance test no later than 180 calendar days after the compliance date specified for your foundry.

If a force majeure delays the initial performance test for an iron and steel foundry subject to this subpart, then you must follow the force majeure notification and extension procedures in §63.7(a)(4).

candidates.title: Metal melting furnaces (performance testing provisions)

criteria.criterion: If you own or operate a metal melting furnace (or group of metal melting furnaces) that is subject to an emissions limit in §63.10895(c), then you must conduct an initial performance test within 180 days of your compliance date and report the results in your notification of compliance status.

If you own or operate an existing metal melting furnace and intend to use prior performance test results to demonstrate compliance, then you may submit prior test results only if the prior test was conducted within the last 5 years using the methods in this subpart and either no process changes have been made since the test or you can demonstrate the prior results (with or without adjustments) reliably demonstrate compliance; you must notify the Administrator of your intent no later than 60 days after your compliance date.

If you are required to submit reports or performance test results electronically under this subpart and a force majeure (as defined) prevents timely electronic submission within the required period, then you may assert a claim of force majeure by notifying the Administrator in writing as soon as practicable and providing a description of the event, a rationale, measures taken to minimize delay, and the date by which you propose to submit; acceptance of the claim and any extension is at the Administrator's discretion.

candidates.title: Notifications, reporting, and related procedures for the integrated iron & steel sector (selected provisions)

criteria.criterion: If you are required by this subpart to submit performance test results, CMS evaluations, or other notifications and you cannot timely comply because of a force majeure occurring within the applicable window, then you may assert a claim of force majeure by notifying the Administrator in writing as soon as practicable and providing a written description of the event, a rationale linking the event to the delay, measures taken to minimize delay, and the date by which you propose to submit; the Administrator has sole discretion to allow an extension.

checklist: Identify which specific NESHAP subpart(s) apply to each affected unit (confirm whether Subpart EEEEE and/or Subpart ZZZZZ and any other subpart govern your melting furnaces and other processes).
Determine the compliance date(s) that apply to your facility and to each affected emission unit (the date(s) from the applicable subpart or §63.7683/§63.10895 as applicable).
Confirm which affected units are required to perform initial performance testing and the regulatory deadlines (180 days after the compliance date unless otherwise specified).
Document the exact dates and nature of the furnace malfunctions and the labor strike and when facility personnel first knew (or should have known) these events could delay testing.
Evaluate whether the malfunction(s) and strike meet the force majeure definition (events beyond your control that prevented timely testing despite best efforts) per §63.2 and §63.7(a)(4).

Confirm whether any prior performance tests exist (for metal melting furnaces) within the last 5 years and whether any process changes occurred since those tests (to determine if prior data may be submitted under §63.10898(a)(1)).

Verify whether a site-specific test plan was submitted and/or approved and the schedule for the performance test per §63.7(c); if using alternative test/monitoring methods, confirm Method 301 validation and required notifications.

Check whether required notifications or test result submissions must be sent electronically via CEDRI/CDX (or ERT) and whether the delay falls within the 5-business-day window for asserting force majeure for electronic submittals (see electronic submission provisions).

Prepare the written force majeure notification and supporting documentation to the Administrator as soon as practicable (or before the deadline if possible) including: description of event, rationale linking event to delay, mitigation measures taken/to be taken, and proposed new test/report date, per §63.7(a)(4) and the applicable subpart reporting provisions.

Retain records of all notices, communications, test plans, test scheduling attempts, repair/maintenance actions, strike-related documentation, and corrective actions; maintain performance test and notification records for at least 5 years as required by the relevant subparts.

candidates.title: Cellulose Products Manufacturing

criteria.criterion: If you own or operate a cellulose products manufacturing operation (including cellulose food casing) that is located at a major source of HAP emissions, then this subpart applies to your operation.

If a continuous monitoring system (CMS) is required by this subpart for an affected source, then you must develop and make available a site-specific monitoring plan that addresses installation, equipment/performance specifications, and performance evaluation procedures (including calibrations) and you must operate CEMS according to the applicable performance specifications listed (e.g., PS-7 for hydrogen sulfide, PS-9 for GC-based organic HAP measurements) and conduct performance evaluations as required.

If you monitor to demonstrate continuous compliance under this subpart, then you must monitor continuously while the affected source is operating and you may not use data recorded during monitoring malfunctions, associated repairs, required QA/QC activities, or periods of no flow in data averages or minimum data-availability calculations.

candidates.title: General Provisions (monitoring, alternative methods, and performance testing)

criteria.criterion: If you wish to use an alternative monitoring procedure (minor, intermediate, or major change) instead of the monitoring method(s) specified in a relevant standard, then you must submit an application to the Administrator and obtain approval as described in §63.8(f) before relying on the alternative (and remain subject to the existing requirements until approval).

If the proposed alternative monitoring procedure will serve as the performance test method to demonstrate compliance, then you must submit the application at least 60 days before the performance evaluation is scheduled and include the information required by §63.8(f) (including a description addressing the elements of monitoring and a performance evaluation test plan per §63.8(e)(3)).

If you intend to use an alternative test method in a required performance test, then you must notify the Administrator at least 60 days before the test, validate the alternative using Method 301, and submit the Method 301 validation results with the notification as required in §63.7(f).

If the Administrator finds reasonable grounds to dispute results obtained by an approved alternative monitoring method, then the Administrator may require use of the monitoring method specified in the relevant standard and, if the specified and alternative methods disagree, the results from the specified method shall prevail.

checklist: Confirm that your facility is a cellulose food casing operation and determine whether it is located at a major source of HAPs (calculate potential-to-emit and actual emissions vs. 10/25 tpy or the 9.1/23 Mg/yr thresholds).

Identify which HAPs your subpart UUUU monitoring/controls require you to measure (e.g., hydrogen sulfide, carbon disulfide, total sulfide) and whether the current permit or subpart language requires CEMS/CPMS for those HAPs.

Determine whether the Baseline‑MOCON Model 8900 will be installed/used as a CEMS, CPMS, or other CMS and whether the instrument type matches the performance specification(s) listed in §63.5545(e) (e.g., PS-7 for H2S, PS-9 for GC-based organic HAP).

Obtain the instrument manufacturer's performance data: detection ranges, calibration gas requirements, response factors, accuracy, precision, and whether calibration/traceability to NIST standards is available.

Compare the 8900's calibration and response procedures to the applicable performance specification requirements (PS-7, PS-9) and to your existing site-specific monitoring plan/OM&M plan to identify deviations needing Administrator approval.

If you plan to use the 8900 as an alternative method, prepare an application addressing the four elements of monitoring (indicator(s), measurement techniques, monitoring frequency, averaging time) and a site-specific performance evaluation test plan (including DQOs, internal and external QA) as required by §63.8(f) and §63.8(e)(3).

If the alternative method will be used for a performance test, plan to notify the Administrator at least 60 days before the performance evaluation and include Method 301 validation data and justification per §63.7(f).

Prepare OM&M plan updates (installation, operation, maintenance, calibration, performance evaluation schedule, and recordkeeping) and the site-specific monitoring plan called for in §63.5545(a); ensure you can perform required performance evaluations and maintain required records.

Verify data acquisition/cycle times and data-reduction requirements (e.g., CEMS 15-minute cycles and hourly averaging, valid data minimums) to ensure the instrument's output can meet averaging and completeness requirements.

Document how you will handle calibration drift, zero/span checks, and periods of instrument malfunction so you do not use invalid data in compliance averages (per §63.5560 and §63.5545 OM&M expectations).

Check timeline/notification needs: whether the change is a minor change that may be included in the site-specific performance evaluation plan or requires a separate application and the 30/60 day administrative timelines in §63.8(f) and §63.7(f).

Confirm whether any permitted or title V conditions reference a specific monitor or method (so that a permit modification or Administrator approval may also be required) and identify the permitting authority contact for submission of the alternative monitoring application and site-specific plans.

candidates.title: Performance testing requirements

criteria.criterion: If an affected source is required to perform a performance test by a relevant standard and no waiver or other approval is obtained, then the owner/operator must perform the performance test within 180 days of the compliance date.

If the owner/operator submits a written application for a waiver of a performance test that includes justification such as technical or economic infeasibility or impracticality at least as required by the section, then the Administrator may approve or deny the waiver.

If the owner/operator proposes to use an alternative test method and follows the notification and Method 301 validation procedures in §63.7(f), then the owner/operator may conduct the performance test using the alternative method upon Administrator approval or under the timing provisions in §63.7(f).

If the owner/operator demonstrates to the Administrator's satisfaction by other means that the affected source is in compliance with the relevant standard, then the Administrator may waive the requirement for a performance test.

candidates.title: Requirements for electric arc furnaces and argon-oxygen decarburization vessels

criteria.criterion: If you own or operate an EAF or AOD vessel that is an affected source under this subpart, then you must conduct PM performance tests to demonstrate initial compliance for each emissions source as specified in §63.10686(d) (subject to the exceptions provided in the subpart).

If you own or operate an existing affected source and a prior performance test for that emissions source was conducted within 5 years of the compliance date using the same methods specified in this section and was representative of current conditions, then you may certify initial compliance based on that prior test in lieu of conducting a new initial performance test.

If emissions from an EAF or AOD vessel are combined with emissions from facilities not subject to this subpart, then you must notify and receive approval from the Administrator for the procedures that will be used to determine compliance for the combined emissions.

candidates.title: Performance test methods and procedures to determine initial compliance

criteria.criterion: If multiple emission points are vented to one common control device to meet the subpart's requirements, then only one performance test is required to demonstrate initial compliance for that group of emission points.

If affected emission points are located in an area with other gaseous emission sources not subject to this subpart, then during a performance test the owner/operator must isolate the affected emission points by either building a temporary total enclosure or shutting down the other gaseous emission points and venting all ventilation air through stacks suitable for testing.

If the conditions of §63.7(e)(2)(iv) or §63.7(h) are met (e.g., waiver obtained or compliance demonstrated by other means), then an owner/operator is not required to conduct an initial performance test under this subpart.

candidates.title: Extension of compliance, and performance test, monitoring, recordkeeping and reporting waivers and alternatives

criteria.criterion: If the owner/operator of a source subject to this subpart submits a written application requesting a waiver of an individual performance test and includes information justifying the request (e.g., technical/economic infeasibility or impracticality) at least as required, then the Administrator may approve or deny the waiver.

checklist: Identify whether each argon stir station is part of an 'affected source' covered by Subpart YYYYY (EAF/AOD) at your facility.

Determine whether the argon stir station exhausts (directly or via ductwork) to the same baghouse/control device that also receives emissions from the ladle metallurgical furnace (LMF) or other units.
If the baghouse is shared, document which emission points vent to the baghouse and whether any of those emission points are NOT subject to Subpart YYYYY.

Confirm whether prior PM performance test(s) were conducted for the shared baghouse or individual emission points within the past 5 years and whether those tests used the test methods specified in 40 CFR part 60 (Method 1/2/3/4/5/17 etc.) required by the subpart.
Verify whether any process changes have occurred since any prior performance test that would affect representativeness of prior test data.

Assess whether it is practicable to isolate the argon stir station emissions for testing by either (a) building a temporary total enclosure around the affected emission point(s) or (b) shutting down other gaseous emission sources not subject to the subpart during the test and venting all ventilation air through stacks suitable for testing (per §63.705(c)(2)(ii)).
If isolation or shutdown is impracticable, prepare technical and/or economic documentation explaining impracticability or infeasibility to support a waiver or alternative monitoring/testing request.

Decide whether to request a performance test waiver or to seek approval to use an alternative test method; if considering an alternative test method, prepare a Method 301 validation plan and submit notification at least 60 days before the scheduled test per §63.7(f).

If seeking waiver: prepare a written waiver application that includes justification (technical/economic infeasibility or impracticality) and submit it with or at the timing required (e.g., at least 60 days before the test unless accompanying an extension request) as described in §63.7(h) and §63.1112(b).

If relying on prior tests under Subpart YYYYY, assemble prior test reports and supporting data showing methods used, dates, operating conditions, and demonstration that tests are representative of current operations as required by §63.10686(d)(6).

Prepare a site-specific test plan (and/or request for alternative monitoring) and be ready to submit it to the Administrator at least 60 days before the performance test or performance evaluation, per §63.7(c) and §63.8(e)(3).

Document process operating parameters and records showing normal representative operating conditions for the argon stir stations and any impacted units to support test representativeness or alternative demonstrations.

If emissions are combined with emissions from facilities not subject to Subpart YYYYY, prepare and be ready to submit a description of the proposed procedures to determine compliance and notify the Administrator for approval as required by §63.10686(d)(4).

candidates.title: National Emission Standards for HCl Production (Subpart NNNNN)

criteria.criterion: If you own or operate an HCl production facility that produces a liquid HCl product at a concentration of 30 weight percent or greater during normal operations and is located at, or is part of, a major source of HAP, then this subpart applies to you.
If the HCl production facility is also subject to one of the listed subparts (including subpart CCC), then the facility is not subject to this subpart.

If you use a caustic scrubber control device and you conduct a performance test, then you must establish the minimum value for scrubber inlet liquid or recirculating liquid flow rate and minimum and maximum values for scrubber effluent pH as the operating limits based on values measured during the performance test.

If you are required by §63.9020(e) to monitor an operating parameter, then you must install, operate, and maintain a continuous monitoring system and collect data at the frequencies and availability described in §63.9025(a).

If you wish to monitor parameters other than those specified in §63.9020(e) for a scrubber, then you may request approval to do so by submitting a monitoring plan under §63.8(f) and meeting the plan content requirements of §63.9025(b).

candidates.title: General Provisions (Subpart A)

criteria.criterion: If you seek to use an alternative nonopacity emission standard or alternative means of emission limitation that will achieve equivalent reductions, then the Administrator may permit that alternative after public notice and comment as described in §63.6(g) and the definitions in §63.2.

If a relevant standard requires a performance test, then you must conduct performance testing in accordance with §63.7 (including notification, site-specific test plan procedures, three runs, and reporting requirements) unless a waiver or other provision applies.

If a continuous monitoring system (CMS) is required by the relevant standard, then the CMS must be operated, maintained, and quality-assured in accordance with §63.8 (including installation, operation, data reduction, and out-of-control procedures).

If you operate an affected source at all times (including startup, shutdown, and malfunction), then you must operate and maintain the source and its pollution control and monitoring equipment consistent with safety and good air pollution control practices as set forth in §63.6(e).

candidates.title: Procedures for Approval of Alternative Means of Emission Limitation (Subpart YY)

criteria.criterion: If you request permission to use an alternative means of emissions limitation to an applicable design, equipment, work practice, or operational standard, then you must demonstrate to the Administrator that the alternative will achieve emission reductions at least equivalent to the required standard and the Administrator will publish a Federal Register notice permitting the alternative after public notice and comment.

If you seek approval of an alternative means of compliance, then you must collect, verify, and submit information showing equivalence and, if not previously tested, a proposed test plan and a description of proposed testing, monitoring, recordkeeping, and reporting per §63.1113(b).

candidates.title: Steel Pickling—HCl Process Facilities and Hydrochloric Acid Regeneration Plants (Subpart CCC)

criteria.criterion: If you are subject to subpart CCC and you use a wet scrubber to achieve compliance, then during the performance test you must establish site-specific operating parameter values for minimum scrubber makeup water flow rate and, for recirculating scrubbers, minimum recirculation water flow rate and monitor those parameters at least once every 15 minutes and use the averages from test runs to set compliant values.

If you are subject to subpart CCC, then you must conduct an initial performance test for each process or emission control device to determine compliance as required by §63.1161(a) in accordance with §63.7.
If your HCl production facility is subject to subpart CCC, then subpart NNNNN does not apply to that facility as stated in the list of exclusions to subpart NNNNN.

checklist: Is your facility an HCl production facility that produces liquid HCl product at ≥30 weight percent during normal operations?
Is the facility part of, or located at, a major source of HAP (≥10 tpy single HAP or ≥25 tpy combined HAP)?
Is the facility already subject to 40 CFR part 63 subpart CCC (steel pickling/HCl regeneration) or one of the other listed subparts that would exclude applicability to NNNNN?
Is the HCl produced via direct synthesis in a chlor-alkali facility (if yes, NNNNN may not apply)?
Does the vent stream at issue route to a caustic scrubber (i.e., an aqueous caustic-containing control device) and is the scrubber operated with recirculation?
Do you have existing performance test data for the scrubber showing inlet/recirculating liquid flow rates and effluent pH measured during representative performance test runs?

If no adequate performance test exists, can you prepare and submit a site-specific test plan and conduct an initial performance test per §63.7 (including 60-day notification) to establish site-specific minimum recirculation flow and pH operating limits?

Can your monitoring system record scrubber recirculation or inlet liquid flow and scrubber effluent pH at the frequencies and data availability required (e.g., at least four equally spaced periods per hour and continuous collection while operating)?

Are you proposing to use alternative operating parameters (e.g., 65 gpm minimum recirculation and ≥2 wt% caustic) that were/will be demonstrated by performance testing to provide equivalent emission reductions, and do you have or can you develop the equivalence data and a proposed test/monitoring/recordkeeping plan?
Will you need to request approval to monitor parameters other than those specified in §63.9020(e) (submit monitoring plan under §63.9025(b) / §63.8(f))?

Do you need to pursue an alternative means of emission limitation approval (prepare submittal per §63.1113(b), including equivalence demonstration and test plan) or seek an alternative emission standard under §63.6(g)?
Which authority will implement/enforce the applicable subpart at your site (EPA or delegated State/local agency)? (determine contact per §63.611)

These criteria capture EPA’s stated need for additional performance testing data before approving the alternatives."}

candidates.title: National Emission Standard for Organic Hazardous Air Pollutants: Bulk Gasoline Terminals

criteria.criterion: If the owner or operator of a bulk gasoline terminal is subject to § 63.422(b)(1) and uses a thermal oxidation system, then a continuous parameter monitoring system (CPMS) capable of measuring temperature must be installed in the firebox or in the ductwork immediately downstream from the firebox before any substantial heat exchange occurs.

If the owner or operator of a bulk gasoline terminal is subject to § 63.422(b)(1) and uses a flare meeting the requirements in § 63.11(b), then a heat-sensing device (e.g., ultraviolet beam sensor or thermocouple) must be installed in proximity to the pilot light to indicate presence of a flame.

If the owner or operator seeks to monitor an alternative operating parameter or a parameter other than those listed for the vapor processing system, then such monitoring will be allowed only upon demonstrating to the Administrator's satisfaction that the alternative parameter demonstrates continuous compliance with the emission standard in § 63.422(b) or § 60.112b(a)(3)(ii).

If the owner or operator is subject to § 63.422(b)(1), then the vapor processing system must be operated consistent with the established operating parameter value (not to exceed or not to go below, as appropriate) established via the procedures in § 63.425, and deviation constitutes a violation of the emission standard.

candidates.title: National Emission Standards for Hazardous Air Pollutants: Bulk Gasoline Terminals (Subpart BBBBBB)

criteria.criterion: If the owner or operator of a bulk gasoline terminal is subject to the emission standard in item 1(b) of Table 2 to this subpart and uses a thermal oxidation system, then a CPMS capable of measuring temperature must be installed in the firebox or in the ductwork immediately downstream from the firebox before any substantial heat exchange occurs.

If the owner or operator of a bulk gasoline terminal is subject to the emission standard in item 1(b) of Table 2 and uses a thermal oxidation system, then as an alternative to temperature monitoring the presence of the pilot flame may be monitored using a heat-sensing device (e.g., ultraviolet beam sensor or thermocouple) installed near the pilot that provides a positive/negative parameter value, subject to submittal and approval of a monitoring and inspection plan and meeting the listed operational safeguards (including automatically preventing loading if pilot absent).

If the owner or operator seeks to monitor an alternative operating parameter other than those listed in paragraphs (b)(1)(i) through (iii), then monitoring of an alternative parameter will be allowed upon demonstrating to the Administrator's satisfaction that the alternative demonstrates continuous compliance with the emission standard in § 63.11088(a), and the rationale, data, monitoring frequency, and averaging time must be provided for Administrator approval.

If the owner or operator is subject to this subpart, then the vapor processing system shall be operated in a manner not to exceed or not to go below the determined operating parameter value (or approved alternative) and operation outside the value constitutes a violation of the emission standard.
If a flare meeting § 63.11(b) requirements is used, then a heat-sensing device such as an ultraviolet beam sensor or thermocouple must be installed near the pilot to indicate presence of flame.

candidates.title: General Provisions (Monitoring and Control Device Requirements)

criteria.criterion: If an owner or operator uses a flare to comply with applicable subparts of this part, then the flare must be operated with a flame present at all times and the presence of the flare pilot flame shall be monitored using a thermocouple or any other equivalent device.

If an owner or operator wishes to use an alternative monitoring procedure or method instead of the monitoring specified in a relevant standard, then the owner or operator may apply to the Administrator under § 63.8(f) (and, for alternative test methods used in performance testing, under § 63.7(f)) describing the proposed alternative and justification, and may be authorized if the Administrator approves.

checklist: Confirm whether the facility is subject to Subpart R (i.e., whether it is an affected bulk gasoline terminal under § 63.422) or to Subpart BBBBBB (i.e., subject to the emission standard in item 1(b) of Table 2 to subpart BBBBBB).
Identify the type of vapor control device currently used for gasoline vapors: thermal oxidizer (thermal oxidation system), flare, carbon adsorber, refrigerated condenser, or other.
If the control device is a thermal oxidizer, confirm whether temperature monitoring in the firebox or immediately downstream (before substantial heat exchange) is currently installed or feasible.

If the control device is a flare, determine whether the flare meets the requirements of § 63.11(b) (e.g., steam- or air-assisted or non-assisted, design/operation parameters) and whether a pilot exists that can be monitored.
Verify whether an existing pilot-flame detection device (thermocouple, UV beam sensor, IR sensor) is installed and capable of providing a continuous positive/negative signal for pilot presence.

Assemble performance-test data (dates, methods, results) for the vapor processing system, including whether a temperature was recorded in the combustion zone during any recent test that could establish an operating limit.

Determine whether the facility conducts intermittent loading operations (document frequency/duration) and whether monitoring exclusions (periods with no gasoline loading) would be applicable under the relevant subpart.

If proposing pilot-flame monitoring in lieu of temperature monitoring, prepare a monitoring and inspection plan addressing monitoring frequency, averaging time, how the pilot-device provides a positive/negative parameter, automatic prevention of loading when pilot absent, verification checks, semi-annual maintenance, and recordkeeping (per the subpart's plan requirements).
Confirm ability to automatically prevent gasoline loading operations when pilot flame is absent (e.g., interlock to prevent startup of loading racks) or document alternative safeguards proposed.

Check whether any prior performance tests (within applicable timeframe) meet the subpart criteria for establishing operating parameters and can be used to set monitoring limits (see cited subpart performance-test provisions).

Verify whether the Administrator (or delegated authority) approval will be required for any alternative monitoring parameter and prepare to submit justification/demonstration data as required (including engineering rationale, calculations, and monitoring data).

Review applicable title V or state/local permit conditions for monitored operating parameters or enforceable permit limits that may affect allowable monitoring alternatives or require permit modification.

The submitted criteria include 63.8(f) (alternative monitoring approval) and 63.427(a)(5) (must demonstrate continuous compliance), but do not mention or address 63.428(c)(3), so only some key EPA reasons are captured."}

candidates.title: Monitoring requirements

criteria.criterion: If the owner or operator is a new, reconstructed, or existing steel pickling facility or acid regeneration plant subject to this subpart, then they must conduct performance tests to measure the HCl mass flows at the control device inlet and outlet or the concentration of HCl exiting the control device either annually or on an alternative schedule approved by the permitting authority but no less frequently than every 2 1/2 years.

If a wet scrubber (control device) is used, then the owner or operator must install, operate, and maintain systems for the measurement and recording of the scrubber makeup water flow rate and, if required, recirculation water flow rate, and monitor these flow rates continuously and record at least once per shift while the scrubber is operating (with excursions below minimum values established during performance testing requiring corrective action).

If the owner or operator wishes to use alternative monitoring requirements for devices covered by this subpart, then those alternative monitoring requirements must be developed and implemented subject to approval by the Administrator.

candidates.title: What are my monitoring installation, operation, and maintenance requirements?

criteria.criterion: If you are required by §63.9020(e) to monitor an operating parameter, then you must install, operate, and maintain each continuous monitoring system according to the CMS requirements in §63.9025(a) including operating the CMS whenever the process is operating and collecting data at the specified frequencies.

If a scrubber is used as the control device, then you may request approval, in accordance with §63.8(f), to monitor parameters other than those specified in §63.9020(e) by submitting a monitoring plan that meets the requirements in §63.9025(b)(1)–(3).

If you request approval to monitor alternative parameters, then your request must include a description of the affected source and parameter(s), methods and procedures demonstrating the parameter can indicate continuous compliance, the proposed monitoring/recording frequency and rationale, supporting calculations, and the proposed averaging time as specified in §63.9025(f)(1)–(5).

candidates.title: Monitoring requirements (general provisions)

criteria.criterion: If an owner or operator wishes to use an alternative monitoring procedure, then they must submit an application to the Administrator under §63.8(f) that describes the monitoring (the four monitoring elements) and includes a performance evaluation test plan, and until permission is granted the owner/operator remains subject to the standard monitoring requirements.

If an owner or operator submits a request to use an alternative monitoring method, then the Administrator will notify the owner or operator of approval or intended denial within 30 calendar days after receipt of the original request (and within 30 days after supplementary information), and if approved the owner/operator must use the approved alternative until further approval.

checklist: Confirm whether your facility is within the source category covered by Subpart CCC (steel pickling facility or acid regeneration plant) for 40 CFR part 63 applicability.

Identify and document the exact type of HCl bubbler control device in use and whether it is considered a wet scrubber under the applicable subpart (design details: dipleg arrangement, recirculation or makeup flow, liquid drain/changeout path).

Assemble the most recent performance test reports showing HCl inlet/outlet mass flows or outlet concentration and the operating parameter values recorded during those tests (including any established minimums used to demonstrate compliance).
Record the currently practiced dipleg immersion depth(s) and the current schedule and historical records for liquid change-outs (dates/times), and whether these are logged automatically or manually.

Determine whether makeup water flow and recirculation flow (or other scrubber parameters) are currently monitored continuously and recorded at least once per shift; collect calibration/certification records for those monitors.

Define the proposed alternative operating limits numerically (proposed minimum dipleg immersion depth in units and proposed maximum time between liquid change-outs) and prepare the technical rationale connecting those limits to HCl control efficiency.

Prepare proposed monitoring methods and frequency for the alternative parameters (how dipleg depth will be measured, how change-out timing will be recorded, measurement accuracy, QA/QC, calibration schedule, data recording and averaging time).

Prepare supporting calculations, data correlations, or testing (e.g., lab or pilot tests, historical test data) demonstrating that the proposed parameters reliably indicate the control performance achieved during the performance test(s).

Identify the permitting authority (EPA vs. South Carolina delegated authority) and the appropriate contact to submit the alternative monitoring application (per §63.8(f)), and confirm any state-specific submission requirements.

Verify that you can meet CMS/CMS-alternative documentation requirements (site-specific monitoring plan, performance evaluation plan, records retention) and can respond to Administrator requests within the timelines referenced in §§63.7 and 63.8.

Confirm availability of manufacturer accuracy certifications for monitoring devices (e.g., within 5% if required by the referencing subpart) and an internal QA program for daily checks, calibrations, and corrective actions.

Determine whether the operating limits you propose will be established during an initial or subsequent performance test (and whether you need to perform an additional performance test per §63.7 to establish enforceable limits) and develop a schedule for any required testing.
