The answer includes the key bases EPA relied on: alternative monitoring must be approved by the Administrator (40 C.F.R. 63.8(f), 63.1162(a)(6), 63.9025(b)) and approval is contingent on performance testing/performance evaluation (references to required performance tests in 63.1162(a)(1), performance evaluation and test plan in 63.8(f) and 63.9025(f), and checklist items about conducting/scheduling tests and establishing limits during testing), which captures EPA’s conditional-approval pending successful performance test."}

candidates.title: General Provisions — monitoring and alternative monitoring approval

criteria.criterion: If you wish to use an alternative monitoring method or alternative monitoring procedure in lieu of a monitoring method specified in an applicable subpart, then you must apply to the Administrator with the information and justification required by the alternative-monitoring provisions and obtain approval before using the alternative.

If your affected source is subject to monitoring requirements in this part, then you must operate and maintain each continuous monitoring system (CMS) consistent with the requirements of this section and with good air pollution control practices, including routine calibration, QA/QC, and keeping spare parts on site.

If an applicable subpart requires Method 21 leak monitoring for equipment, then you may elect to use the alternative optical gas imaging work practice in lieu of Method 21 provided you follow the procedures, daily instrument checks, and recordkeeping specified in § 63.11.

candidates.title: Monitoring requirements (capture/collection systems; alternatives to Method 1/2 verification)

criteria.criterion: If you inspect capture/collection systems as an alternative to annual Methods 1 and 2 flow measurements, then you may use one of the alternative procedures described (pitot/differential pressure indicator, fan RPM or amps, static pressure device, hotwire/anemometer, or PTE verification) and must maintain the daily parametric readings at or above 90 percent of the average measured during the most recent Method 2 performance test series.

If you choose the static pressure measurement alternative, then you must install the static pressure measurement device in the duct immediately downstream of the hood exit and make daily pressure readings by taking three measurements at least 5 minutes apart, averaging them, and maintaining the daily averaged readings at 90 percent or better of the average vacuum recorded during the most recent Method 2 performance test series.

If you use verification of a permanent total enclosure (PTE) instead of annual Methods 1 and 2, then you may verify the enclosure once every 5 years provided you monitor negative pressure directly at a representative location and either record readings daily or interlock material feed to halt if negative pressure is lost, and you annually inspect the pressure indicator for integrity.

candidates.title: Monitoring and continuous compliance requirements (emission capture systems and thermal oxidizers)

criteria.criterion: If you have an emission capture system enclosure that vents to an add-on control device, then for each enclosure you must install a device to measure and record either the gas volumetric flow rate or the duct static pressure in the duct between the enclosure and the add-on control device.

If you use a thermal oxidizer (e.g., RTO) as an add-on control device, then you must install a combustion temperature monitoring device in the firebox or in the duct immediately downstream of the firebox (before substantial heat exchange), locate the sensor to provide a representative temperature, perform semiannual electronic calibrations and validation checks, and continuously monitor and record combustion temperature at least every 15 minutes and maintain the 3-hour average at or above the performance-test-derived operating limit.

If any enclosure has bypass lines that could divert flow away from the add-on control device, then you must either monitor/secure the bypass valve so it cannot be opened without creating a record (flow control position indicator, car-seal/lock-and-key, valve position monitoring, or automatic shutdown) and record inspections or events as required.

candidates.title: Monitoring requirements and alternate monitoring approval (general CPMS/pressure requirements; alternate monitoring application)

criteria.criterion: If you want the Administrator to approve alternate monitoring requirements (including replacing required capture/enclosure face-velocity or other parameters with alternative parameters such as duct static pressure), then you must submit an application no later than the notification of performance test that documents technical justification, description of the proposed alternative, averaging period, and data showing the alternative provides equivalent or better assurance of compliance.

If an operating limit requires use of a pressure measurement device, then the pressure sensor(s) must be located to provide a representative measurement, minimize pulsation and corrosion, use a gauge with minimum tolerance of 1.27 centimeters of water or a transducer with minimum tolerance of 1 percent of the pressure range, check the pressure tap daily, check gauge calibration with a manometer quarterly and transducer calibration monthly, and perform calibration checks whenever the sensor exceeds manufacturer's maximum operating pressure range.

checklist: Determine whether the capture/collection system enclosure(s) at your facility are permanent total enclosures (PTE) as defined by Method 204 (and when the last Method 204 verification or Method 1/2 performance test was performed).

Identify the duct location between each enclosure and the RTO (add-on control device) where a static pressure sensor would be installed; confirm the location provides a representative measurement (per 63.5725(f)(1) and 63.1350(m)(6)(i)).

Verify whether you have established, and have records of, the average vacuum or Method 2/Method 204 test results (the baseline average) from the most recent performance test to which daily static pressure readings must be maintained at ≥90% (per 63.1510(d)(2)(iii)(B) and alternatives in 63.1510(d)(2)).

Confirm the static pressure sensor and/or gauge meet the required accuracy/tolerance (e.g., gauge tolerance ≥1.27 cm water or transducer ±1% of range) and that you have procedures to check the pressure tap daily and to perform manometer/transducer calibration checks on the quarterly/monthly schedule required (per 63.1350(m)(6)).

If your add-on control is an RTO/thermal oxidizer, verify where the combustion-temperature monitor will be located (firebox or duct before heat exchange) and that the sensor meets the representative-location, tolerance, calibration, and recording-frequency requirements (per 63.5725(d)(1)-(5)).

Prepare a monitoring plan (site-specific) including description of the alternative parameter (duct static pressure), test results demonstrating that using static pressure will ensure capture and continuous compliance, operating limits based on performance-test averages, monitoring frequency, QA/QC, and O&M (per 63.8(f), 63.1510(p)/(o), 63.1350(o)).

Determine whether you must obtain Administrator approval (or State-delegated authority approval) prior to implementing the alternative monitoring method and identify the appropriate approving authority (per 63.8(f)(4)-(5) and subpart-specific guidance).

Document procedures for daily measurement (three readings ≥5 minutes apart averaged), recordkeeping, and actions if daily average falls below the established percent-of-baseline (e.g., inspection, corrective actions, reporting and backup monitoring) as required by the applicable subpart.

Confirm that continuous monitors (CPMS/CMS) will meet minimum cycle/averaging requirements (e.g., complete a cycle at least once every 15 minutes for CPMS used in many subparts) and that you can generate valid hourly/3-hour averages as required (per 63.5725(b)(1)-(3) and 63.8(c)(4)).

Assemble and retain performance-test records, baseline parametric averages from the performance test, and the proposed alternative monitoring dataset to include with the approval application (per 63.7(c) and subpart application requirements).

judge_text: {"score":2,"reason":"EPA's note hinges on approval of an alternative monitoring method to demonstrate continuous compliance with PTE requirements. Our Answer includes the key authorities and criteria supporting that outcome: the requirement to seek Administrator approval for alternative monitoring (40 CFR 63.8(f)), the static-pressure alternative and the ≥90% baseline maintenance and daily-averaging procedures (40 CFR 63.1510(d)(2)(iii)(B)), the requirement to monitor duct static pressure between enclosure and control device (40 CFR 63.5725(f)(1)), PTE verification alternatives (40 CFR 63.1510(d)(2)(iv)), and sensor/QA/QC and application details for alternate monitoring (40 CFR 63.1350/63.8). These capture the key reasons in the EPA Notes."}

candidates.title: Equipment leak standards for natural gas processing plants

criteria.criterion: If ancillary equipment or compressors are located at a natural gas processing plant and operate in VHAP service equal to or greater than 300 hours per calendar year, then they are subject to the equipment leak standards of this subpart.

If the owner or operator demonstrates that a piece of ancillary equipment or a compressor contains or contacts a fluid with a total VHAP concentration that can reasonably be expected never to exceed 10.0 percent by weight (using the methods in § 63.772(a)), then that piece is not in VHAP service for the purposes of this subpart.

If any ancillary equipment or compressor is subject to and controlled under the requirements of subpart H of this part or is subject to and controlled under the requirements of 40 CFR part 60, subpart OOOO, then the equipment leak standards in this section do not apply to that equipment.

If an owner or operator detects leaks under this subpart, leak definition, monitoring, repair timeframes and the use of Method 21 for 'no detectable emissions' determinations are those specified in § 63.772(c) and in the referenced portions of 40 CFR part 61 (with the valve-instrument reading exceptions noted in § 63.769(c)), then those test/repair requirements apply.

candidates.title: General Provisions — alternative work practice for leak detection (optical gas imaging)

criteria.criterion: If the applicable subpart requires monitoring of equipment with a 40 CFR part 60, appendix A-7, Method 21 monitor, then the owner or operator may elect to use the alternative work practice (optical gas imaging) instead of Method 21 by complying with the requirements in § 63.11(c)–(e).

If the alternative work practice is used to identify leaks, then all leaks detected by the alternative work practice must be identified for repair as required in the applicable subpart and the owner or operator must perform annual Method 21 screening for the regulated equipment and keep the required records.

If the alternative work practice is used, then the optical gas imaging instrument must meet the instrument specifications, daily instrument check procedures, leak survey procedure, and the recordkeeping and video requirements specified in § 63.11(e).

If equipment is closed-vent, designated leakless, or identified in the applicable subpart as having no detectable emissions (instrument reading < 500 ppm above background), then the alternative work practice provisions do not apply to that equipment.

candidates.title: Test methods and procedures (Method 21 performance & applicability to organic HAP service)

criteria.criterion: If equipment is subject to monitoring under this subpart, then monitoring shall comply with Method 21 of 40 CFR part 60, appendix A, including Method 21 performance criteria (with the instrument response factor allowed to be for the average composition of the process fluid) and daily calibration before use.

If a piece of equipment is presumed to be in organic HAP (VOC/HAP) service under this subpart, then it is in organic HAP service unless the owner/operator demonstrates that the percent organic HAP content can be reasonably expected not to exceed 5 percent by weight using Method 18 (or ASTM D6420 where allowed) as specified in § 63.180(d).

If an owner/operator elects to adjust instrument readings for background when conducting Method 21 monitoring under this subpart, then they must determine and apply background using the procedures in § 63.180(c).

candidates.title: Leak inspection provisions for vapor collection/closed vent systems, covers and fixed roofs

criteria.criterion: If a vapor collection system, closed vent system, fixed roof, cover, or enclosure is required to comply with this section, then it must be inspected per § 63.148 including an initial Method 21 inspection where specified and periodic visual or Method 21 inspections per the schedules in § 63.148(b)–(c).

If an owner/operator elects to adjust Method 21 instrument readings for background for inspections under this section, then the background measurement and subtraction procedures of § 63.148(c)(5) and the Method 21 background procedures of § 63.180(c) apply.
If a vapor collection or closed vent system is also subject to § 63.172, then the owner/operator shall comply with § 63.172 and is exempt from the requirements of § 63.148.

checklist: Confirm the facility meets the definition of a natural gas processing plant (location and operations) and identify the facility boundary.

List every piece of ancillary equipment and compressors on site (pumps, pressure relief devices, sampling connection systems, open-ended valves/lines, valves, flanges, connectors) and identify which pieces are in the cooling jacket water service.
For each piece, determine the number of hours per calendar year it operates in VHAP service (document hours to test the ≥300 hours/yr HH threshold).

For each process fluid contacting ancillary equipment (including your ethylene glycol + water mixture in the cooling jacket), determine the total VHAP concentration by weight and document the analytical method used (e.g., Method 18 of 40 CFR part 60 appendix A or ASTM D6420 per § 63.772(a)(1)).
If claiming equipment is not in VHAP service, prepare the Method 18 or ASTM D6420-99 (2004) demonstration and supporting data per 40 CFR 63.772(a)(1)(i)/(ii).

Determine whether any ancillary equipment or compressors are already subject to and controlled under Subpart H or 40 CFR part 60 subpart OOOO (if so, § 63.769(b) may exempt HH applicability for those items).
Identify whether any items are part of a closed-vent system, cover, fixed roof, or enclosure (if so, inspect applicability of § 63.148 and § 63.773(c)).

Verify whether the applicable subpart requires Method 21 monitoring for the equipment in question (if yes, note that Subpart A § 63.11 offers an optical gas imaging alternative but not a naked-eye quarterly visual-only substitute).

If you plan to use the Subpart A alternative work practice (optical gas imaging) instead of Method 21, confirm instrument meets § 63.11(e)(1) specifications, plan for daily instrument checks per § 63.11(e)(2), video recordkeeping and retention per § 63.11(e)(4)–(5), selection of detection sensitivity and monitoring frequency per Table 1 to subpart A, and annual Method 21 re-screening per § 63.11(d)(7).

If you propose to rely on visual/sensory monitoring, confirm which specific regulated items and subparts allow sensory monitoring (see relevant subpart text) — do not assume sensory inspection alone replaces Method 21 unless a subpart explicitly allows it.

Ensure repair timing, first attempt and completion deadlines, and delay-of-repair provisions are understood and documented for detected leaks as specified in the applicable subpart (e.g., § 63.769(c)(3) and § 63.773(c)(3)).
Prepare the required recordkeeping and retention (including video records and Method 21 annual results) and retention locations/times consistent with § 63.774 and § 63.11(e)(4)–(5).

If any alternative monitoring or alternative test methods are being considered, prepare and, if required, submit the site‑specific test/monitoring plan and request approvals as specified in § 63.7 and § 63.8 (and in § 63.11(e) for the OGI daily check alternative approval path).

Therefore only some of the EPA note’s reasons are reflected."}

candidates.title: General Provisions

criteria.criterion: If you are required to do a performance test by a relevant standard, then you must notify the Administrator in writing of your intention to conduct the performance test at least 60 calendar days before the performance test is scheduled to begin.

If a force majeure event will or has caused a delay in testing beyond the regulatory deadline, then you must notify the Administrator in writing as soon as practicable (and before the performance test deadline unless delayed) and provide a written description and proposed reschedule date so the Administrator may consider an extension.

If you request a waiver of an initial performance test (and a site-specific test plan is not submitted), then the application for the waiver must be submitted at least 60 days before the performance test date.

If you request an adjustment to any time period or postmark deadline for a required communication, then you must request the adjustment in writing as soon as practicable and the Administrator may approve the adjustment after review, with the Administrator notifying the owner or operator in writing of approval or disapproval within 15 calendar days of receiving sufficient information.

If a performance test must represent normal operating conditions, then operations during periods of startup, shutdown, and malfunction do not constitute representative conditions for the purpose of a performance test.

candidates.title: National Emission Standards for Hazardous Air Pollutants: Asphalt Roofing Manufacturing

criteria.criterion: If you are required to conduct a performance test under this subpart, then you must submit a notification of intent to conduct the performance test at least 60 calendar days before the performance test is scheduled to begin, as required by § 63.7(b)(1).

If you are an existing affected source, then you must conduct initial performance tests no later than 180 days after the compliance date specified in § 63.8683, or for new sources within 180 days after April 29, 2003 or startup whichever is later, consistent with § 63.7(a)(2).

If you plan to use data from a previously-conducted emission test in lieu of conducting an initial performance test, then you may submit those test data as the initial performance test results provided the prior test meets the subpart's conditions (no process changes, conforming methods/conditions, control/process parameters used to show continuous compliance, and completed within the last 60 months).

If you conduct a performance test under this subpart, then the test must be conducted under normal operating conditions and not during startup, shutdown, or malfunction, and you must record process information demonstrating the conditions represent normal operation.

If you complete the initial compliance demonstration/performance test, then you must submit the Notification of Compliance Status including the performance test results before the close of business on the 60th calendar day following completion of the performance test.

candidates.title: Subpart AAAAAAA notification, recordkeeping, and reporting requirements

criteria.criterion: If you are required to conduct a compliance (performance) test under this subpart, then you must submit a notification of intent to conduct the compliance test at least 60 calendar days before the compliance test is scheduled to begin, as required in § 63.7(b)(1).

If you intend to use previously-conducted emission test data to serve as documentation of compliance with this subpart, then you must submit the prior test data in lieu of an initial compliance test with your Notification of Compliance Status and meet the subpart's documentation requirements.

checklist: Confirm which relevant NESHAP subpart(s) your facility is subject to (verify whether Subpart LLLLL and/or Subpart AAAAAAA apply) and whether the State has delegation for notifications under 40 CFR 63.9(a)(4).

Determine whether the upcoming test is an initial performance test required by the applicable subpart or a subsequent/periodic test and whether the regulatory deadline (e.g., within 180 days of compliance date) applies (see 40 CFR 63.8686).

Decide whether you will rely on a previously-conducted emission test (check that the prior test was completed within the last 60 months and that no process or control changes have occurred and that methods/conditions conform to the subpart's requirements).
Identify the proposed test dates and calculate whether you can provide the required 60-calendar-day notification to the Administrator (or delegated State authority) prior to the scheduled test.

If you cannot provide 60 days' notice, determine whether you will submit a written request for (a) an adjustment by mutual agreement under 40 CFR 63.9(i), (b) a waiver of the initial performance test under 40 CFR 63.7(h), or (c) a force majeure extension under 40 CFR 63.7(a)(4); prepare the supporting documentation required for the chosen approach.

Prepare a site-specific test plan and note whether you will request Administrator review (if requested, plan to submit the test plan simultaneously with the 60-day notification per 40 CFR 63.7(c)(2)(iv)).

Document that the planned performance test will be conducted under representative normal operating conditions (not during startup/shutdown/malfunction) and assemble records that show the planned operating conditions are normal.

If submitting a waiver or force majeure claim, prepare the justification information (technical/economic infeasibility for waiver; description, rationale, corrective measures, and proposed test date for force majeure) consistent with the cited provisions.

Identify the correct recipient for notifications (EPA Regional Office vs. delegated State authority) per 40 CFR 63.9(a)(4) and whether electronic submission via CEDRI/CDX is required for your report type and date.

Ensure arrangements for an EPA observer (if requested) and availability of required performance testing facilities, sampling ports, safe access, utilities, and QA/QC (including audit samples per 40 CFR 63.7 and CMS evaluation requirements if applicable).

Plan for submission of the Notification of Compliance Status and performance test results no later than 60 calendar days after completion of the performance test (or as otherwise specified) and prepare records retention for at least 5 years after the test.

candidates.title: General Provisions

criteria.criterion: If an owner or operator wishes to use an alternative monitoring procedure instead of the monitoring methods specified in a relevant standard, then the owner or operator must submit a written application to the Administrator and obtain approval before using the alternative (except minor changes as allowed), or remain subject to the standard monitoring requirements until approval is granted.

If the alternative monitoring procedure will serve as the performance test method to demonstrate compliance, then the application must be submitted at least 60 days before the performance evaluation is scheduled to begin and must meet the alternative test method requirements in §63.7(f).

If the owner or operator submits a proposed alternative monitoring method, then the Administrator will notify the applicant of approval or intention to deny within 30 calendar days after receipt of the original request and any supplementary information, and may allow the applicant opportunity to supply additional information before final disapproval.

If the Administrator finds reasonable grounds to dispute results obtained by an alternative monitoring method, then the Administrator may require use of the monitoring method specified in this part or the relevant standard and the specified method's results shall prevail where they disagree.

If an owner or operator proposes an alternative test method for performance testing, then the alternative must be validated using Method 301 and the owner or operator must notify the Administrator at least 60 days before the scheduled performance test.

candidates.title: Chromium Electroplating and Anodizing (Subpart N)

criteria.criterion: If an owner or operator of a source subject to Subpart N wishes to use an alternative monitoring method, then the request and approval process for that alternative will be considered in accordance with §63.8(f)(1), (f)(3), (f)(4), and (f)(5) as referenced by Subpart N.

If an owner or operator uses an air pollution control device not listed in the monitoring/operation tables of Subpart N, then the owner or operator must submit a description of the device, Method 306 test results verifying device performance, a copy of the operation and maintenance plan including practices, and proposed operating parameters to the Administrator for approval before using that device to demonstrate compliance.

If an owner or operator requests a major alternative to monitoring as defined for this subpart, then approval of major alternatives to monitoring is retained by the EPA Administrator and cannot be delegated to State, local, or Tribal agencies.

If an owner or operator intends to establish site-specific operating parameters or to use alternative monitoring to demonstrate continuous compliance for Subpart N, then the owner or operator must develop and, if requested, submit a site-specific performance evaluation test plan (including QA/QC) in accordance with the performance evaluation requirements of §63.8(e)(3).

checklist: Confirm each tank type: are they enclosed hard chromium electroplating tanks (not decorative or anodizing) and will they be new or existing sources (note relevant Subpart N compliance/startup date criteria)?

Determine facility designation (large vs small) by calculating maximum cumulative potential and/or actual cumulative rectifier capacity (ampere-hours) per §63.342(c)(3) to know which numerical standards and monitoring apply.

Verify whether the Palm Technology Emission Eliminating Devices (the control device) are listed in Subpart N Table 1 or otherwise identified in the rule; if not listed, prepare to submit device description, Method 306 test results, O&M plan, and proposed operating parameters for Administrator approval per §63.343(d).

Decide whether the proposed alternative monitoring will be used as the performance test method; if so, plan to submit the alternative test method application and Method 301 validation and notify the Administrator at least 60 days before the performance evaluation per §63.7(f) and §63.8(f)(4)(i).
Prepare a site-specific performance evaluation / monitoring plan (including QA/QC, performance evaluation test plan) consistent with §63.8(e)(3) and ready for submittal if requested.

Determine whether the proposed alternative monitoring/change is minor, intermediate, or major (per definitions in §63.90) because major alternatives to monitoring for this subpart require Administrator approval and cannot be delegated (contact EPA Region or CT permitting authority to confirm delegation status per §63.348(a) and §63.348(c)(3)).

Document technical justification showing why specified monitoring methods are infeasible for your equipment (e.g., interference, liquid water, geometry) and collect any supporting data or pilot test results to include with the alternative monitoring application as described in §63.8(f)(4)(ii) and §63.343(c)(8)(ii).

Assemble the O&M plan and any changes to it required by Subpart N §63.342(f) and be prepared to revise it within 45 days if it does not address a malfunction event or if the Administrator requests changes.

candidates.title: General Provisions

criteria.criterion: If you propose to use a test method or monitoring procedure other than those specified in the applicable standard (e.g., composite sampling in place of a specified grab sampling approach), then you must validate the alternative per Method 301 and obtain Administrator approval following the alternative test/monitoring procedures in § 63.7(f) before relying on it for compliance.

If you propose an alternative monitoring procedure (minor, intermediate, or major change) to replace the monitoring specified in a relevant standard, then you must apply for and receive Administrator approval under the alternative monitoring provisions in § 63.8(f) before using that procedure for compliance.

candidates.title: Heat exchange system requirements

criteria.criterion: If the heat exchange system cools process equipment in a chemical manufacturing process unit that meets the § 63.100(b)(1)–(3) criteria, then the owner/operator must monitor that heat exchange system according to § 63.104 unless one of the exceptions in § 63.104(a) applies.

If you elect to monitor cooling water for the presence of organic HAP (the § 63.104(b) option), then concentrations must be determined using an EPA‑approved part 136 method (sensitive to 10 ppm), samples must be collected at the entrance and exit (or exchanger locations) using the same analytical method for entrance and exit, and a minimum of three sets of entrance/exit samples must be taken and averaged as required by § 63.104(b)(3)–(5).

If you propose to use an alternative analytical or sampling technique (for example, composite sample collection instead of specified grab samples or an alternate sampling configuration), then that alternative method may be used only upon approval by the Administrator (and, where applicable, after validation per Method 301 and the procedures in § 63.7(f)).

If 99 percent by weight or more of the organic compounds that could leak into the heat exchange system are water soluble and have Henry's Law constants < 5.0E-6 atm·m3/mol at 25 °C, then you may monitor the cooling water under § 63.104(b) in lieu of using the Modified El Paso Method as allowed by § 63.104(l).

candidates.title: Process vent and process wastewater monitoring and test methods

criteria.criterion: If performing process‑vent or control‑device performance tests using Method 18, Method 25A, Method 320, or similar referenced methods, then the minimum sampling time per run is 1 hour and you may use either an integrated (i.e., an integrated/composite) sample or a minimum of four grab samples taken at approximately equal time intervals (e.g., ~15‑minute intervals); thus an integrated/composite sample is an authorized option where the regulation permits an "integrated sample."

If conducting wastewater treatment or control performance tests under § 63.145 (noncombustion, combustion, or biological treatment processes), then samples may be grab samples or composite (integrated) samples, shall be taken at approximately equally spaced time intervals over a 1‑hour period (each 1‑hour period is a run), and the performance test shall consist of at least three runs.

If you propose to use methods or data other than the specified reference methods (for example, an analytical/sampling procedure that would replace Method 18 or Method 25A for transfer rack or control device testing), then those methods/data may only be used if validated according to the Method 301 protocol (or otherwise approved by the Administrator) as allowed by § 63.128(a)(11) and § 63.7(f).

If you wish to monitor parameters other than those specified for a process vent, recovery device, or recapture device (i.e., a different monitored parameter than the rule lists), then you must request approval to monitor alternative parameters according to the procedures in § 63.114(c).

checklist: Determine whether your plant/site and the specific process unit meet the Subpart F applicability criteria in 40 CFR 63.100(b)(1)–(3) (i.e., is it a CMPU at a major source producing listed chemicals or using listed organic HAP).

Confirm which heat exchange systems cool process equipment in CMPUs subject to § 63.104 and whether any § 63.104(a) exceptions apply (e.g., minimum cooling‑water pressure differential, intervening fluid, applicable NPDES permit conditions).

For the heat exchange monitoring option you intend to use, confirm whether you are electing the § 63.104(b) (cooling‑water organics) or § 63.104(g)/(l) (stripping or aqueous‑soluble compound provisions) path and which specific analytical method(s) are prescribed.

Verify whether the selected analytical method is an EPA‑approved part 136 method sensitive to 10 ppm (or identify the alternative method you intend to use) and whether the same method will be used for both entrance and exit samples as required by § 63.104(b)(3).

Record the planned sampling locations (entrance and exit or heat‑exchanger inlet/outlet points) and confirm you can collect the minimum of three sets of entrance/exit samples and compute entrance and exit means per § 63.104(b)(4)–(5).

If you plan composite (integrated) samples instead of grab samples, identify whether the applicable test method or performance test regulation expressly allows an 'integrated' or 'integrated/composite' sample (e.g., Method 18/25A/320/Modified El Paso language in Subpart G) or whether the standard calls for grab samples only.

If your planned composite approach would deviate from the wording of the applicable method/standard, prepare a Method 301 validation plan for the alternative sampling/analytical approach (showing precision, accuracy, representativeness, limits of detection) and the Administrator notification/approval schedule required under § 63.7(f) and § 63.8(f).

Prepare the site‑specific test/monitoring plan (and any CMS performance evaluation plan if applicable) to submit on request and be ready to provide the 60‑day notifications required for performance testing or performance evaluations per § 63.7(b) and § 63.8(e)(2).

Identify whether the compounds that could leak into the heat exchange system meet the § 63.104(l) criterion (≥99% water soluble and Henry's Law < 5.0E‑6 atm·m3/mol) because that affects the allowed monitoring methods.

If proposing an alternative monitoring parameter (for process vents/recovery devices), document the justification and follow the approval request path in § 63.114(c) (including cross‑references to the applicable § 63.151/§ 63.152 submission procedures as required by that provision).

Confirm recordkeeping and reporting capabilities to retain test/monitoring records, audit/validation data, and approvals as required by the cited sections (e.g., the performance test report, Method 301 validation records, and any Administrator approval letters).

candidates.title: National Emission Standards for Hazardous Air Pollutants for Primary Aluminum Production (Subpart LL)

criteria.criterion: If the facility operates a paste production plant or a pitch storage tank as part of a primary aluminum reduction plant, then Subpart LL applies to those units and their POM/PM emission and control requirements.

If a pitch storage tank will be used to store pitch upon restart, then the owner/operator must demonstrate initial compliance with the pitch-storage-tank POM standard by preparing a design evaluation or by conducting a performance test and must have a control system that achieves the required POM reduction (95% or greater).

If an existing pitch storage tank was shut down when compliance would otherwise have been required and is subsequently restarted, then the owner/operator must conduct the required initial performance test by the 30th day following startup of that pitch storage tank.

candidates.title: General Provisions (Subpart A)

criteria.criterion: If the owner/operator of an existing affected source is unable to comply with a relevant section 112(d) standard because additional time is necessary for installation of controls, then the owner/operator may request an extension of compliance of up to 1 additional year under § 63.6(i).

If requesting an extension of compliance, then the request must be submitted in writing to the appropriate authority not later than 120 days prior to the affected source's compliance date, except that a later request is allowed if the need for the extension arose after that 120-day deadline due to circumstances beyond the owner/operator's reasonable control and the request includes the date the owner/operator first learned of the problem.

If requesting an extension, then the request must include information describing the controls to be installed and a compliance schedule containing, at minimum, the dates to initiate on-site construction/installation and the date by which final compliance will be achieved.
If an extension has not yet been granted, then the owner/operator remains subject to all applicable requirements of the relevant standard until the extension is granted.

If the owner/operator has requested an extension of compliance, then they may apply for a waiver of an initial performance test and the Administrator may waive the test while the extension request is under consideration.

checklist: Confirm whether your facility is a primary aluminum reduction plant and whether you operate a paste production plant and/or pitch storage tank (units to which Subpart LL applies).

Confirm whether the pitch storage tank will be placed back into service (date when the tank will first store pitch) and the date you restarted or plan to restart the smelter/pitch tank (for performance-test timing).
Determine whether your source is an 'existing' source under Subpart LL (i.e., not a new or reconstructed source as defined in the Subpart LL compliance-date provisions).
Confirm the applicable compliance date for the pitch storage tank POM limit (Oct 16, 2017 per Subpart LL) and whether you intend to request an extension before or after the 120-day-before deadline.

If requesting an extension, prepare the required written request showing: description of the controls to be installed (e.g., carbon adsorber), and a compliance schedule with milestone dates (award/order date, on-site construction/installation start date, completion date, and final compliance date) as required by 40 CFR 63.6(i)(6).

Document the factual reason why an additional 60 days is necessary (e.g., delivery/contract/installation delays) and, if submitting after the 120-day window, document the date you first learned of the problem and why it was beyond your control (to support the §63.6(i)(4)(i)(C) exception).

Determine the appropriate authority to submit the extension request to (EPA Administrator or State permitting authority if State has approved part 70 program) and whether Title V permit revision is required to incorporate extension conditions.

Prepare performance-test and monitoring plans: schedule initial performance test (Subpart LL requires pitch tank test within 30 days of startup for restarted tanks) or include a waiver request for the initial performance test along with the extension request (see §63.7(h)).

Prepare required pitch storage tank control documentation (design evaluation for carbon adsorber) including parameters specified in 40 CFR 63.847(g)(2)(v) (carbon affinity, carbon amount per bed, number of beds, humidity, temperature, flow rate, desorption/regeneration schedule and conditions).

Assemble records showing operations will be maintained consistent with safety and good air pollution control practices during any extension period (per 40 CFR 63.6(e) and Subpart LL operation/maintenance expectations).
